- [Understand](understand/README.md) explains architecture, authority, runtime flow, and system boundaries.
- [Operate](use/README.md) explains planning, installation, daily operation, diagnosis, recovery, maintenance, and retirement.
- [Extend](extend/README.md) explains plugin authoring, testing, packaging, and supported extension points.
- [Reference](reference/README.md) contains generated facts from current source, configuration references, and the glossary.
- [Current Status](status/current.md) links current work, local closure and separate live acceptance.
- [Open issues](status/open-issues.md) lists remaining implementation work and completion criteria.
- [Roadmap](status/roadmap.md) explains planned platform improvements and why they matter.
- [Decisions](decisions/README.md) records enduring constraints, their rationale and approval evidence.

The [Product Surface Map](product-surfaces.md) lists every public surface family.
Use it when you do not know which track owns a component, interface, or configuration.

The first-project exercise supplies the complete local project and repository
inputs, compiles the eight-stage graph, and explains inspection, failures and
cleanup. It does not admit or execute that graph. A governed run additionally
requires operator-owned runtime platform configuration, grants and services.
[The two command forms](use/operate.md#understand-the-two-command-forms)
define that separate execution boundary.

Final authoritative gate evidence must be complete; earlier continuation may be policy-permitted only when safe, with gaps visible. Source boundary: Preserve the agent-output boundary during the replacement. An agent-backed
registration owns a closed `outputContract`: protocol, agent, identity, task,
evidence, and rules supplied in the request are input, not fields the agent may
echo into its domain output. The runtime owns invocation identity and durable
session evidence; trusted runtime code adds that evidence before the extension
parser validates the completion. Bind run, stage, module, gate, project, and
attempt identity from trusted invocation input, not agent-supplied identity.
Reject unknown output fields and keep durable output outside disposable
worktrees, with atomic writes. Provider replacement must preserve terminal-state,
cancellation, and durable-result behavior; a package listing or configuration
change is not proof of a successful dispatch or live end-to-end execution.
expectedResults: Whole Extend KubeClaw route must preserve its declared proof ladder/observations; native input/check results are limited to their actual owning action, not activation by association.

Preserve the agent-output boundary during the replacement. An agent-backed
registration owns a closed `outputContract`: protocol, agent, identity, task,
evidence, and rules supplied in the request are input, not fields the agent may
echo into its domain output. The runtime owns invocation identity and durable
session evidence; trusted runtime code adds that evidence before the extension
parser validates the completion. Bind run, stage, module, gate, project, and
attempt identity from trusted invocation input, not agent-supplied identity.

worktrees, with atomic writes. Provider replacement must preserve terminal-state,
cancellation, and durable-result behavior; a package listing or configuration
change is not proof of a successful dispatch or live end-to-end execution.

contracts.scope: Five registration contracts, shared package envelope, input/result/identity/config/authority comparison and compatible implementation route.
prerequisites: Select closed schema/version, surface registration, provider and grants; a type/schema does not grant authority.

Source boundary: KubeClaw therefore selects five narrow contracts. Each contract gives one host a
clear responsibility. Core can then validate data and authority before code runs.

Source boundary: Every package has one inert `plugin.json`. Discovery reads this file before it
imports executable code. The manifest supplies a package ID, API version, semantic
package version, and registration arrays. At least one registration array must be
non-empty.

Source boundary: Registration modules and schemas use package-relative paths. They cannot use an
absolute path or escape through `..`. Registry construction checks referenced files,
schema validity, registration conflicts, and global ownership before activation.
errors: For Understand The Five Pipeline Extension Contracts, stop on the first owning schema/authority/identity/tool/lifecycle failure; preserve original diagnostic and respect explicitly unsupported routes.

Source boundary: They share package discovery and immutable package identity. They do not share the
same caller, data, authority, retry rules, or failure meaning. A package can contain
more than one registration and more than one registration type.

Source boundary: **Rejected alternative:** One callback with optional fields would permit invalid
combinations. For example, an observer could appear to return a stage result.

Source boundary: The result does not mutate Core state directly. Core validates it and maps its
outcome to lifecycle state. `passed`, `retry`, `request_fix`, `wait`, `blocked`,
`failed`, `timed_out`, `rate_limited`, `cancelled`, and
`orchestrator_required` have different stop and recovery meanings. A plugin must not
invent a new outcome or a private lifecycle transition.
effects: Verification reads/builds selected source; adding registration/schema/module changes package authority, not automatically runtime activation.

| Registration | One manifest entry that connects an identity to a schema and executable export |
| Canonical state | The authoritative run and stage state that Core records |
| Capability | One named type of bounded external authority |
| Grant | An operator rule that permits one registration to use one capability within constraints |
| Receipt | A durable record of an adapter result for one effect identity |
| Checkpoint | The last observer delivery state that Nova can resume |
| Port | A typed value or artifact connection between Buster nodes |
| Immutable identity | Package or plan identity that changes when its bound content changes |

that run during the current drain, but it does not change the pipeline result.

Source boundary: Candidate selection uses visible artifacts from the current run and configured
summary producer. It requires exactly one artifact at the latest attempt;
absence or a tied latest selection is an error. `test.plan.evidence` performs
the original summary/native-import qualification. A caller's passed flag,
HTTP 200, or arbitrary same-digest object is not that authority.

Source boundary: Before delivery, the adapter rereads and binds the original candidate and
qualified evidence. The URL must be exact HTTPS without credentials, query or
fragment. Generated username/password come from that evidence, not config.
The stable delivery ID hashes current run, candidate digest and target.
Private-message receipt lookup binds that identity, original delivery stage
and exact transport payload. Changed payloads, foreign owners or legacy
unbound receipts cannot authorize readiness.

Source boundary: All three stage configuration objects are closed and empty. Their inputs are
closed, required objects. Unknown input fields fail; no caller-supplied result
or receipt bypasses evidence selection.

Source boundary: JSON Schema string lengths and runtime string lengths are different measures.
The helper also rejects control characters and measures its text bound using
JavaScript UTF-16 code units. A schema-valid string is not automatically valid
for every runtime helper.

Source boundary: The delivery stage selects the configured candidate and invokes
`demo.handoff` operation `deliver`, resource type `demo.candidate`, canonical ID
equal to the candidate artifact ID. Its output is persisted under

binds the full candidate reference, stable delivery ID, exact private transport
payload digest and authoritative receipt. Failure returns blocked
`demo.delivery_unresolved`; it is not proof that no private message was sent.
effects: Package checks are local; actual message delivery/controller record and exposure are separate external effects, explicitly not claimed by this guide.

contracts.scope: pipeline-review advisory assessment and case-study cited draft admission from completed Core source evidence; neither changes verdict nor establishes factual truth/acceptance.
prerequisites: Completed original journals/snapshot/latest attempts, exact artifact bytes, evidence bundles, grants and budgets.

Source boundary: The closed response requires `status: reviewed`, a nonblank summary of at most
8,192 UTF-16 code units, and 5–128 observations covering every dimension.
Each observation is closed: one valid dimension, priority low/medium/high,
nonblank finding of at most 8,192 UTF-16 code units, and 1–128 unique known
evidence IDs. No uncited observation or extra agent-owned control field passes.

Source boundary: The stage adds current `execution`, current report run/attempt, historical
`reportTarget`, `evidenceStatus: verified-source-bundle`,
`narrativeStatus: draft-not-entailment-verified`, and the verified source bundle.
It stores JSON in namespace `kubeclaw.pipeline-review` under
`pipeline-review:<digest-of-active-execution>`. It verifies the original store
response against exact canonical bytes, byte length and active producing attempt
before returning passed with the artifact reference.

Source boundary: The agent protocol is `kubeclaw.case-study.v4`. The agent owns only
`{status, markdown, evidenceIds}`, with `status: generated`.
Markdown is 1–131,072 UTF-16 code units without NUL or carriage return.
The parser requires each exact marker `## Context`, `## Challenge`,
`## Approach`, `## Implementation`, `## Verification`, `## Outcome` once and
in that order. These are substring/order checks, not a full Markdown AST or
proof of section quality. Every returned evidence ID must be unique, known,
and appear as `[evidence:ID]` in the Markdown.
errors: For Extend Pipeline Review and Case Study Reports, stop on the first owning schema/authority/identity/tool/lifecycle failure; preserve original diagnostic and respect explicitly unsupported routes.

Source boundary: Both use the original `kubeclaw.pipeline-review:evidence` adapter. That adapter
reads original completed Core state and selected original artifacts. The agent
receives a bounded structured projection, never authority to supply historical
success facts. This keeps source evidence independent of generated prose. Its
cost is explicit selection, integrity checks and omissions: it cannot answer
questions that require an omitted raw log or unsupported artifact class.
Reconsider that boundary only with a source-qualified new content class and
bounded reader tests, not by copying arbitrary agent text into trusted facts.

Source boundary: The adapter accepts only terminal succeeded, failed or cancelled source runs. A
waiting, reopened, blocked, incomplete, stale-head or unresolved-effect source
is not completed report authority. Failed/cancelled completed history can be
reported honestly; reporting it never converts its outcome to success.

Source boundary: Other artifacts are unsupported, not silently trusted. For example, the local
one-stage Delivery Lint workflow does not provide the required implementation
artifact and cannot be relabelled into this report source contract.
effects: Selected package/reliability tests differ from model dispatch and storing generated reports; passed means a structurally valid stored draft, not true narrative.

Source boundary: `kubeclaw.pipeline-review` generates an advisory assessment of a completed run.
`kubeclaw.case-study` generates a cited Markdown draft about that run. Neither
changes the source run's verdict, repairs its code, establishes product
acceptance or authorizes publication. `passed` means that the package generated
and stored its own valid output, not that every narrative sentence is true.

Source boundary: Both use the original `kubeclaw.pipeline-review:evidence` adapter. That adapter
reads original completed Core state and selected original artifacts. The agent
receives a bounded structured projection, never authority to supply historical
success facts. This keeps source evidence independent of generated prose. Its
cost is explicit selection, integrity checks and omissions: it cannot answer
questions that require an omitted raw log or unsupported artifact class.
Reconsider that boundary only with a source-qualified new content class and
bounded reader tests, not by copying arbitrary agent text into trusted facts.

Source boundary: Each package is version 1.0.0 in the Nova role. The case-study package does not
register its own evidence adapter. Use the
[package catalogues](../plugin-catalogue/README.md) for generated registration
facts, and [Core state/recovery](../../understand/nova-core.md) for the original
run authority.
cleanup: Drain retained dispatch; preserve original run, bundle/report/artifact evidence; do not rewrite v3 history or promise rollback-all.

Source boundary: v4 intentionally removes caller `facts`, `evidence`, project labels and target
attempt numbers as authority. Migrate old authored inputs explicitly. There is
no v3 fallback and no automatic rewrite of retained report inputs.

Source boundary: The evidence adapter creates no separate report history store. It reads the
original Nova/artifact authority. Core owns durable report attempts, dispatch
effects and receipts; the original artifact store owns completed report JSON.
The report's active execution identity remains separate from its historical
target. Do not remove either history when changing or uninstalling a package.

Source boundary: At entry, the adapter asserts the current resource fence only for a
non-confidential invocation. The confidential branch does not assert a fence;
it is not evidence of fencing enforcement. Both branches reject stopped or
cancelled work, propagate the invocation signal to artifact reads, and check
stopped/cancelled state again before returning. `shutdown` marks the reader
stopped. Synchronous history parsing is bounded by byte limits, not a claimed
preemptible native process.
The generic Core/adapter effect protocol owns dispatch idempotency and lost
responses. These packages have no universal report-specific receipt import,
automatic compensation or rollback of external agent execution.
expectedResults: Whole Extend Pipeline Review and Case Study Reports route must preserve its declared proof ladder/observations; native input/check results are limited to their actual owning action, not activation by association.

Source boundary: The schema and runtime readers perform different checks; strings are not

owning artifact records, not from a generated report. The
[SDK artifact rules](../../reference/sdk.md#artifact-byte-verification) explain
why an arbitrary same-digest reference is insufficient.

anchors.exactExcerpt:
The closed response requires `status: reviewed`, a nonblank summary of at most
8,192 UTF-16 code units, and 5–128 observations covering every dimension.
Each observation is closed: one valid dimension, priority low/medium/high,
nonblank finding of at most 8,192 UTF-16 code units, and 1–128 unique known
evidence IDs. No uncited observation or extra agent-owned control field passes.

The stage adds current `execution`, current report run/attempt, historical
`reportTarget`, `evidenceStatus: verified-source-bundle`,
`narrativeStatus: draft-not-entailment-verified`, and the verified source bundle.
It stores JSON in namespace `kubeclaw.pipeline-review` under
`pipeline-review:<digest-of-active-execution>`. It verifies the original store
response against exact canonical bytes, byte length and active producing attempt
before returning passed with the artifact reference.

The agent protocol is `kubeclaw.case-study.v4`. The agent owns only
`{status, markdown, evidenceIds}`, with `status: generated`.
Markdown is 1–131,072 UTF-16 code units without NUL or carriage return.
The parser requires each exact marker `## Context`, `## Challenge`,
`## Approach`, `## Implementation`, `## Verification`, `## Outcome` once and
in that order. These are substring/order checks, not a full Markdown AST or
proof of section quality. Every returned evidence ID must be unique, known,
and appear as `[evidence:ID]` in the Markdown.

The schema and runtime readers perform different checks; strings are not
permissions. Obtain these identities from preserved completed run state and
owning artifact records, not from a generated report. The
[SDK artifact rules](../../reference/sdk.md#artifact-byte-verification) explain
why an arbitrary same-digest reference is insufficient.

Selected artifacts must occur in that exact run projection and latest attempt.
The adapter reads original JSON bytes with the complete expected reference,
checks digest/size/media type and budget, and only admits these fact classes:

Both use the original `kubeclaw.pipeline-review:evidence` adapter. That adapter
reads original completed Core state and selected original artifacts. The agent
receives a bounded structured projection, never authority to supply historical
success facts. This keeps source evidence independent of generated prose. Its
cost is explicit selection, integrity checks and omissions: it cannot answer
questions that require an omitted raw log or unsupported artifact class.
Reconsider that boundary only with a source-qualified new content class and
bounded reader tests, not by copying arbitrary agent text into trusted facts.

The adapter accepts only terminal succeeded, failed or cancelled source runs. A
waiting, reopened, blocked, incomplete, stale-head or unresolved-effect source
is not completed report authority. Failed/cancelled completed history can be
reported honestly; reporting it never converts its outcome to success.

Other artifacts are unsupported, not silently trusted. For example, the local
one-stage Delivery Lint workflow does not provide the required implementation
artifact and cannot be relabelled into this report source contract.

`kubeclaw.pipeline-review` generates an advisory assessment of a completed run.
`kubeclaw.case-study` generates a cited Markdown draft about that run. Neither
changes the source run's verdict, repairs its code, establishes product
acceptance or authorizes publication. `passed` means that the package generated
and stored its own valid output, not that every narrative sentence is true.

Each package is version 1.0.0 in the Nova role. The case-study package does not
register its own evidence adapter. Use the
[package catalogues](../plugin-catalogue/README.md) for generated registration
facts, and [Core state/recovery](../../understand/nova-core.md) for the original
run authority.

v4 intentionally removes caller `facts`, `evidence`, project labels and target
attempt numbers as authority. Migrate old authored inputs explicitly. There is
no v3 fallback and no automatic rewrite of retained report inputs.

The evidence adapter creates no separate report history store. It reads the
original Nova/artifact authority. Core owns durable report attempts, dispatch
effects and receipts; the original artifact store owns completed report JSON.
The report's active execution identity remains separate from its historical
target. Do not remove either history when changing or uninstalling a package.

At entry, the adapter asserts the current resource fence only for a
non-confidential invocation. The confidential branch does not assert a fence;
it is not evidence of fencing enforcement. Both branches reject stopped or
cancelled work, propagate the invocation signal to artifact reads, and check
stopped/cancelled state again before returning. `shutdown` marks the reader
stopped. Synchronous history parsing is bounded by byte limits, not a claimed
preemptible native process.
The generic Core/adapter effect protocol owns dispatch idempotency and lost
responses. These packages have no universal report-specific receipt import,
automatic compensation or rollback of external agent execution.

Source boundary: A **workspace** is an npm package installed through the root lockfile. A
**runtime role** is the package set assembled for a deployable Nova, Buster, or
Prism runtime. A workspace install does not prove that a role contains that
package. A **contract** is a versioned machine boundary. A **projection** is a
view derived from durable records; it does not replace those records. A
**digest** identifies exact bytes or a declared canonical encoding of a value.
A **fixture** is bounded input and expected behavior for a check.
An **invariant** is a rule that must remain true after each supported action.
**Admission** is the decision to accept new work before it starts. **Fencing**
closes that path when the current owner cannot prove its authority; it does not
mean that running work has already stopped. A **spool** stores queued output
bytes on disk until their owner can deliver or seal them. **Backpressure** slows
or rejects new input when a bounded queue cannot accept more data.
**Portable JSON** is the SDK's restricted JSON value/encoding contract, not
arbitrary JavaScript serialization. I

Source boundary: Use a filesystem qualified for the required Linux locks, complete append
writes, and file synchronization. Do not assume a shared/network mount has the
same durability behavior. Never unlink or replace a stable lock inode while a
process can use it. Synchronizing the journal file does not by itself prove
that the entry linking it into its parent directory survives a host crash.
The C isolation launcher requires a C11 compiler named `cc`.
Use Bash and GNU `tar` for bundle scripts. Use Git for checkout, source-identity,
and compatibility fixtures. Keep fixture work outside a deployed run root.

roots, exclusions, and supported syntax. An unsupported source form is a blocker

A nested configuration field changes its default. Updating a table is not enough:
the consumer may apply a different default, an operator may need a restart, and
an old example may now request the wrong behavior. This workflow connects the
source change to its explanation, generated facts, failure path, and reader task.

uses the same steps and stop conditions as a human maintainer.

itself inventory every public surface, run a reader task, or choose every test.

prerequisites: Root preparation, schema/types/resolver/runner/protocol/Go/CRD/role and selected native dependencies; unknown identity or stale writers stop.

Source boundary: 1. Add a versioned JSON file under `contracts/pipeline-test-gate/v1/suites`.
2. Use a globally unique `contractId` and the current template schema version.
3. Give every fixture and test a stable local name.
4. Select exact provider contract IDs. Do not name packages or source paths.
5. Set mode, retries, dependencies, port links, conditions, matrices, evidence
   choices, and concurrency groups explicitly where needed.
6. Keep project-specific commands, origins, image names, and credentials out of
   a shared template unless they are a deliberate product default.
7. Add the suite to the catalogue input used by Nova and test duplicate IDs.
8. Add resolver vectors for selection, exclusion, permitted override, matrix,
   link compatibility, retry safety, deterministic order, and stable digest.
9. Add a remote runner vector for success and one representative failure.
10. Document purpose, boundary, all fields and defaults, prerequisites,
    evidence, pass/fail/skip, diagnosis, customization, and verification.

Source boundary: Treat CRD schema, controller validation, reconciliation, RBAC, and admission
fence as one feature. When adding a spec field, decide immutability and include
it in the stored specification digest. When adding a resource, label it with
lease identity, verify ownership before update or delete, and add it to cleanup.
errors: For Develop Buster Core, stop on the first owning schema/authority/identity/tool/lifecycle failure; preserve original diagnostic and respect explicitly unsupported routes.

Source boundary: - **Problem and constraints:** New tests need executable meaning, but a change to
  Buster Core changes the authority and recovery surface shared by all suites.
- **Decision:** Put test meaning in versioned providers,
  report parsing in adapters, and composition in suites. Change the engine only
  when a public extension contract cannot express the required behavior.
- **Rejected alternative:** Add common test behavior directly to the engine.
  [ADR-003](../../decisions/core-and-plugins.md#adr-003-keep-buster-test-semantics-outside-nova-and-worker-core)

cleanup.statement: The deployment script also performs two narrower maintenance operations. A patch describes changes to an existing object. A strategic merge patch uses the schema to combine fields and identify matching list items. Nova's retired trust cleanup uses a strategic merge patch with keyed container, environment, mount and volume deletion directives. Buster's port cleanup uses JSON Patch: it tests the selected container name at the discovered index, then replaces that container's complete ports list. Neither patch is a general update route for every Deployment field. The JSON test can fail after a concurrent container-order change; do not remove the test to force a stale index. [Nova cleanup](../../../scripts/deploy.sh#L1237-L1254). [Buster cleanup](../../../scripts/deploy.sh#L1257-L1281).

A map associates keys with values; a list contains items. A scalar is one value, such as a number or string. Client-side apply first reads the live object. If it is absent, the client records the apply annotation, removes null-valued map entries and creates the object. Fresh typed decoding/defaulting follows at the API server. A null manifest leaf at this create step therefore cannot be treated as a retained typed scalar null case. A present list element or its parent can still fail decoding or validation. paths. Do not downgrade an unhandled execution, contract, authority, or
evidence failure into an ordinary test assertion or a passing result.

The production verification harness reads `KUBECLAW_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS` as
JSON. This is a remote capability routing catalogue, not the installed Buster
plugin registry or a Kubernetes namespace configuration. Its provider IDs use lowercase DNS-label syntax (1–63 characters). Each provider
needs an agentRole and a nonempty capabilities map. The parser checks
`String(agentRole)` and `String(adapter)` against the same DNS-label pattern,
but returns their original values without string conversion. For example, JSON
boolean `true` and number `1` pass that lexical check and remain a boolean
and number in the returned record; this is not string-only type validation.
Capability names are dotted lowercase identifiers; each route needs an adapter
whose string form passes that check and an HTTP(S)
origin without credentials, path beyond '/', query, or fragment. The parser
normalizes the endpoint to its origin. Unknown input fields are not rejected,
but they are not copied to the returned records.

1. The loader resolves the runtime file itself to a real path. Relative paths
   in the file resolve from its containing directory.
2. It reads `KUBECLAW_BUILD_REVISION` and named secrets from the supplied
   environment. Secret values do not come from JSON.
3. It loads `platformConfig`, discovers installed packages, applies package
   trust, and builds one immutable registry snapshot.
4. It validates root service limits and each configured capability block.
5. It creates durable stores, the execution service, and the HTTP runtime.
6. `start()` recovers durable jobs before it opens the listener.

## Common Node Rules

Each test or fixture name is local to the resolved plan. `uses` selects the
exact provider contract. `config` must satisfy that provider's strict schema;
unknown fields fail. `needs` orders nodes. `inputs` connects a named input
port to one exact upstream output. A dependency alone does not transfer data.

`mode: blocking` contributes failure to the gate. `mode: advisory` records the
result without blocking the gate. A fixture supplies a resource and has no
quality mode. Positive `retries` requires `retrySafe: true` or the explicit
`acceptUnsafeRetry: true` acknowledgment, and must stay within the policy retry
limit. A non-retry-safe provider gets zero retries when `retries` is omitted.
A retry creates a new attempt identity; it does not erase
prior evidence. `concurrencyGroup` uses the resolved group limit.

A condition can produce `skipped`. An unavailable dependency can also skip a
consumer. A skipped node is not a pass. Required coverage still applies after
suite exclusions and condition evaluation. Buster distinguishes:

- `passed`: execution completed and all provider assertions passed;
- `failed`: execution completed and an assertion or budget failed;
- `errored`: execution could not produce a trustworthy assertion result;
- `skipped`: the declared condition or dependency prevented execution;
- `cancelled`: the job or attempt authority requested cancellation.

## Verification Matrix

| Change | Minimum checks | Environment claim |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Suite composition | `npm run verify:test-gate:suite-resolver` | Deterministic local contract proof. |
| Provider manifest/schema | `npm run verify:test-gate:provider-registry` and package tests | Discovery, identity, schema, and provider logic. |
| Runner or evidence | `npm run verify:test-gate:plan-runner` | Local execution-contract proof. |
| One concrete provider | Its `verify:test-gate:*implementation` script | Read the script; some checks need real tools or network. |
| Namespace fixture | `go test ./cmd/buster-namespace-controller/...` plus Helm rendering | Controller logic and rendered policy, not live cluster proof. |
| Browser, scanner, BuildKit, registry, Kubernetes, or Tailscale | Provider check in a disposable configured environment | Live integration proof. |

### Exact suite checks

Use the implementation command after a schema, provider, runtime, or report
change. Use the live command only in its configured environment. A preflight
command proves that dependencies and policy are ready; it does not replace the
implementation command.

| Suite | Local implementation check | Live or production check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | `npm run verify:test-gate:phase8` | `npm run verify:test-gate:unit-live` |
| Container build | `npm run verify:test-gate:container-build-implementation` | `npm run verify:test-gate:container-build-live` |
| Kubernetes fixture | `npm run verify:test-gate:kubernetes-fixture-implementation` | `npm run verify:test-gate:kubernetes-fixture-live` |
| HTTP | `npm run verify:test-gate:http-implementation` | `npm run verify:test-gate:http-live` |
| Tailscale exposure | `npm run verify:test-gate:tailscale-exposure-implementation` | `npm run verify:test-gate:tailscale-exposure-live` |
| API | `npm run verify:test-gate:api-implementation` | `npm run verify:test-gate:api-cutover` |
| Accessibility | `npm run verify:test-gate:a11y-implementation` | `npm run verify:test-gate:a11y-live` |
| Performance | `npm run verify:test-gate:lighthouse-implementation` | `npm run verify:test-gate:lighthouse-live` |
| Visual | `npm run verify:test-gate:visual-implementation` | `npm run verify:test-gate:visual-live` |
| End-to-end | `npm run verify:test-gate:e2e-implementation` | `npm run verify:test-gate:e2e-live` |
| Security | `npm run verify:test-gate:security-implementation` | `npm run verify:test-gate:security-live` |
| Size budget | `npm run verify:test-gate:size-budget-implementation` | `npm run verify:test-gate:size-budget-production` |

API and size budget have no live alias. Their right-hand commands are the
strongest registered production-boundary checks. A successful check does not
claim that an unrelated external target is healthy.

### Configure, execute, and diagnose each suite

The commands above are maintained verification programs. The `implementation`
commands use controlled fixtures and prove provider behavior without claiming
that an external service is ready. A `live` command uses configured external
dependencies or submits a real remote plan. Read its source before use because
the source defines required environment variables and safety checks. Never set
an environment flag only to make a precondition disappear.

For a project run, put the configuration described below in the applicable
test scope, resolve it, and let Nova submit it as described in the
[operator workflow](../use/workflows/buster-suite.md#supported-execution-paths).
The platform operator must first enable the matching capability in the
[Buster runtime configuration](buster-runtime-configuration.md#capability-blocks).
For a repository proof, first complete the canonical
[Locked Dependency Installation](../use/quickstart.md#locked-dependency-installation),
then run the exact command from the repository root. A command must exit zero
and print its final success record. Keep the
command, output, Git revision, and external target identity together.

| Suite | Project configuration that makes work explicit | Executable repository proof | What to inspect first when it fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | Select `kubeclaw.unit-suite@1`; add a `direct-command` node with an operator-catalog executable and a declared JUnit path. Start from `unit-suite-blocking.json`. | `npm run verify:test-gate:phase8`; use `npm run verify:test-gate:unit-live` only with the remote token, source key, and configured Buster route required by its source. | Catalogue denial or process start means runtime policy. A zero exit with missing or invalid JUnit means report production, not transport. |
| Container build | Add `kubeclaw.container-build@1` to the empty suite; select exactly one Dockerfile or template definition and an allowed Linux platform. | `npm run verify:test-gate:container-build-implementation`; then `npm run verify:test-gate:container-build-live` where BuildKit and the target registry are configured. | Separate BuildKit execution from registry manifest read-back. A pushed digest that cannot be read and matched is an error. |
| Kubernetes fixture | Add a manifest-producing node and link its checked-manifest output to `kubeclaw.kubernetes-fixture@1`; use an immutable image and bounded retention. | `npm run verify:test-gate:kubernetes-fixture-implementation`; the remote production path is `npm run verify:test-gate:kubernetes-fixture-live`. | Inspect broker authorization, lease phase, manifest/image binding, readiness, and cleanup in that order. Preserve a retained lease expiry. |
| HTTP | Add `kubeclaw.http@1` with an approved direct target or a typed deployment/exposure input, expected statuses, and bounded response size. | `npm run verify:test-gate:http-implementation`; use `npm run verify:test-gate:http-live` for the complete remote fixture path or the explicitly gated `http-capability-live` check for one in-cluster origin. | Distinguish origin-policy denial and transport error from a received response that violates an assertion. |
| Tailscale exposure | Link a retained deployment to `kubeclaw.tailscale-exposure@1`; choose `release` or the durable `await-readiness` handoff and an allowed host suffix. | `npm run verify:test-gate:tailscale-exposure-implementation`; use `npm run verify:test-gate:tailscale-exposure-live` only with the cluster, Tailscale operator, immutable image, and remote credentials required by the script. | Inspect deployment ownership, exposure generation, ingress status, handoff, and release. Never delete an object owned by a newer generation. |
| API | Select `kubeclaw.api-suite@1`; provide `.swarm/api-flow.json` and `.swarm/openapi.json`, then override target selection and operations for the project. | `npm run verify:test-gate:api-implementation`; `npm run verify:test-gate:api-cutover` is the strongest registered boundary check, not a general external API health test. | For flow, inspect the first failed step and cleanup result. For OpenAPI, inspect supported-subset validation and operation selection before network evidence. |
| Accessibility | Select `kubeclaw.a11y-suite@1`; provide the endpoint and optional project profile, and use only exact, reasoned, expiring acceptances. | `npm run verify:test-gate:a11y-implementation`; use `npm run verify:test-gate:a11y-live` with the configured browser and remote endpoint path. | Separate browser launch or origin denial from Axe violations. An expired acceptance cannot suppress a violation; a matching violation remains a failed finding, not an execution error. |
| Performance | Select `kubeclaw.lighthouse-suite@1`; provide the settings file, profile, target, and operator-known budget for blocking performance. | `npm run verify:test-gate:lighthouse-implementation`; use `npm run verify:test-gate:lighthouse-live` with its Chrome, target, and remote-runtime prerequisites. | Inspect Chrome launch and bounded report parsing before score or audit findings. Compare the retained median representative with all run summaries. |
| Visual | Select `kubeclaw.visual-suite@1`; commit a reviewed baseline manifest, images, browser profile, and exact browser identity. | `npm run verify:test-gate:visual-implementation`; use `npm run verify:test-gate:visual-live` only in an environment with the required browser and target. | Check baseline digest and browser family/version before pixel findings. A provider failure must not update the baseline. |
| End-to-end | Select `kubeclaw.e2e-suite@1`; commit the Playwright configuration and tests, set a positive blocking test minimum, and declare required test titles where omission matters. | `npm run verify:test-gate:e2e-implementation`; use `npm run verify:test-gate:e2e-live` with the sandbox, browsers, remote endpoint, and credentials declared by the script. | Inspect sandbox/process admission, Playwright JSON, executed-test count, required titles, and attachment limits before individual assertions. |
| Security | Select `kubeclaw.security-suite@1`; link its deployment, image, and checked manifest; configure strict policies and exact expiring acceptances. | `npm run verify:test-gate:security-implementation`; use `npm run verify:test-gate:security-live` only with Trivy databases, registry access, cluster observation, endpoint, and remote runtime ready. | Route by node. Check database freshness for Trivy, response evidence for headers, immutable input binding for static scans, and observation freshness for runtime security. |
| Size budget | Add `kubeclaw.size-budget@1` to the empty suite, link one build-output artifact, and set at least one blocking absolute or growth limit. | `npm run verify:test-gate:size-budget-implementation`; `npm run verify:test-gate:size-budget-production` proves the production boundary without an external build service. | Check artifact digest and archive safety before budget findings. A growth rule without a valid baseline is an error. |

The empty suites need an added project node. The composed suites still need
their project files, targets, and typed inputs. A resolver success with no node
in an empty suite proves only that the declaration is valid; it does not prove
that a test ran. The final result must name an attempt for every required node,
show a passed gate decision, import all evidence, and prove cleanup or bounded
retention.

For a worked composition and diagnosis path, continue with
[Run and diagnose a Buster suite](../use/workflows/buster-suite.md). For a new
provider or suite contract, continue with [Extend Buster](../extend/buster.md).

## Evidence and Reports

Evidence is immutable attempt output. A provider can declare only types in its
manifest. Buster checks relative path safety, file presence, digest, size,
duplicate IDs, and outcome-specific requirements before storage. Logs are
runner-owned evidence. A report is evidence plus a declared format that an
installed adapter can normalize.

The current report adapter supports JUnit XML. Normalization can cap retained
case details, but the original report remains stored and the adapter still
validates the complete document. A provider result with a missing required
report is an error, even when its process returned zero.

### JUnit input forms and normalization

The adapter accepts a `testsuite` root or a `testsuites` container, including
nested suites. Direct `testsuites/testcase` children are supported for Node's
reporter shape. Their stable suite path uses the container's `name`, defaulting
to `testsuites`; nested cases use their enclosing suite names. Missing suite
names receive ordinal fallbacks. Case IDs include suite path, class/name and
case ordinal, so repeated names do not collapse into one result.

Each case begins passed. `failure` records a failed case; `error` takes precedence
over failure; `skipped` applies while the case remains passed. Observed cases,
not declared suite count attributes, determine totals. Durations are finite,
nonnegative decimal seconds, converted to milliseconds, with a 30-day per-case
ceiling. The adapter emits normalized data; it does not reread source files,
change the report artifact or decide the pipeline gate.

During entity decoding, the adapter accepts the named references `amp`, `lt`,
`gt`, `quot`, `apos` and valid decimal/hexadecimal numeric references. Invalid XML
characters and unknown/malformed references reject when decoded. DTD/custom
entity declarations are forbidden; escaped text or CDATA containing declaration
characters is text, not a declaration. XML syntax continues to be parsed after
retained-detail caps. Issue text capture is bounded at 8192 UTF-16 units and
normalized displayed text at 4096 units; omitted text is not evidence of a full
retained diagnostic. Use the [SDK report contract](sdk.md#test-providers-and-report-adapters)
for complete/truncated counts and omitted-detail relationships.

> **Source evidence — JUnit forms, entities and normalized results**
>
> **Claim:** JUnit supports nested suites and direct-container cases; permitted character references are distinct from forbidden declarations.
>
> **Implementation:** [entity decoder](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/3cf7dc4f72c2ae1e0ba4c47cceb08c98f4c70b7f/skills/buster/plugins/junit-report-adapter/src/adapter.js#L28-L63) and [root/suite/case admission](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/3cf7dc4f72c2ae1e0ba4c47cceb08c98f4c70b7f/skills/buster/plugins/junit-report-adapter/src/adapter.js#L214-L257).
>
> **Contract or setting:** [XML completion and retained-result rules](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/3cf7dc4f72c2ae1e0ba4c47cceb08c98f4c70b7f/skills/buster/plugins/junit-report-adapter/src/adapter.js#L316-L365). Buster retains the original report separately from normalized detail caps.
>
> **Test evidence:** [nested/direct-container/entity/truncation assertions](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/3cf7dc4f72c2ae1e0ba4c47cceb08c98f4c70b7f/skills/buster/plugins/junit-report-adapter/tests/adapter.test.mjs#L12-L55) were read, not run. They are not a live adapter-sandbox or full-report acceptance result.
>
> **Revision:** `3cf7dc4f72c2ae1e0ba4c47cceb08c98f4c70b7f`; each linked whole file matches current Source.
>
> **Limit:** This path grants no arbitrary file reads, report mutation, new parser dialect or pipeline decision authority.

## Error Codes and Safe Actions

An error code identifies the boundary that could not produce trustworthy test
facts. A failed assertion is a provider result with findings, not an
exception code. Preserve the complete code suffix because it can contain the
node, field, port, or artifact that failed.

Use the [exact Buster error-code reference](buster-error-codes.md) to find every
code emitted by the shipped suite providers. The table below is the shorter
routing view. It groups codes by the operator action that they require.

| Suite or boundary | Code families and important exact codes | Safe action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plan and suite | `TEST_PLAN_SUITE_*`, `TEST_PLAN_NODE_*`, `TEST_PLAN_CONFIGURATION_INVALID`, `TEST_PLAN_MATRIX_*`, `TEST_PLAN_DEPENDENCY_*`, `TEST_PLAN_PORT_*`, `TEST_PLAN_COVERAGE_*` | Correct the declaration or installed registry. Do not send an unresolved plan. |
| Unit and reports | `DIRECT_COMMAND_*`, `TEST_REPORT_*`, `JUNIT_*`, `COVERAGE_*` | Check catalogue executable, paths, exit, report/LCOV bytes, and declared outputs. Keep JUnit required when the tool supports it. |
| Container build | `CONTAINER_BUILD_*` | Check repository paths, definition, BuildKit, registry policy, pushed manifest, and digest equality. |
| Kubernetes fixture | `KUBERNETES_FIXTURE_*` | Check image/manifest inputs, lease status, broker authorization, credentials, readiness, and cleanup. Do not bypass the lease. |
| HTTP | `HTTP_CONFIG_*`, `HTTP_INPUT_*`, `HTTP_TARGET_*`, `HTTP_REQUEST_FAILED`, `HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, `HTTP_RESPONSE_INVALID` | Separate invalid declaration, target selection, transport failure, and assertion findings. |
| Tailscale exposure | `TAILSCALE_EXPOSURE_*` | Check deployment lease, selected endpoint, ingress owner/generation, Tailscale readiness, handoff, and release. |
| API flow | `API_FLOW_*` | Validate the flow file, variables, dependencies, bounded steps, origin policy, response limits, and cleanup result. |
| OpenAPI | `OPENAPI_*` | Validate the document and selected operation against the supported subset; then inspect request and response facts. |
| Accessibility | `AXE_*` and `BROWSER_AXE_*` | Check target, profile, route, acceptance expiry, browser policy, and bounded result. |
| Performance | `LIGHTHOUSE_*` and `BROWSER_LIGHTHOUSE_*` | Check target, settings, profile, budget, Chrome launch, network evidence, and representative report. |
| Visual | `VISUAL_*` and `BROWSER_VISUAL_*` | Check baseline contract/digest, browser identity, masks, target selection, PNG limits, and comparison output. |
| End-to-end | `PLAYWRIGHT_*` and `BROWSER_PLAYWRIGHT_*` | Check project/config paths, target, process isolation, JSON report, executed-test minimum, required titles, and attachments. |
| Security | `SECURITY_*`, `DEPENDENCY_SCAN_*`, `IMAGE_SCAN_*`, `KUBERNETES_POLICY_*`, `KUBERNETES_RUNTIME_SECURITY_*` | Check strict policy, acceptance expiry, database evidence, immutable inputs, scanner result, and live cluster proof. |
| Size budget | `SIZE_BUDGET_*` | Check input and baseline digests, archive safety, glob rules, decompression limits, and blocking budget presence. |
| Remote engine | `BUSTER_REMOTE_*`, `BUSTER_SOURCE_*`, `TEST_PROVIDER_*`, `TEST_REPORT_ADAPTER_*` | Diagnose admission, store, package, attempt, evidence, result, and import in that order. Never translate an integrity error into a test failure. |

The code family is stable for operator routing. The generated exact reference
must stay equal to the provider and capability sources. Do not infer retry
safety from `TIMEOUT` or `FAILED`. Use the provider contract and attempt state.

errors.statement: Unknown provider config/link/matrix/policy rejects at its owner. Positive retries require actual retrySafe or explicit unsafe acknowledgement within policy; new attempt does not erase evidence. Exact HTTP_REQUEST_FAILED/TIMEOUT translate to findings, while other capability/integrity/cancellation errors remain execution errors. Preserve provider/report outcome and original cause.

## Evidence and Reports

Evidence is immutable attempt output. A provider can declare only types in its
manifest. Buster checks relative path safety, file presence, digest, size,
duplicate IDs, and outcome-specific requirements before storage. Logs are
runner-owned evidence. A report is evidence plus a declared format that an
installed adapter can normalize.

The current report adapter supports JUnit XML. Normalization can cap retained
case details, but the original report remains stored and the adapter still
validates the complete document. A provider result with a missing required
report is an error, even when its process returned zero.

### JUnit input forms and normalization

The adapter accepts a `testsuite` root or a `testsuites` container, including
nested suites. Direct `testsuites/testcase` children are supported for Node's
reporter shape. Their stable suite path uses the container's `name`, defaulting
to `testsuites`; nested cases use their enclosing suite names. Missing suite
names receive ordinal fallbacks. Case IDs include suite path, class/name and
case ordinal, so repeated names do not collapse into one result.

Each case begins passed. `failure` records a failed case; `error` takes precedence
over failure; `skipped` applies while the case remains passed. Observed cases,
not declared suite count attributes, determine totals. Durations are finite,
nonnegative decimal seconds, converted to milliseconds, with a 30-day per-case
ceiling. The adapter emits normalized data; it does not reread source files,
change the report artifact or decide the pipeline gate.

During entity decoding, the adapter accepts the named references `amp`, `lt`,
`gt`, `quot`, `apos` and valid decimal/hexadecimal numeric references. Invalid XML
characters and unknown/malformed references reject when decoded. DTD/custom
entity declarations are forbidden; escaped text or CDATA containing declaration
characters is text, not a declaration. XML syntax continues to be parsed after
retained-detail caps. Issue text capture is bounded at 8192 UTF-16 units and
normalized displayed text at 4096 units; omitted text is not evidence of a full
retained diagnostic. Use the [SDK report contract](sdk.md#test-providers-and-report-adapters)
for complete/truncated counts and omitted-detail relationships.

## Common Node Rules

Each test or fixture name is local to the resolved plan. `uses` selects the
exact provider contract. `config` must satisfy that provider's strict schema;
unknown fields fail. `needs` orders nodes. `inputs` connects a named input
port to one exact upstream output. A dependency alone does not transfer data.

`mode: blocking` contributes failure to the gate. `mode: advisory` records the
result without blocking the gate. A fixture supplies a resource and has no
quality mode. Positive `retries` requires `retrySafe: true` or the explicit
`acceptUnsafeRetry: true` acknowledgment, and must stay within the policy retry
limit. A non-retry-safe provider gets zero retries when `retries` is omitted.
A retry creates a new attempt identity; it does not erase
prior evidence. `concurrencyGroup` uses the resolved group limit.

A condition can produce `skipped`. An unavailable dependency can also skip a
consumer. A skipped node is not a pass. Required coverage still applies after
suite exclusions and condition evaluation. Buster distinguishes:

- `passed`: execution completed and all provider assertions passed;
- `failed`: execution completed and an assertion or budget failed;
- `errored`: execution could not produce a trustworthy assertion result;
- `skipped`: the declared condition or dependency prevented execution;
- `cancelled`: the job or attempt authority requested cancellation.

`mode: blocking` contributes failure to the gate. `mode: advisory` records the
result without blocking the gate. A fixture supplies a resource and has no
quality mode. Positive `retries` requires `retrySafe: true` or the explicit

limit. A non-retry-safe provider gets zero retries when `retries` is omitted.

prior evidence. `concurrencyGroup` uses the resolved group limit.

- `skipped`: the declared condition or dependency prevented execution;
- `cancelled`: the job or attempt authority requested cancellation.

## Evidence and Reports

Evidence is immutable attempt output. A provider can declare only types in its
manifest. Buster checks relative path safety, file presence, digest, size,
duplicate IDs, and outcome-specific requirements before storage. Logs are
runner-owned evidence. A report is evidence plus a declared format that an
installed adapter can normalize.

The current report adapter supports JUnit XML. Normalization can cap retained
case details, but the original report remains stored and the adapter still
validates the complete document. A provider result with a missing required
report is an error, even when its process returned zero.

### JUnit input forms and normalization

The adapter accepts a `testsuite` root or a `testsuites` container, including
nested suites. Direct `testsuites/testcase` children are supported for Node's
reporter shape. Their stable suite path uses the container's `name`, defaulting
to `testsuites`; nested cases use their enclosing suite names. Missing suite
names receive ordinal fallbacks. Case IDs include suite path, class/name and
case ordinal, so repeated names do not collapse into one result.

Each case begins passed. `failure` records a failed case; `error` takes precedence
over failure; `skipped` applies while the case remains passed. Observed cases,
not declared suite count attributes, determine totals. Durations are finite,
nonnegative decimal seconds, converted to milliseconds, with a 30-day per-case
ceiling. The adapter emits normalized data; it does not reread source files,
change the report artifact or decide the pipeline gate.

During entity decoding, the adapter accepts the named references `amp`, `lt`,
`gt`, `quot`, `apos` and valid decimal/hexadecimal numeric references. Invalid XML
characters and unknown/malformed references reject when decoded. DTD/custom
entity declarations are forbidden; escaped text or CDATA containing declaration
characters is text, not a declaration. XML syntax continues to be parsed after
retained-detail caps. Issue text capture is bounded at 8192 UTF-16 units and
normalized displayed text at 4096 units; omitted text is not evidence of a full
retained diagnostic. Use the [SDK report contract](sdk.md#test-providers-and-report-adapters)
for complete/truncated counts and omitted-detail relationships.

> **Source evidence — JUnit forms, entities and normalized results**
>
> **Claim:** JUnit supports nested suites and direct-container cases; permitted character references are distinct from forbidden declarations.
>
> **Implementation:** [entity decoder](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/3cf7dc4f72c2ae1e0ba4c47cceb08c98f4c70b7f/skills/buster/plugins/junit-report-adapter/src/adapter.js#L28-L63) and [root/suite/case admission](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/3cf7dc4f72c2ae1e0ba4c47cceb08c98f4c70b7f/skills/buster/plugins/junit-report-adapter/src/adapter.js#L214-L257).
>

They are not a live adapter-sandbox or full-report acceptance result.

## Evidence and Reports

Evidence is immutable attempt output. A provider can declare only types in its
manifest. Buster checks relative path safety, file presence, digest, size,
duplicate IDs, and outcome-specific requirements before storage. Logs are
runner-owned evidence. A report is evidence plus a declared format that an
installed adapter can normalize.

The current report adapter supports JUnit XML. Normalization can cap retained
case details, but the original report remains stored and the adapter still
validates the complete document. A provider result with a missing required
report is an error, even when its process returned zero.

The adapter accepts a `testsuite` root or a `testsuites` container, including
nested suites. Direct `testsuites/testcase` children are supported for Node's
reporter shape. Their stable suite path uses the container's `name`, defaulting
to `testsuites`; nested cases use their enclosing suite names. Missing suite
names receive ordinal fallbacks. Case IDs include suite path, class/name and
case ordinal, so repeated names do not collapse into one result.

Each case begins passed. `failure` records a failed case; `error` takes precedence
over failure; `skipped` applies while the case remains passed. Observed cases,
not declared suite count attributes, determine totals. Durations are finite,
nonnegative decimal seconds, converted to milliseconds, with a 30-day per-case
ceiling. The adapter emits normalized data; it does not reread source files,
change the report artifact or decide the pipeline gate.

During entity decoding, the adapter accepts the named references `amp`, `lt`,
`gt`, `quot`, `apos` and valid decimal/hexadecimal numeric references. Invalid XML
characters and unknown/malformed references reject when decoded. DTD/custom
entity declarations are forbidden; escaped text or CDATA containing declaration
characters is text, not a declaration. XML syntax continues to be parsed after
retained-detail caps. Issue text capture is bounded at 8192 UTF-16 units and
normalized displayed text at 4096 units; omitted text is not evidence of a full
retained diagnostic. Use the [SDK report contract](sdk.md#test-providers-and-report-adapters)
for complete/truncated counts and omitted-detail relationships.

## Common Node Rules

Each test or fixture name is local to the resolved plan. `uses` selects the
exact provider contract. `config` must satisfy that provider's strict schema;
unknown fields fail. `needs` orders nodes. `inputs` connects a named input
port to one exact upstream output. A dependency alone does not transfer data.

`mode: blocking` contributes failure to the gate. `mode: advisory` records the
result without blocking the gate. A fixture supplies a resource and has no
quality mode. Positive `retries` requires `retrySafe: true` or the explicit
`acceptUnsafeRetry: true` acknowledgment, and must stay within the policy retry
limit. A non-retry-safe provider gets zero retries when `retries` is omitted.
A retry creates a new attempt identity; it does not erase
prior evidence. `concurrencyGroup` uses the resolved group limit.

A condition can produce `skipped`. An unavailable dependency can also skip a
consumer. A skipped node is not a pass. Required coverage still applies after
suite exclusions and condition evaluation. Buster distinguishes:

- `passed`: execution completed and all provider assertions passed;
- `failed`: execution completed and an assertion or budget failed;
- `errored`: execution could not produce a trustworthy assertion result;
- `skipped`: the declared condition or dependency prevented execution;
- `cancelled`: the job or attempt authority requested cancellation.

The cache manager adds a reference on the first registration of a Pod, or

invalidate every existing reference on each Pod update. When the last
reference is removed, it removes the cached item. anchors.exactExcerpt:
# Configuration Compatibility

Status: current support reference
Audience: operator, maintainer, plugin author
Owner: configuration-owning components
Evidence: skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/config/platform.schema.json; skills/common/plugin-runtime/contracts/plugin-system/v2/plugin-system-v2.schema.json; skills/nova/core/execution/engine-snapshots.ts; contracts/pipeline-worker-core/v1/schemas/pipeline-worker-core.v2.schema.json; contracts/pipeline-worker-core/v1/schemas/pipeline-worker-core.v3.schema.json
Applies to: current readers and retained durable versions
Last verified: 2026-09-21 at source revision `1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de`

## Support meanings

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Author | A current tool creates this version for new work. |
| Read | A current tool validates and consumes this version. |
| Recover only | Current code reads the version to continue retained state but does not create it for a new run. |
| Reject | The current boundary fails rather than guessing or translating it. |

Compatibility is per artifact. A process that can read an older snapshot does
not imply that its current project input, plugin packages, or worker result can
be mixed with that snapshot.

## Current map

| Artifact/contract | New authoring | Current read | Conditions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pipeline-platform.v2` | Author | Read | Exact version only; closed schema. There is no version fallback or field translation. |
| `nova-project.v2` | Author | Read | Exact version only. Current CLI requires explicit architecture and Blueprint declarations. |
| `pipeline-definition.v2` | Author | Read | Exact version only; plugin-owned `config`/`input` must match the installed registration schemas. |
| `.swarm/pipeline.json` | Author | Read | Current structural declaration has no root schema-version field. Compatibility is determined by loader fields, suite/provider contract IDs, registration schemas, resolver policy, and coupled generation. |
| `.swarm/progress.json` version 1 | Author through scaffold | Read by project setup and explicit import tooling | It is project authoring state, not a resumable Core snapshot. |
| `published-json-pair.v1` | Author | Read | Exact manifest/member shape, generation digest, and byte equality. |
| `run-snapshot.v4` | Author | Read/recover | Current format; includes runtime-dispatch and cache semantic profiles. |
| `run-snapshot.v3` | No new authoring | Recover only | Requires its runtime-dispatch profile; has no cache profile. |
| `run-snapshot.v1` / `v2` | No new authoring | Recover only | Must not contain newer semantic profile fields. Original runtime/package compatibility remains required. |
| `execution-graph-snapshot.v3` | Author | Read/recover | Current portable JSON digest ordering. |
| `execution-graph-snapshot.v2` | No new authoring | Recover only | Recovery rebuilds using the stored version before digest comparison. |
| `worker-attempt-envelope/result/profile.v3` | Author for native Prism | Read | Uses native-attempt-tree resources and Linux tasks. Producer, worker, and result versions must agree. |
| Worker v2 envelope/result/profile | Author for current Prism agent launcher | Read | Uses resource capability/budget v1 and `maximumProcesses`; unavailable measurement is explicit. |
| Worker v1 envelope/result/profile | Author for current Buster local test execution; also retained records | Read where the v1 contract path is selected | Buster creates capability-selected `buster.local.<capability-key>` profiles and new v1 attempts using `buster-test-engine` / `kubeclaw.buster-engine@1`, bound to the registry snapshot digest. No resource-accounting fields may be inferred. Do not turn absence into zero. |
| `worker-protocol.v1` | Author | Read | Exact protocol value in current worker versions. |
| Prism native pool policy schema `1` | Host preparation | Read | Exact role, node, digest, paths, and positive aggregate limits; actual cgroup must match. |
| Compact swarm profile `standard` | Shipped test/runtime authoring | Read only by callers of the expander | Exact feature/tuning assertions; unknown profiles/paths reject. Not a pipeline-platform version. |

Buster v1 is a current producer, not a retained-only compatibility path.
The [profile constructor](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f99aecbb00cb399b46dfbbeb3ddb375fba6218e7/skills/buster/engine/test-gates/runner.ts#L566-L588)
selects `provider.execute` plus granted provider capabilities and binds the engine
to the registry snapshot. The [attempt constructor](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f99aecbb00cb399b46dfbbeb3ddb375fba6218e7/skills/buster/engine/test-gates/runner.ts#L1518-L1525)
creates new `worker-attempt-envelope.v1` records. This does not change the
separate Prism v2 agent and v3 native authoring routes or prove live execution.

## What pins a Nova run

Run recovery checks more than a schema version:

- pipeline ID and normalized graph digest,
- registry snapshot and its dependency-identity format,
- exact package set, versions, and content digests,
- effective providers, grants, adapters, active adapters, observers, and
  isolation configuration,
- runtime-dispatch and cache semantic profiles where the snapshot version
  contains them,
- project compiler source/report/semantic selections reconstructed from the
  stored graph.

A current parser can therefore read a stored snapshot but still reject the
current runtime as incompatible. This is deliberate: reading bytes is not
authority to reinterpret a running workflow.

## Contract-ID compatibility

Stage types, provider `uses`, suite `uses`, worker engine contracts, and
capability providers are versioned identities. Selection is exact. Installing
a newer package does not redirect an older contract ID unless that package
still registers and implements it. Configuration schema defaults are part of
the selected registration version and do not backfill stored effective values.

For `.swarm/pipeline.json`, retain the suite template digest and resolved
provider package/content digests in the resolved plan. The same authored JSON
can resolve differently if the registry or operator resolver policy changes;
the plan digest makes that difference visible.

## Unsupported combinations

- A v3 native profile with v2 `maximumProcesses` budgets.
- A v2 agent profile presented to a worker that advertises only its v3 digest.
- A changed graph supplied to an existing run ID.
- A changed platform authority or unapproved package set during recovery.
- One member from each of two `.swarm` publication generations.
- A compact `swarm.config.json` passed as `--platform`.
- A project test declaration passed to the Core `--pipeline` flag.
- A chart value assumed to be effective without schema validation, rendering,
  rollout, and process readiness.

## Change procedure

Before changing a versioned configuration or package:

1. Inventory active runs and retained worker attempts that use the old version.
2. Keep the old executable and configuration available until those records are
   terminal or proved recoverable by the intended release.
3. Validate the new authoring input and compile/resolve it without effects.
4. Start new work under a new run/plan/profile digest as applicable.
5. Prove recovery separately from new-run success.

Do not edit retained snapshots, plan digests, profile digests, or publication
manifests to declare compatibility.

> **Source evidence — retained version handling**
>
> **Claim:** Current Nova authors run snapshot v4 but validates v1–v4 under version-specific fields, and graph recovery preserves the stored v2/v3 digest algorithm before comparison.
>
> **Implementation:** [snapshot versions and checks](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/nova/core/execution/engine-snapshots.ts#L75-L109); [stored graph version comparison](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/nova/core/execution/engine-snapshots.ts#L68-L73)
>
> **Contract or setting:** [current graph contract](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/common/plugin-runtime/contracts/plugin-system/v2/plugin-system-v2.schema.json#L515-L529); [current native worker profile contract](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/contracts/pipeline-worker-core/v1/schemas/pipeline-worker-core.v3.schema.json#L113-L160)
>
> **Test evidence:** [historical worker fixture test](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/prism/tests/worker-service.test.mts#L120-L151)
>
> **Check status:** On 2026-10-09, Node.js `v24.21.0` ran `node --test skills/prism/tests/worker-service.test.mts` against implementation revision `c8987b18b450bc27571d5037cb6ce3fb26e0cbd0`: six tests passed, exit zero. These tests establish the stated local rejection behavior; they do not establish a supported live upgrade or rollback pair.
>
> **Revision:** `1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de`
>
> **Limit:** Source compatibility does not prove that an older deployment image, external provider, or off-host backup remains available.

contracts.scope: Route platform/registration/compiler/graph/test-plan/publication/Prism failures by their first owning prefix and preserve bounded diagnostic identity without treating compiler admission as execution.

prerequisites.statement:
Do not delete the publication directory to force loose-file fallback. Preserve
it for diagnosis. Follow [bounded republish admission](project-pipeline-publication.md#bounded-republish-of-an-intact-generation) before any supported `--apply` retry. The CLI cannot repair malformed loose `progress.json` or replace conflicting immutable generation bytes. Keep execution stopped and follow [unsupported corruption repair](project-pipeline-publication.md#unsupported-corruption-repair) with the project-setup and storage owners for those cases.

`RECOVERY_RUNTIME_CONFIGURATION_MISMATCH`, `RECOVERY_GRAPH_DIGEST_MISMATCH`,
and `RECOVERY_PINNED_PACKAGE_*` mean the current inputs differ from recorded
authority. Restore the recorded inputs. `RUN_SNAPSHOT_INTEGRITY_INVALID` means
the durable snapshot itself fails its digest/version contract; stop and use the
documented recovery procedure.

errors.statement: Preserve this page's unsupported/uncertain/failure boundaries; do not promote a source check into runtime success.

anchors.exactExcerpt:
KubeClaw error codes identify the component that rejected the value. Preserve
the exact code and suffix. Do not remove a validation check to make an input
load.

Every `PUBLISHED_PAIR_*` error is fail-closed. `UNCOMMITTED` means the
publication directory exists without a committed pointer. `MANIFEST_INVALID`,
`MEMBER_INVALID`, and `MATERIALIZATION_DIVERGED` mean metadata/content/copies
do not agree. `CHANGED` detects a concurrent or substituted path.
`TARGET_INVALID` rejects a symlink, non-file, or multi-link target.
`GENERATION_CONFLICT` means immutable bytes already exist under the same
generation identity but differ.

effects.statement:

publication directory exists without a committed pointer. `MANIFEST_INVALID`,

generation identity but differ.

`overrides`, `discord_webhook_url`, `project`, `repo_root`, `paths`, and `run_id`.
Before expansion, the input must select `profile: "standard"`. The `features`
object must contain exactly `observability`, `buster`, and `discord_alerts`,
each set to `true`. The `tuning` object must contain `safety_margins`,
`retention`, `alerts`, `logs`, `checks`, and `determinism`, with the exact
values shown below. These objects select the supported profile shape; they
are not arbitrary feature switches. An unsupported profile, extra top-level
key, incomplete feature/tuning object, or mismatched fixed value rejects.
`overrides`, when supplied, must be an object, not an array or `null`.
A supplied `discord_webhook_url` must be a string.
