## Failure Domains And Stop Boundaries

A component boundary must also be a failure boundary.
One failed dependency must not silently move authority to another component.

| Failure domain | Direct dependency | Authoritative retained data | Safe response | Forbidden response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Project compilation | Project document, repository layout, and fixed source revision | Validated project input and compiled graph | Reject the input before a run starts | Guess a revision, path, module, or graph edge |
| Nova process | Durable run root and immutable package bytes | Graph snapshot, registry snapshot, lifecycle journal, signals, and effect records | Recover from the recorded history with the same identities | Continue from process memory or current package bytes |
| Plugin registry | Installed manifests, schemas, package roots, and trust configuration | Canonical package and registration identities with digests | Reject discovery, admission, conflict, or activation as a startup error | Import unvalidated code or select a registration by load order |
| Capability adapter | Selected provider, grant, resource constraint, and external service | Effect request, idempotency key, acceptance state, and receipt | Recover the receipt or stop for reconciliation | Repeat an accepted effect because its response was lost |
| Redis transport | Redis availability, stream policy, and authenticated callers | Transport records and the component's own durable control state | Retry transport delivery within its contract; recover authority from the owning store | Treat Redis delivery as the canonical lifecycle decision |
| Buster service | Immutable plan, source snapshot, providers, Worker Core, and result store | Remote job status, complete plan result, evidence identities, and import record | Resume or import only after identity and terminal-result checks | Convert transport completion directly into a quality verdict |
| Worker host | Profile, capacity pool, trusted supervisor, engine, and persistent attempt stores | Admission, claim, ownership, journal, output spool, observations, cleanup, and sealed result | Reconcile ownership and process state; stop when either remains uncertain | Launch a replacement attempt while an earlier process can still run |
| Prism service | PostgreSQL, artifact storage, Worker Core, and approved design identities | Projects, revisions, operations, approvals, bundles, and immutable artifacts | Recover canonical records and rebuild only declared projections | Treat a preview, editor state, or local receipt as canonical approval |
| Git or artifact storage | Repository or object-store availability and exact identity | Commit identity or artifact digest, namespace, size, and producer | Stop or recover the exact object before dependent work continues | Substitute a newer commit or an object with the same display name |
| Observer or telemetry sink | Event subscription, delivery policy, and sink | Core journal plus observer-owned checkpoint and delivery evidence | Preserve lifecycle truth and expose degraded or exhausted delivery | Reconstruct lifecycle state from a dashboard or notification |
| Kubernetes and required services | Scheduling, storage, DNS, identities, registries, BuildKit, databases, and configured network paths | Component-owned persistent volumes and external service stores | Stop the affected operation and preserve diagnostic evidence | Claim platform readiness from manifests or local source checks alone |

The table separates three questions.
A dependency can transport data, store authority, or present a projection.
Those roles are not interchangeable.

## Data Authority And Derived Copies

| Data | Canonical owner | Permitted copies or projections | Required identity check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Compiled pipeline graph | Nova run snapshot | Operator display and audit read model | Run ID and graph digest |
| Lifecycle state | Nova lifecycle journal and reducer | Status page, notification, telemetry, and audit projection | Run, stage, attempt, event sequence, and schema version |
| Plugin selection | Frozen registry and package snapshot | Catalogue and activation diagnostics | Package ID, version, content digest, registration ID, and API version |
| External effect outcome | Adapter receipt in the effect journal | Stage evidence and recovery diagnostics | Effect ID, idempotency key, owner attempt, capability, and resource |
| Human or orchestrator response | Accepted resume-signal record | Resolved-wait lifecycle event | Wait, signal, issuer, issue time, and idempotency identity |
| Worker attempt fact | Worker journal, ownership state, and sealed terminal result | Buster or Prism specialist result | Attempt, claim generation, engine, profile, protocol, result digest, and transport identity |
| Test-plan result | Buster result store | Nova import record, report, and operator view | Job, plan, run, source, request, result, and evidence digests |
| Design state | Prism PostgreSQL records and immutable artifact objects | Studio projection, preview, export, Forge assignment, and Buster plan | Project, design, revision, operation, approval, bundle, and artifact identities |
| Source state | Git object database and authorized workspace | Source archive, diff, review bundle, and build context | Repository identity and immutable commit digest |
| Large evidence | Artifact store | Report attachment and bounded display summary | Artifact ID, namespace, digest, size, and producer attempt |

## Communication, Persistence, And Retention Map

This table lists each communication path that crosses a component boundary in
the documented platform baseline. It does not list private calls inside one
component. A later implementation can replace a transport only if it preserves
the contract, authority, persistence, and failure behavior in the same row.

| Producer | Consumer | Contract or message | Transport | Authoritative persistence | Retention or cleanup owner | Effect of a failed handoff |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Project author or automation | Nova project compiler | `nova-project.v2`, referenced control files, and the selected source revision | CLI arguments and local files | Admitted project input, compiled graph, and source identity in the run root | Nova run-root policy | Compilation stops before execution. Nova does not guess a missing file, revision, or graph value. |
| Nova Core | Stage plugin | Resolved stage input, attempt lease, limits, grants, and typed stage result | In-process call for trusted code; bounded child protocol for an external stage | Nova lifecycle journal, plugin-state journal, effect journal, and artifacts | Nova run owner and artifact-store policy | The attempt fails, times out, or stops for reconciliation. A returned result cannot directly change lifecycle state. |
| Stage or observer plugin | Capability adapter | Capability, operation, canonical resource, payload, effect identity, and fence | Bounded host context; external plugins relay requests through the isolated protocol | Effect request, acceptance, receipt, and resource-lock record | Nova effect and lock-store policy | Authority is denied before the adapter, or recovery stops if an accepted effect has no known result. |
| Nova Core | Observer plugin | Ordered lifecycle or plugin-domain event with run and sequence identity | Observer invocation through the admitted registry | Core journal plus observer delivery attempts and checkpoints | Core retains the event; observer policy retains or expires delivery evidence | Required-observer exhaustion fails the flush. Optional-observer failure records a visible gap without rewriting lifecycle truth. |
| Nova test gate | Buster remote-plan service | Immutable plan job, source snapshot identity, status, result, and evidence digests | Authenticated HTTP or loopback HTTP behind the SPIFFE proxy | Nova dispatch/import stores and Buster job/result stores | Nova owns import records; Buster owns jobs, results, and evidence | Nova retries only declared transport failures. It reconciles the same job identity before a new dispatch. |
| Buster or Prism runtime | Worker Core | Worker envelope, profile, claim, cancellation, progress, logs, evidence, and terminal result | Local runtime call or a role-owned remote transport | Worker attempt journal, ownership store, output spool, and result seal | Worker host policy and the calling role's result policy | Admission rejects before launch, or recovery fences new work until ownership and process state are safe. |
| Trusted native supervisor | Unprivileged specialist host | Length-bounded envelope, framed control messages, cancellation, and provisional result | Standard input/output plus a private framed control endpoint | Supervisor-owned journal, spool, ownership record, observations, and final seal | Native worker host policy | The supervisor terminates and drains the process tree. It does not accept a result while control requests remain unsettled. |
| Redis transport adapter | Redis and an external consumer | `transport.publish` or `telemetry.emit` payload plus idempotency identity | RESP over `redis:` or TLS-protected `rediss:` | Redis stream and deduplication key; lifecycle authority stays in Nova | Redis stream length and deduplication TTL from platform configuration | Delivery can retry within adapter policy. Redis loss cannot create or change a lifecycle decision. |
| OpenClaw host agent-observer extension | Redis ingress streams and downstream observability readers | Versioned host hook, diagnostic, and agent-event projections; distinct from Nova observer delivery | Host-owned Redis client, bounded in-process queues, then `XADD` with JSON in `data` | Process queues are volatile; Redis ingress is a projection, not the Nova lifecycle journal | Host observer configuration bounds each queue, event size, stream length, command timeout, and control retry attempts | Payload writes get one writer attempt. Control writes have bounded retries, then best-effort dead-letter publication. Queue overflow, process loss, or write failure can lose projections without changing lifecycle truth. |
| Source-capable stage or service | Git repository and isolated workspace | Repository identity, immutable revision, allowed path, commit, merge, or sync request | Git process through the selected capability adapter | Git object database; Nova stores the accepted commit identity | Repository owner and workspace-cleanup policy | The operation stops on identity or path mismatch. Recovery does not substitute the current branch head. |
| Buster container-build provider | BuildKit and OCI registry | Bounded build context, Dockerfile, platform, image reference, and digest-bearing result | BuildKit API and OCI registry protocol | BuildKit cache is derived; registry content digest is the image authority | BuildKit cache policy and registry retention policy | The suite reports an execution error or failed check. It does not treat a local cache hit as a published image. |
| Prism services | PostgreSQL and artifact storage | Projects, revisions, operations, approvals, retrieval records, bundles, and artifact identities | PostgreSQL protocol and artifact capability calls | PostgreSQL owns relational design state; artifact storage owns immutable bytes | Prism database and artifact retention policy | Prism stops the affected operation. It can rebuild a declared projection, but it cannot recreate an approval from a preview. |
| Private service | Authorized remote user or test client | Service-specific HTTP route | Kubernetes Service plus Tailscale exposure when the declared path needs private external access | The service store remains authoritative; Tailscale stores connectivity state only | Service owner and Tailscale operator | The service can remain healthy while the route is unavailable. Route recovery must not replay product work. |
| Helm or Argo CD owner | Kubernetes API | Rendered Kubernetes objects and declared ownership labels | Kubernetes API | Kubernetes stores desired and observed object state; component stores retain product truth | The selected deployment owner | Reconciliation stops or reports drift. Direct Helm and Argo CD must not control the same object set. |
| Runtime and platform exporters | Monitoring stack | Metrics, logs, and traces with correlation identity | Scrape, log, or trace protocol selected by the deployment | Monitoring storage is a diagnostic projection | Monitoring retention policy | Loss reduces visibility. It does not change the run, attempt, effect, or approval state. |

> **Source evidence — component-boundary communication**
>
> **Claim:** Component handoffs retain owner-specific identities, durable records and failure decisions.
>
> **Implementation:** Stage, remote gate, observer, Redis and Worker paths below ground the communication table.
>
>
> [Nova dispatches a resolved attempt through one bounded stage context](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/13bff0a18a64e74f2cbbaa1978e746fcdeff0c10/skills/nova/core/execution/stage-executor.ts#L31-L119).

>
> [The Redis adapter publishes with a stream bound and a deduplication key](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/13bff0a18a64e74f2cbbaa1978e746fcdeff0c10/skills/common/plugins/redis-transport/src/adapter.ts#L14-L91).

> **Limit:** The table proves source-level contracts and ownership. Deployment-specific retention periods and live reachability still require the target environment's configuration and acceptance evidence.
>
> **Contract or setting:** Attempt/job/event/effect identities and delivery policies differ by owner; transport does not transfer lifecycle authority.
>
> **Test evidence:** No complete live communication/recovery matrix is established by these implementation links.
>

>

### Separate OpenClaw host observer path

The host extension normalizes hooks, model-usage diagnostics, and agent events.
It writes to `pipeline:agent-observability:control:v1` or
`pipeline:agent-observability:payload:v1`, according to the ingress event type.
The writer drains control events before payload events.
Its queue admission checks event size and the per-stream queue ceiling.
These queues and duplicate filters belong to the process, not a durable outbox.

After exhausted control-write retries, the writer attempts
`pipeline:agent-observability:deadletter:v1` with the failed source stream,
serialized event, failure time, and error. Dead-letter publication can also fail.
Payload failure does not take this dead-letter path.
Redis stream length uses approximate trimming, not an age-based retention guarantee.
A timed-out command can have reached Redis; retries do not prove exactly-once delivery.
Downstream readers must retain their own interpretation and duplicate-handling rules.
This ingress does not replay or authorize Nova lifecycle decisions.

> **Source boundary — host observer ingress**
>
> **Claim:** The OpenClaw host observer writes bounded volatile queues and Redis projections, not Nova lifecycle authority.
>
> **Implementation:** The [host observer](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f50e90cd19501dcbf422423310a8f1fe7f3ca9c8/skills/common/plugins/openclaw-agent-observer/src/index.ts), [queue, retry, and dead-letter writer](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f50e90cd19501dcbf422423310a8f1fe7f3ca9c8/skills/common/plugins/openclaw-agent-observer/src/redis-writer.ts), and [ingress constants](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f50e90cd19501dcbf422423310a8f1fe7f3ca9c8/contracts/agent-observability/v1/src/constants.ts) define this separate producer path.
>
> **Contract or setting:** Queue/event bounds, control retries, dead-letter attempts and approximate stream trimming constrain delivery.
>
> **Test evidence:** No fresh host-hook-to-Redis or downstream-consumer exercise ran for this source summary.
>
> **Revision:** `f50e90cd19501dcbf422423310a8f1fe7f3ca9c8`. Source bindings, not execution receipts.
>
> **Limit:** Process loss or exhausted delivery can lose projections; retries do not establish exactly-once delivery.
>

**Why this design exists:** Recovery needs one answer for each fact.
A cache or transport copy can disappear without changing the fact's owner.

**Cost:** Each handoff needs explicit identities and duplicate checks.
The system stops when it cannot prove that two copies describe the same fact.

**Rejected alternative:** A shared database or message bus does not become one
universal authority merely because several components can read it.

> **Source evidence — retained authority across boundaries**
>
> **Claim:** Each handoff preserves its canonical owner and verifies retained identity before continued work.
>
> **Implementation:** Snapshot, effect, remote import and native seal paths below define those retained boundaries.
>
>
> [Nova writes graph and registry snapshots before execution](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/13bff0a18a64e74f2cbbaa1978e746fcdeff0c10/skills/nova/core/execution/engine-run.ts#L36-L43).
>
> [The effect path records a request before invocation and records the returned receipt](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/13bff0a18a64e74f2cbbaa1978e746fcdeff0c10/skills/nova/core/effects/durable-invocation.ts#L88-L117).
>
> [Nova verifies a terminal Buster result and its evidence before import](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/13bff0a18a64e74f2cbbaa1978e746fcdeff0c10/skills/nova/core/test-gates/remote-result-import.ts#L213-L247).
>
> [Worker Core writes admission before launch and seals the result before delivery](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/13bff0a18a64e74f2cbbaa1978e746fcdeff0c10/skills/worker/core/worker/native-attempt-executor.ts#L20-L60).
>
> **Limit:** These source paths prove ordering and validation in the inspected implementation. They do not prove storage durability or service availability in a live environment.
>
> **Contract or setting:** Original graph/request/result/claim identities govern reuse; a similar replacement is not the same operation.
>
> **Test evidence:** No fresh cross-service recovery or target-volume durability exercise is established here.
>
> **Revision:** `13bff0a18a64e74f2cbbaa1978e746fcdeff0c10`. Source bindings, not execution receipts.

### LiteLLM row retention

The [checked-in gateway YAML selects no row-retention policy](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/my-values/infra/litellm-config.yaml#L1-L14).
Both selected LiteLLM revisions can schedule deletion of old request-cost
records (spend logs), request-routing sessions (autorouter sessions), and
health-check records when their effective retention settings enable cleanup.
[Direct scheduling](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L9588-L9629)
and [GitOps scheduling](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L10008-L10049)
are conditional. Database-stored settings can change and reschedule this job;
see [direct setting application](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L6805-L6825)
and [GitOps setting application](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L7162-L7182).
The cleanup implementation [deletes aged rows in bounded batches](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/db/db_transaction_queue/spend_log_cleanup.py#L308-L336)
from [these record tables](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/db/db_transaction_queue/spend_log_cleanup.py#L456-L505).

Before assuming indefinite retention, identify the mounted configuration and
database-stored values of `maximum_spend_logs_retention_period`,
`maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period`, and
`maximum_health_check_retention_period`. Cleanup can remove aged diagnostic or
accounting rows before a later backup. A retained earlier dump can still contain
those rows. Preserve the dumps and determine the effective policy before treating
this difference as corruption. These settings do not define a common expiry for
models, keys, or budgets, and do not delete retained backup groups.

#### Read retention inputs without changing the service

This procedure applies to the two [selected LiteLLM revisions](#selected-litellm-source-and-image-boundary).
Run it from the bound independent administration machine. It reads one running
LiteLLM Pod and its database; it does not change retention or start cleanup.
Use `kubectl`, Python 3 with PyYAML in the selected container, and `psql` on the
administration machine. Do not install tools into the running container.

Before starting, the LiteLLM and database owners must identify the deployed
profile, immutable image, upstream revision, database service and database
name, applied schema-change history, and the exact Pod/container. They must
supply an authorized read-only database connection profile privately. It must
select that instance and a role with only the necessary read access. Use a
libpq service file and password file through their private paths; never put a
credential URL or password in a command, record, or shell trace. Cluster access
must permit reading the selected Pod and executing this file-read command.
The owners must confirm that the deployed `LiteLLM_Config` table is in `public`,
with `param_name` as its unique text key and `param_value` as JSON or JSONB.
The [direct schema](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/schema.prisma#L618-L623)
and [GitOps schema](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/schema.prisma#L621-L626)
describe the selected schema, but do not prove that live migrations completed.
Stop if this instance, schema, read-only access, or tool selection is unverified.

1. Bind the cluster as specified in [Bind Cluster Authority](../use/install.md#bind-cluster-authority).
   Set `LITELLM_POD` to the owner's exact running Pod name and
   `LITELLM_POD_UID` to its recorded UID. Keep its non-secret owner/image/mount
   record with the observation time. Both repository profiles mount
   `/app/config.yaml`; confirm that this is the selected container's actual
   configuration file. The [direct mount](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/my-values/infra/litellm-deployment.yaml#L60-L74)
   and [GitOps mount](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/gitops/platform/litellm/resources.yaml#L40-L50)
   use `subPath`. A ConfigMap alone is insufficient: the `subPath` mount
   can keep older bytes after a ConfigMap change.

```bash
assert_cluster_binding || exit 126
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
test "$(kubectl --context "$EXPECTED_CONTEXT" -n "$NAMESPACE" get pod \
  "$LITELLM_POD" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}')" = "$LITELLM_POD_UID"
kubectl --context "$EXPECTED_CONTEXT" -n "$NAMESPACE" exec -i \
  "$LITELLM_POD" -c litellm -- python - <<'PY'
try:
    import hashlib, json, re, yaml
    raw = open('/app/config.yaml', 'rb').read()
    config = yaml.safe_load(raw)
    if not isinstance(config, dict):
        raise ValueError()
    g = config.get('general_settings', {})
    if not isinstance(g, dict):
        raise ValueError()
    keys = ('maximum_spend_logs_retention_period',
            'maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period',
            'maximum_health_check_retention_period')
    def safe(v):
        if v is None or type(v) is int:
            return v
        if type(v) is str and re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]+(s|m|h|d|w|mo)', v):
            return v
        return {'uninterpreted_type': type(v).__name__, 'value_withheld': True}
    print(json.dumps({'mounted_file_sha256': hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
        'settings': {k: {'present': k in g, 'value': safe(g.get(k))} for k in keys}}))
except Exception:
    raise SystemExit('LITELLM_RETENTION_CONFIG_READ_FAILED') from None
PY
```

Expected result: one mounted-file digest and exactly three setting records.
`present: false` differs from an explicit YAML null. The output withholds
unexpected values instead of exposing arbitrary configuration strings.
A missing Pod, changed UID, file-read failure, unavailable Python/PyYAML, or
unexpected value stops this identification. File-read, import, parse, and
mapping-shape failures return nonzero with only
`LITELLM_RETENTION_CONFIG_READ_FAILED`; raw YAML, exception text and tracebacks
are withheld. An empty/null document or a nonmapping `general_settings` is
rejected. Keep this constant failure record and ask the owner to diagnose the
configuration privately. Obtain a versioned owner procedure
that exports only these fields and the exact mounted-file identity if this
read command is unavailable. Do not dump the configuration or environment.

2. In a dedicated query shell, set `PGSERVICE`, `PGSERVICEFILE`, and
   `PGPASSFILE` to the owner's read-only service name and absolute private
   service-file and password-file paths. Ordinary shell assignments are not
   inherited by `psql`; the command block below explicitly exports them.
   The owner must confirm that this service name exists in that exact file,
   selects the verified source host/address, port, database and read-only user,
   and contains the approved transport and authentication settings. The files
   must be privately owned and readable; the password file must deny group and
   other access. The service section must contain neither a `password` nor a
   `passfile` setting for this password-file procedure. Do not print file
   contents or selector values.

   A [service-file field](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/libpq-pgservice.html)
   overrides its corresponding environment value. A field omitted from the
   service can still use an inherited variable or a built-in default. A direct
   connection argument overrides the service. Therefore the block rejects
   every other `PG*` shell input and supplies no host, user, database, password
   or connection-string argument. In particular, inherited `PGPASSWORD` can
   supply a password before the [password file](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/libpq-pgpass.html)
   is considered. Reject it instead of silently using it. The selected service
   must define all target identity and required security fields; owners must
   approve any deliberately omitted default. Selector export and a clean
   environment do not by themselves prove which server accepted a connection.

   If the guard rejects an inherited input, stop and ask the owner for a clean
   query shell with the same approved files. Do not dump the environment,
   inspect secrets, or remove an input to guess a connection. Run this exact
   projection only after the live schema and instance checks above:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
for pg_input in ${!PG@}; do
  case "$pg_input" in
    PGSERVICE|PGSERVICEFILE|PGPASSFILE) ;;
    *) printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_INPUT_REJECTED' >&2; exit 126 ;;
  esac
done
if test -z "${PGSERVICE-}" || test -z "${PGSERVICEFILE-}" || test -z "${PGPASSFILE-}"; then
  printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_INPUT_MISSING' >&2
  exit 126
fi
for profile_path in "$PGSERVICEFILE" "$PGPASSFILE"; do
  case "$profile_path" in
    /*) ;;
    *) printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_PATH_INVALID' >&2; exit 126 ;;
  esac

    printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_FILE_UNAVAILABLE' >&2
    exit 126
  fi
done
export PGSERVICE PGSERVICEFILE PGPASSFILE
psql --no-psqlrc --set=ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY;
SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5s';
SHOW transaction_read_only;

 ('maximum_spend_logs_retention_period'),
 ('maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period'),
 ('maximum_health_check_retention_period')),
settings AS (

 WHERE param_name = 'general_settings'

SELECT keys.key, settings.value IS NOT NULL AS record_has_value,
       jsonb_typeof(settings.value) AS record_type,
       COALESCE(settings.value ? keys.key, false) AS key_present,
       jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) AS value_type,
       CASE
         WHEN jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) = 'null' THEN 'null'
         WHEN jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) = 'number'
           AND (settings.value ->> keys.key) ~ '^-?[0-9]+$'
           THEN settings.value ->> keys.key
         WHEN jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) = 'string'
           AND (settings.value ->> keys.key) ~ '^[0-9]+(s|m|h|d|w|mo)$'

Expected result: `transaction_read_only` is `on`, three rows and `ROLLBACK`.
`record_type` must be `object` or null; stop for any other record shape.
The query reads only the three retention fields from the `general_settings`
record. A missing record, SQL null record, absent key and JSON null key are
not an enabled policy. An unexpected type or withheld value needs owner
interpretation against the selected parser. Do not broaden the query to whole
records, Secrets, provider credentials, or key tables. On connection, schema,
permission, timeout, or shape failure, stop; preserve the safe error and obtain
the database owner's corrected read-only procedure. Do not try a write-capable
profile or run a migration.

3. Compare the mounted and stored observations with these rules.

| Input or observation | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Key absent from initial mounted settings and not applied from the database | No retention period for that record type; deletion is disabled. There is no built-in number of retention days for these three keys. |
| Database key present and applied by the selected process | It overwrites the loaded value even when YAML also supplied that key. A changed value, including null, reschedules cleanup. |
| Database key absent | The setter does not assign that key. It does not prove that the process has forgotten an earlier stored value or now equals the mounted file. |
| Applied null, or a string that raises `ValueError` in the retention parser | The corresponding deletion path is disabled. Other unexpected types can fail parsing; do not call them a safe disabled policy without owner investigation. |
| Integer | The retention parser treats it as days. Use an explicit string such as `7d` when the owner later changes policy. |
| Explicit duration string | `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, `w`, and `mo` mean seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, and calendar months. Zero can parse; do not assume zero disables deletion. Calendar-month seconds depend on parsing time. |

Spend retention applies to `LiteLLM_SpendLogs.startTime` and its derived
`LiteLLM_SpendLogToolIndex.start_time` rows. Autorouter retention applies to
`LiteLLM_AutoRouterSession.last_turn_at`; health retention applies to
`LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable.checked_at`. Each uses its own cutoff. These are
current-database deletions, not changes to previously published backup groups.

The authenticated admin-view `GET /config/field/info?field_name=<key>` reads
stored settings and can fail for an absent field. It is not a loaded-value
read. `GET /config/list?config_type=general_settings` reports loaded settings
but falls back to the database when the loaded value is `None`.
Its `stored_in_db` flag describes presence, not proof of successful application.
Use the owner's private authenticated administration surface for these GETs;
retain only these three fields, not the full response. Neither endpoint is an
unconditional observation of the cleanup task in every running worker.

**Effective runtime policy can remain unknown.** The mounted-file and SQL
results prove inputs at their recorded times. They do not prove that each worker
loaded the same inputs, that a database change was applied, that a scheduler
ran, or that deletion succeeded. To claim an effective policy, the LiteLLM owner
must supply a versioned read-only observation procedure bound to each relevant
Pod/process and observation time. It must identify the loaded values, their
parsed seconds or disabled/error result, the scheduled cleanup state, and any
change between the input reads. Stop at this boundary if that observation is
unavailable or conflicts with the inputs. Keep both dumps and mark the effective
policy `unknown`; do not restart, change retention, or delete rows to make the
observations agree.

## Prepare a Redis RDB as a fresh AOF dataset

The supported repository primitive is **offline RDB-to-AOF preparation**, not
an arbitrary AOF restore or an automatic cluster cutover. Its input is one
checksum-bound RDB from a fenced source; its output is a new private local
directory for the selected Redis version. Keep the original release, volume,
source snapshot, independent password authority and consumer configuration.
Do not run this tool against the only retained copy or a destination in use.

Before capture, the Redis owner must inventory and stop publishers, schedulers
and reconciliation that could restart them. Preserve streams, consumer groups,
pending deliveries and absolute dedup expiries. Obtain the RDB with the selected
authenticated snapshot transport while source writes remain fenced. The existing
migration procedure uses `CLIENT PAUSE 600000 WRITE`, a bounded 240-second
`redis-cli --rdb` capture, then stops the source within that pause window.
A pause alone is temporary, not an enduring fence. If the owner cannot prove
that no newer source writes occurred, discard the candidate for cutover and
repeat capture after restoring the fence. Retain the RDB/checksum outside the
source-volume failure domain. An old source PVC is not proof of the latest state.

For the **offline step**, use a Linux maintenance host with Bash, Node.js and
locked repository dependencies (`js-yaml`), coreutils, `setsid`, `timeout`, and
the actual native `redis-server`, `redis-cli` and `redis-check-rdb` binaries.
`versions.json` selects the destination server version; a different server
version fails admission. Supply these private, explicitly selected paths:

```bash
set -eu
export REDIS_SERVER=/absolute/selected/redis-server
export REDIS_CLI=/absolute/selected/redis-cli
export REDIS_CHECK_RDB=/absolute/selected/redis-check-rdb
# Set SNAPSHOT to the retained absolute RDB path and RDB_SHA256 to its recorded hash.
# NEW_DATA_DIRECTORY must be an absolute canonical path that does not yet exist.
bash scripts/redis-prepare-migration.sh "$SNAPSHOT" "$RDB_SHA256" "$NEW_DATA_DIRECTORY"
(cd "$NEW_DATA_DIRECTORY" && sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS)
```

The tool verifies the snapshot checksum, size and RDB format before creating the
new directory. It loads RDB with AOF disabled on loopback using a random temporary
password, enables AOF, waits for rewrite, persists configuration, then shuts down.
It removes the loaded RDB from the destination and verifies a second startup
from AOF, `appendfsync always` and `noeviction`, followed by clean shutdown.
The input RDB remains unchanged. `REDIS_MIGRATION_MAXIMUM_SECONDS` defaults to
600. Each server start gets a fresh timeout; polling also checks a shared
deadline. This is not a whole-command deadline. Snapshot hashing, RDB checking,
copying, final hashing and synchronization run outside that server timeout.
`REDIS_MIGRATION_MAXIMUM_BYTES` defaults to 21,474,836,480. It bounds input size,
the server's individual file-growth limit and a final aggregate destination check.
It does not cap total temporary disk use during conversion. Reserve headroom
for source, destination, rewrite and temporary files. If the maintenance window
requires a total deadline or capacity ceiling, the owner must supply an
independently bounded procedure and preserve interrupted-state evidence.

Success prints the new directory and produces `migration-receipt.txt` with
`state=aof-restart-verified` and `cutover=not-performed`, plus `SHA256SUMS` for
AOF files and the receipt. Preserve the initial output and verify checksums.
Existing destination, invalid/mismatched checksum, wrong selected version,
invalid RDB, deadline, size, rewrite or restart failure is a stop condition.
An interrupted directory remains visibly incomplete; the tool refuses to
silently overwrite or resume it. Preserve it for diagnosis and choose a fresh
absent destination only after resolving the failure. No source credentials,
Kubernetes mutation or client switch belong to this offline command.

The Redis owner must separately provision and isolate a compatible target,
copy and verify the full AOF manifest/files into a fresh correctly owned volume,
retain the external password authority, and verify the selected server version,
streams/groups/pending state, original absolute dedup expiries, lost-ACK replay
without an extra entry, and a target restart. Render client endpoints and
network policies for the selected release before opening access. Switch clients
last with the old source fenced. Before new target writes, a compatible restore
of the retained snapshot may support rollback; after new writes it is stale.
Fence and capture the new authoritative dataset or fix forward instead of
starting both writers or downgrading AOF in place. A copied directory, checksum
or offline receipt proves neither Kubernetes/CSI durability nor a complete
live restore. Stop before cluster install/cutover without the owners' bound
provisioning, security, verification and rollback procedure.

Before assuming indefinite retention, identify the mounted configuration and
database-stored values of `maximum_spend_logs_retention_period`,
`maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period`, and
`maximum_health_check_retention_period`. Cleanup can remove aged diagnostic or
accounting rows before a later backup. A retained earlier dump can still contain
those rows. Preserve the dumps and determine the effective policy before treating
this difference as corruption. These settings do not define a common expiry for
models, keys, or budgets, and do not delete retained backup groups.

#### Read retention inputs without changing the service

This procedure applies to the two [selected LiteLLM revisions](#selected-litellm-source-and-image-boundary).
Run it from the bound independent administration machine. It reads one running
LiteLLM Pod and its database; it does not change retention or start cleanup.
Use `kubectl`, Python 3 with PyYAML in the selected container, and `psql` on the
administration machine. Do not install tools into the running container.

Before starting, the LiteLLM and database owners must identify the deployed
profile, immutable image, upstream revision, database service and database
name, applied schema-change history, and the exact Pod/container. They must
supply an authorized read-only database connection profile privately. It must
select that instance and a role with only the necessary read access. Use a
libpq service file and password file through their private paths; never put a
credential URL or password in a command, record, or shell trace. Cluster access
must permit reading the selected Pod and executing this file-read command.
The owners must confirm that the deployed `LiteLLM_Config` table is in `public`,
with `param_name` as its unique text key and `param_value` as JSON or JSONB.
The [direct schema](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/schema.prisma#L618-L623)
and [GitOps schema](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/schema.prisma#L621-L626)
describe the selected schema, but do not prove that live migrations completed.

   and [GitOps mount](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/gitops/platform/litellm/resources.yaml#L40-L50)
   use `subPath`. A ConfigMap alone is insufficient: the `subPath` mount

| Integer | The retention parser treats it as days. Use an explicit string such as `7d` when the owner later changes policy. |
| Explicit duration string | `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, `w`, and `mo` mean seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, and calendar months. Zero can parse; do not assume zero disables deletion. Calendar-month seconds depend on parsing time. |

Spend retention applies to `LiteLLM_SpendLogs.startTime` and its derived
`LiteLLM_SpendLogToolIndex.start_time` rows. Autorouter retention applies to
`LiteLLM_AutoRouterSession.last_turn_at`; health retention applies to
`LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable.checked_at`. Each uses its own cutoff. These are
current-database deletions, not changes to previously published backup groups.

The authenticated admin-view `GET /config/field/info?field_name=<key>` reads
stored settings and can fail for an absent field. It is not a loaded-value
read. `GET /config/list?config_type=general_settings` reports loaded settings
but falls back to the database when the loaded value is `None`.
Its `stored_in_db` flag describes presence, not proof of successful application.
Use the owner's private authenticated administration surface for these GETs;
retain only these three fields, not the full response. Neither endpoint is an
unconditional observation of the cleanup task in every running worker.

**Effective runtime policy can remain unknown.** The mounted-file and SQL
results prove inputs at their recorded times. They do not prove that each worker
loaded the same inputs, that a database change was applied, that a scheduler
ran, or that deletion succeeded. To claim an effective policy, the LiteLLM owner
must supply a versioned read-only observation procedure bound to each relevant
Pod/process and observation time. It must identify the loaded values, their
parsed seconds or disabled/error result, the scheduled cleanup state, and any
change between the input reads. Stop at this boundary if that observation is
unavailable or conflicts with the inputs. Keep both dumps and mark the effective
policy `unknown`; do not restart, change retention, or delete rows to make the
observations agree.

## Prepare a Redis RDB as a fresh AOF dataset

The supported repository primitive is **offline RDB-to-AOF preparation**, not
an arbitrary AOF restore or an automatic cluster cutover. Its input is one
checksum-bound RDB from a fenced source; its output is a new private local
directory for the selected Redis version. Keep the original release, volume,
source snapshot, independent password authority and consumer configuration.
Do not run this tool against the only retained copy or a destination in use.

Before capture, the Redis owner must inventory and stop publishers, schedulers
and reconciliation that could restart them. Preserve streams, consumer groups,
pending deliveries and absolute dedup expiries. Obtain the RDB with the selected
authenticated snapshot transport while source writes remain fenced. The existing
migration procedure uses `CLIENT PAUSE 600000 WRITE`, a bounded 240-second
`redis-cli --rdb` capture, then stops the source within that pause window.
A pause alone is temporary, not an enduring fence. If the owner cannot prove
that no newer source writes occurred, discard the candidate for cutover and
repeat capture after restoring the fence. Retain the RDB/checksum outside the
source-volume failure domain. An old source PVC is not proof of the latest state.

For the **offline step**, use a Linux maintenance host with Bash, Node.js and
locked repository dependencies (`js-yaml`), coreutils, `setsid`, `timeout`, and
the actual native `redis-server`, `redis-cli` and `redis-check-rdb` binaries.
`versions.json` selects the destination server version; a different server
version fails admission. Supply these private, explicitly selected paths:

```bash
set -eu
export REDIS_SERVER=/absolute/selected/redis-server
export REDIS_CLI=/absolute/selected/redis-cli
export REDIS_CHECK_RDB=/absolute/selected/redis-check-rdb
# Set SNAPSHOT to the retained absolute RDB path and RDB_SHA256 to its recorded hash.
# NEW_DATA_DIRECTORY must be an absolute canonical path that does not yet exist.
bash scripts/redis-prepare-migration.sh "$SNAPSHOT" "$RDB_SHA256" "$NEW_DATA_DIRECTORY"
(cd "$NEW_DATA_DIRECTORY" && sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS)
```

The tool verifies the snapshot checksum, size and RDB format before creating the
new directory. It loads RDB with AOF disabled on loopback using a random temporary
password, enables AOF, waits for rewrite, persists configuration, then shuts down.
It removes the loaded RDB from the destination and verifies a second startup
from AOF, `appendfsync always` and `noeviction`, followed by clean shutdown.
The input RDB remains unchanged. `REDIS_MIGRATION_MAXIMUM_SECONDS` defaults to
600. Each server start gets a fresh timeout; polling also checks a shared
deadline. This is not a whole-command deadline. Snapshot hashing, RDB checking,
copying, final hashing and synchronization run outside that server timeout.
`REDIS_MIGRATION_MAXIMUM_BYTES` defaults to 21,474,836,480. It bounds input size,
the server's individual file-growth limit and a final aggregate destination check.
It does not cap total temporary disk use during conversion. Reserve headroom
for source, destination, rewrite and temporary files. If the maintenance window
requires a total deadline or capacity ceiling, the owner must supply an
independently bounded procedure and preserve interrupted-state evidence.

Success prints the new directory and produces `migration-receipt.txt` with
`state=aof-restart-verified` and `cutover=not-performed`, plus `SHA256SUMS` for
AOF files and the receipt. Preserve the initial output and verify checksums.
Existing destination, invalid/mismatched checksum, wrong selected version,
invalid RDB, deadline, size, rewrite or restart failure is a stop condition.
An interrupted directory remains visibly incomplete; the tool refuses to
silently overwrite or resume it. Preserve it for diagnosis and choose a fresh
absent destination only after resolving the failure. No source credentials,
Kubernetes mutation or client switch belong to this offline command.

The Redis owner must separately provision and isolate a compatible target,
copy and verify the full AOF manifest/files into a fresh correctly owned volume,
retain the external password authority, and verify the selected server version,
streams/groups/pending state, original absolute dedup expiries, lost-ACK replay
without an extra entry, and a target restart. Render client endpoints and
network policies for the selected release before opening access. Switch clients
last with the old source fenced. Before new target writes, a compatible restore
of the retained snapshot may support rollback; after new writes it is stale.
Fence and capture the new authoritative dataset or fix forward instead of
starting both writers or downgrading AOF in place. A copied directory, checksum
or offline receipt proves neither Kubernetes/CSI durability nor a complete
live restore. Stop before cluster install/cutover without the owners' bound
provisioning, security, verification and rollback procedure.

### LiteLLM row retention

The [checked-in gateway YAML selects no row-retention policy](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/my-values/infra/litellm-config.yaml#L1-L14).
Both selected LiteLLM revisions can schedule deletion of old request-cost
records (spend logs), request-routing sessions (autorouter sessions), and
health-check records when their effective retention settings enable cleanup.
[Direct scheduling](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L9588-L9629)
and [GitOps scheduling](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L10008-L10049)
are conditional. Database-stored settings can change and reschedule this job;
see [direct setting application](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L6805-L6825)
and [GitOps setting application](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L7162-L7182).
The cleanup implementation [deletes aged rows in bounded batches](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/db/db_transaction_queue/spend_log_cleanup.py#L308-L336)
from [these record tables](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/db/db_transaction_queue/spend_log_cleanup.py#L456-L505).

Before assuming indefinite retention, identify the mounted configuration and
database-stored values of `maximum_spend_logs_retention_period`,
`maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period`, and
`maximum_health_check_retention_period`. Cleanup can remove aged diagnostic or
accounting rows before a later backup. A retained earlier dump can still contain
those rows. Preserve the dumps and determine the effective policy before treating
this difference as corruption. These settings do not define a common expiry for
models, keys, or budgets, and do not delete retained backup groups.

#### Read retention inputs without changing the service

This procedure applies to the two [selected LiteLLM revisions](#selected-litellm-source-and-image-boundary).
Run it from the bound independent administration machine. It reads one running
LiteLLM Pod and its database; it does not change retention or start cleanup.
Use `kubectl`, Python 3 with PyYAML in the selected container, and `psql` on the
administration machine. Do not install tools into the running container.

Before starting, the LiteLLM and database owners must identify the deployed
profile, immutable image, upstream revision, database service and database
name, applied schema-change history, and the exact Pod/container. They must
supply an authorized read-only database connection profile privately. It must
select that instance and a role with only the necessary read access. Use a
libpq service file and password file through their private paths; never put a
credential URL or password in a command, record, or shell trace. Cluster access
must permit reading the selected Pod and executing this file-read command.
The owners must confirm that the deployed `LiteLLM_Config` table is in `public`,
with `param_name` as its unique text key and `param_value` as JSON or JSONB.
The [direct schema](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/schema.prisma#L618-L623)
and [GitOps schema](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/schema.prisma#L621-L626)
describe the selected schema, but do not prove that live migrations completed.
Stop if this instance, schema, read-only access, or tool selection is unverified.

1. Bind the cluster as specified in [Bind Cluster Authority](../use/install.md#bind-cluster-authority).
   Set `LITELLM_POD` to the owner's exact running Pod name and
   `LITELLM_POD_UID` to its recorded UID. Keep its non-secret owner/image/mount
   record with the observation time. Both repository profiles mount
   `/app/config.yaml`; confirm that this is the selected container's actual
   configuration file. The [direct mount](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/my-values/infra/litellm-deployment.yaml#L60-L74)
   and [GitOps mount](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/gitops/platform/litellm/resources.yaml#L40-L50)
   use `subPath`. A ConfigMap alone is insufficient: the `subPath` mount
   can keep older bytes after a ConfigMap change.

```bash
assert_cluster_binding || exit 126
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
test "$(kubectl --context "$EXPECTED_CONTEXT" -n "$NAMESPACE" get pod \
  "$LITELLM_POD" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}')" = "$LITELLM_POD_UID"
kubectl --context "$EXPECTED_CONTEXT" -n "$NAMESPACE" exec -i \
  "$LITELLM_POD" -c litellm -- python - <<'PY'
try:
    import hashlib, json, re, yaml
    raw = open('/app/config.yaml', 'rb').read()
    config = yaml.safe_load(raw)
    if not isinstance(config, dict):
        raise ValueError()
    g = config.get('general_settings', {})
    if not isinstance(g, dict):
        raise ValueError()
    keys = ('maximum_spend_logs_retention_period',
            'maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period',
            'maximum_health_check_retention_period')
    def safe(v):
        if v is None or type(v) is int:
            return v
        if type(v) is str and re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]+(s|m|h|d|w|mo)', v):
            return v
        return {'uninterpreted_type': type(v).__name__, 'value_withheld': True}
    print(json.dumps({'mounted_file_sha256': hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
        'settings': {k: {'present': k in g, 'value': safe(g.get(k))} for k in keys}}))
except Exception:
    raise SystemExit('LITELLM_RETENTION_CONFIG_READ_FAILED') from None
PY
```

Expected result: one mounted-file digest and exactly three setting records.
`present: false` differs from an explicit YAML null. The output withholds
unexpected values instead of exposing arbitrary configuration strings.
A missing Pod, changed UID, file-read failure, unavailable Python/PyYAML, or
unexpected value stops this identification. File-read, import, parse, and
mapping-shape failures return nonzero with only
`LITELLM_RETENTION_CONFIG_READ_FAILED`; raw YAML, exception text and tracebacks
are withheld. An empty/null document or a nonmapping `general_settings` is
rejected. Keep this constant failure record and ask the owner to diagnose the
configuration privately. Obtain a versioned owner procedure
that exports only these fields and the exact mounted-file identity if this
read command is unavailable. Do not dump the configuration or environment.

   service-file and password-file paths. Ordinary shell assignments are not
   inherited by `psql`; the command block below explicitly exports them.
   The owner must confirm that this service name exists in that exact file,
   selects the verified source host/address, port, database and read-only user,
   and contains the approved transport and authentication settings. The files
   must be privately owned and readable; the password file must deny group and
   other access. The service section must contain neither a `password` nor a
   `passfile` setting for this password-file procedure. Do not print file
   contents or selector values.

   A [service-file field](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/libpq-pgservice.html)
   overrides its corresponding environment value. A field omitted from the
   service can still use an inherited variable or a built-in default. A direct
   connection argument overrides the service. Therefore the block rejects
   every other `PG*` shell input and supplies no host, user, database, password
   or connection-string argument. In particular, inherited `PGPASSWORD` can
   supply a password before the [password file](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/libpq-pgpass.html)
   is considered. Reject it instead of silently using it. The selected service
   must define all target identity and required security fields; owners must
   approve any deliberately omitted default. Selector export and a clean
   environment do not by themselves prove which server accepted a connection.

   If the guard rejects an inherited input, stop and ask the owner for a clean
   query shell with the same approved files. Do not dump the environment,
   inspect secrets, or remove an input to guess a connection. Run this exact
   projection only after the live schema and instance checks above:

umask 077
for pg_input in ${!PG@}; do
  case "$pg_input" in
    PGSERVICE|PGSERVICEFILE|PGPASSFILE) ;;
    *) printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_INPUT_REJECTED' >&2; exit 126 ;;
  esac
done
if test -z "${PGSERVICE-}" || test -z "${PGSERVICEFILE-}" || test -z "${PGPASSFILE-}"; then
  printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_INPUT_MISSING' >&2
  exit 126
fi
for profile_path in "$PGSERVICEFILE" "$PGPASSFILE"; do
  case "$profile_path" in
    /*) ;;
    *) printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_PATH_INVALID' >&2; exit 126 ;;
  esac

    printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_FILE_UNAVAILABLE' >&2
    exit 126

done

psql --no-psqlrc --set=ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY;
SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5s';
SHOW transaction_read_only;
WITH keys(key) AS (VALUES

 ('maximum_health_check_retention_period')),
settings AS (

       COALESCE(settings.value ? keys.key, false) AS key_present,
       jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) AS value_type,

         WHEN jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) = 'number'

           AND (settings.value ->> keys.key) ~ '^[0-9]+(s|m|h|d|w|mo)$'
           THEN settings.value ->> keys.key
         ELSE '[absent or withheld]'
       END AS retention_value
FROM keys LEFT JOIN settings ON true ORDER BY keys.key;
ROLLBACK;
SQL

## Prepare a Redis RDB as a fresh AOF dataset

The supported repository primitive is **offline RDB-to-AOF preparation**, not
an arbitrary AOF restore or an automatic cluster cutover. Its input is one
checksum-bound RDB from a fenced source; its output is a new private local
directory for the selected Redis version. Keep the original release, volume,
source snapshot, independent password authority and consumer configuration.
Do not run this tool against the only retained copy or a destination in use.

Before capture, the Redis owner must inventory and stop publishers, schedulers
and reconciliation that could restart them. Preserve streams, consumer groups,
pending deliveries and absolute dedup expiries. Obtain the RDB with the selected
authenticated snapshot transport while source writes remain fenced. The existing
migration procedure uses `CLIENT PAUSE 600000 WRITE`, a bounded 240-second
`redis-cli --rdb` capture, then stops the source within that pause window.
A pause alone is temporary, not an enduring fence. If the owner cannot prove
that no newer source writes occurred, discard the candidate for cutover and
repeat capture after restoring the fence. Retain the RDB/checksum outside the
source-volume failure domain. An old source PVC is not proof of the latest state.

For the **offline step**, use a Linux maintenance host with Bash, Node.js and
locked repository dependencies (`js-yaml`), coreutils, `setsid`, `timeout`, and
the actual native `redis-server`, `redis-cli` and `redis-check-rdb` binaries.
`versions.json` selects the destination server version; a different server
version fails admission. Supply these private, explicitly selected paths:

```bash
set -eu
export REDIS_SERVER=/absolute/selected/redis-server
export REDIS_CLI=/absolute/selected/redis-cli
export REDIS_CHECK_RDB=/absolute/selected/redis-check-rdb
# Set SNAPSHOT to the retained absolute RDB path and RDB_SHA256 to its recorded hash.
# NEW_DATA_DIRECTORY must be an absolute canonical path that does not yet exist.
bash scripts/redis-prepare-migration.sh "$SNAPSHOT" "$RDB_SHA256" "$NEW_DATA_DIRECTORY"
(cd "$NEW_DATA_DIRECTORY" && sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS)
```

The tool verifies the snapshot checksum, size and RDB format before creating the
new directory. It loads RDB with AOF disabled on loopback using a random temporary
password, enables AOF, waits for rewrite, persists configuration, then shuts down.
It removes the loaded RDB from the destination and verifies a second startup
from AOF, `appendfsync always` and `noeviction`, followed by clean shutdown.
The input RDB remains unchanged. `REDIS_MIGRATION_MAXIMUM_SECONDS` defaults to
600. Each server start gets a fresh timeout; polling also checks a shared
deadline. This is not a whole-command deadline. Snapshot hashing, RDB checking,
copying, final hashing and synchronization run outside that server timeout.
`REDIS_MIGRATION_MAXIMUM_BYTES` defaults to 21,474,836,480. It bounds input size,
the server's individual file-growth limit and a final aggregate destination check.
It does not cap total temporary disk use during conversion. Reserve headroom
for source, destination, rewrite and temporary files. If the maintenance window
requires a total deadline or capacity ceiling, the owner must supply an
independently bounded procedure and preserve interrupted-state evidence.

Success prints the new directory and produces `migration-receipt.txt` with
`state=aof-restart-verified` and `cutover=not-performed`, plus `SHA256SUMS` for
AOF files and the receipt. Preserve the initial output and verify checksums.
Existing destination, invalid/mismatched checksum, wrong selected version,
invalid RDB, deadline, size, rewrite or restart failure is a stop condition.
An interrupted directory remains visibly incomplete; the tool refuses to
silently overwrite or resume it. Preserve it for diagnosis and choose a fresh
absent destination only after resolving the failure. No source credentials,
Kubernetes mutation or client switch belong to this offline command.

The Redis owner must separately provision and isolate a compatible target,
copy and verify the full AOF manifest/files into a fresh correctly owned volume,
retain the external password authority, and verify the selected server version,
streams/groups/pending state, original absolute dedup expiries, lost-ACK replay
without an extra entry, and a target restart. Render client endpoints and
network policies for the selected release before opening access. Switch clients
last with the old source fenced. Before new target writes, a compatible restore
of the retained snapshot may support rollback; after new writes it is stale.
Fence and capture the new authoritative dataset or fix forward instead of
starting both writers or downgrading AOF in place. A copied directory, checksum
or offline receipt proves neither Kubernetes/CSI durability nor a complete
live restore. Stop before cluster install/cutover without the owners' bound
provisioning, security, verification and rollback procedure.

### LiteLLM row retention

The [checked-in gateway YAML selects no row-retention policy](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/my-values/infra/litellm-config.yaml#L1-L14).
Both selected LiteLLM revisions can schedule deletion of old request-cost
records (spend logs), request-routing sessions (autorouter sessions), and
health-check records when their effective retention settings enable cleanup.
[Direct scheduling](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L9588-L9629)
and [GitOps scheduling](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L10008-L10049)
are conditional. Database-stored settings can change and reschedule this job;
see [direct setting application](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L6805-L6825)
and [GitOps setting application](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L7162-L7182).
The cleanup implementation [deletes aged rows in bounded batches](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/db/db_transaction_queue/spend_log_cleanup.py#L308-L336)
from [these record tables](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/db/db_transaction_queue/spend_log_cleanup.py#L456-L505).

Before assuming indefinite retention, identify the mounted configuration and
database-stored values of `maximum_spend_logs_retention_period`,
`maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period`, and
`maximum_health_check_retention_period`. Cleanup can remove aged diagnostic or
accounting rows before a later backup. A retained earlier dump can still contain
those rows. Preserve the dumps and determine the effective policy before treating
this difference as corruption. These settings do not define a common expiry for
models, keys, or budgets, and do not delete retained backup groups.

#### Read retention inputs without changing the service

This procedure applies to the two [selected LiteLLM revisions](#selected-litellm-source-and-image-boundary).
Run it from the bound independent administration machine. It reads one running
LiteLLM Pod and its database; it does not change retention or start cleanup.
Use `kubectl`, Python 3 with PyYAML in the selected container, and `psql` on the
administration machine. Do not install tools into the running container.

Before starting, the LiteLLM and database owners must identify the deployed
profile, immutable image, upstream revision, database service and database
name, applied schema-change history, and the exact Pod/container. They must
supply an authorized read-only database connection profile privately. It must
select that instance and a role with only the necessary read access. Use a
libpq service file and password file through their private paths; never put a
credential URL or password in a command, record, or shell trace. Cluster access
must permit reading the selected Pod and executing this file-read command.
The owners must confirm that the deployed `LiteLLM_Config` table is in `public`,
with `param_name` as its unique text key and `param_value` as JSON or JSONB.
The [direct schema](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/schema.prisma#L618-L623)
and [GitOps schema](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/schema.prisma#L621-L626)
describe the selected schema, but do not prove that live migrations completed.
Stop if this instance, schema, read-only access, or tool selection is unverified.

1. Bind the cluster as specified in [Bind Cluster Authority](../use/install.md#bind-cluster-authority).
   Set `LITELLM_POD` to the owner's exact running Pod name and
   `LITELLM_POD_UID` to its recorded UID. Keep its non-secret owner/image/mount
   record with the observation time. Both repository profiles mount
   `/app/config.yaml`; confirm that this is the selected container's actual
   configuration file. The [direct mount](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/my-values/infra/litellm-deployment.yaml#L60-L74)
   and [GitOps mount](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/gitops/platform/litellm/resources.yaml#L40-L50)
   use `subPath`. A ConfigMap alone is insufficient: the `subPath` mount
   can keep older bytes after a ConfigMap change.

```bash
assert_cluster_binding || exit 126
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
test "$(kubectl --context "$EXPECTED_CONTEXT" -n "$NAMESPACE" get pod \
  "$LITELLM_POD" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}')" = "$LITELLM_POD_UID"
kubectl --context "$EXPECTED_CONTEXT" -n "$NAMESPACE" exec -i \
  "$LITELLM_POD" -c litellm -- python - <<'PY'
try:
    import hashlib, json, re, yaml
    raw = open('/app/config.yaml', 'rb').read()
    config = yaml.safe_load(raw)
    if not isinstance(config, dict):
        raise ValueError()
    g = config.get('general_settings', {})
    if not isinstance(g, dict):
        raise ValueError()
    keys = ('maximum_spend_logs_retention_period',
            'maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period',
            'maximum_health_check_retention_period')
    def safe(v):
        if v is None or type(v) is int:
            return v
        if type(v) is str and re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]+(s|m|h|d|w|mo)', v):
            return v
        return {'uninterpreted_type': type(v).__name__, 'value_withheld': True}
    print(json.dumps({'mounted_file_sha256': hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
        'settings': {k: {'present': k in g, 'value': safe(g.get(k))} for k in keys}}))
except Exception:
    raise SystemExit('LITELLM_RETENTION_CONFIG_READ_FAILED') from None
PY
```

Expected result: one mounted-file digest and exactly three setting records.
`present: false` differs from an explicit YAML null. The output withholds
unexpected values instead of exposing arbitrary configuration strings.
A missing Pod, changed UID, file-read failure, unavailable Python/PyYAML, or
unexpected value stops this identification. File-read, import, parse, and
mapping-shape failures return nonzero with only
`LITELLM_RETENTION_CONFIG_READ_FAILED`; raw YAML, exception text and tracebacks
are withheld. An empty/null document or a nonmapping `general_settings` is
rejected. Keep this constant failure record and ask the owner to diagnose the
configuration privately. Obtain a versioned owner procedure
that exports only these fields and the exact mounted-file identity if this
read command is unavailable. Do not dump the configuration or environment.

2. In a dedicated query shell, set `PGSERVICE`, `PGSERVICEFILE`, and
   `PGPASSFILE` to the owner's read-only service name and absolute private
   service-file and password-file paths. Ordinary shell assignments are not
   inherited by `psql`; the command block below explicitly exports them.
   The owner must confirm that this service name exists in that exact file,
   selects the verified source host/address, port, database and read-only user,
   and contains the approved transport and authentication settings. The files
   must be privately owned and readable; the password file must deny group and
   other access. The service section must contain neither a `password` nor a
   `passfile` setting for this password-file procedure. Do not print file
   contents or selector values.

   A [service-file field](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/libpq-pgservice.html)
   overrides its corresponding environment value. A field omitted from the
   service can still use an inherited variable or a built-in default. A direct
   connection argument overrides the service. Therefore the block rejects
   every other `PG*` shell input and supplies no host, user, database, password
   or connection-string argument. In particular, inherited `PGPASSWORD` can
   supply a password before the [password file](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/libpq-pgpass.html)
   is considered. Reject it instead of silently using it. The selected service
   must define all target identity and required security fields; owners must
   approve any deliberately omitted default. Selector export and a clean
   environment do not by themselves prove which server accepted a connection.

   If the guard rejects an inherited input, stop and ask the owner for a clean
   query shell with the same approved files. Do not dump the environment,
   inspect secrets, or remove an input to guess a connection. Run this exact
   projection only after the live schema and instance checks above:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
for pg_input in ${!PG@}; do
  case "$pg_input" in
    PGSERVICE|PGSERVICEFILE|PGPASSFILE) ;;
    *) printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_INPUT_REJECTED' >&2; exit 126 ;;
  esac
done
if test -z "${PGSERVICE-}" || test -z "${PGSERVICEFILE-}" || test -z "${PGPASSFILE-}"; then
  printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_INPUT_MISSING' >&2
  exit 126
fi
for profile_path in "$PGSERVICEFILE" "$PGPASSFILE"; do
  case "$profile_path" in
    /*) ;;
    *) printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_PATH_INVALID' >&2; exit 126 ;;
  esac
  if ! test -f "$profile_path" || ! test -r "$profile_path"; then
    printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_FILE_UNAVAILABLE' >&2
    exit 126
  fi
done
export PGSERVICE PGSERVICEFILE PGPASSFILE
psql --no-psqlrc --set=ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY;
SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5s';
SHOW transaction_read_only;
WITH keys(key) AS (VALUES
 ('maximum_spend_logs_retention_period'),
 ('maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period'),
 ('maximum_health_check_retention_period')),
settings AS (
 SELECT param_value::jsonb AS value FROM public."LiteLLM_Config"
 WHERE param_name = 'general_settings'
)
SELECT keys.key, settings.value IS NOT NULL AS record_has_value,
       jsonb_typeof(settings.value) AS record_type,
       COALESCE(settings.value ? keys.key, false) AS key_present,
       jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) AS value_type,
       CASE
         WHEN jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) = 'null' THEN 'null'
         WHEN jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) = 'number'
           AND (settings.value ->> keys.key) ~ '^-?[0-9]+$'
           THEN settings.value ->> keys.key
         WHEN jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) = 'string'
           AND (settings.value ->> keys.key) ~ '^[0-9]+(s|m|h|d|w|mo)$'
           THEN settings.value ->> keys.key
         ELSE '[absent or withheld]'
       END AS retention_value
FROM keys LEFT JOIN settings ON true ORDER BY keys.key;
ROLLBACK;
SQL
```

Expected result: `transaction_read_only` is `on`, three rows and `ROLLBACK`.
`record_type` must be `object` or null; stop for any other record shape.
The query reads only the three retention fields from the `general_settings`
record. A missing record, SQL null record, absent key and JSON null key are
not an enabled policy. An unexpected type or withheld value needs owner
interpretation against the selected parser. Do not broaden the query to whole
records, Secrets, provider credentials, or key tables. On connection, schema,
permission, timeout, or shape failure, stop; preserve the safe error and obtain
the database owner's corrected read-only procedure. Do not try a write-capable
profile or run a migration.

3. Compare the mounted and stored observations with these rules.

| Input or observation | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Key absent from initial mounted settings and not applied from the database | No retention period for that record type; deletion is disabled. There is no built-in number of retention days for these three keys. |
| Database key present and applied by the selected process | It overwrites the loaded value even when YAML also supplied that key. A changed value, including null, reschedules cleanup. |
| Database key absent | The setter does not assign that key. It does not prove that the process has forgotten an earlier stored value or now equals the mounted file. |
| Applied null, or a string that raises `ValueError` in the retention parser | The corresponding deletion path is disabled. Other unexpected types can fail parsing; do not call them a safe disabled policy without owner investigation. |
| Integer | The retention parser treats it as days. Use an explicit string such as `7d` when the owner later changes policy. |
| Explicit duration string | `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, `w`, and `mo` mean seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, and calendar months. Zero can parse; do not assume zero disables deletion. Calendar-month seconds depend on parsing time. |

Spend retention applies to `LiteLLM_SpendLogs.startTime` and its derived
`LiteLLM_SpendLogToolIndex.start_time` rows. Autorouter retention applies to
`LiteLLM_AutoRouterSession.last_turn_at`; health retention applies to
`LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable.checked_at`. Each uses its own cutoff. These are
current-database deletions, not changes to previously published backup groups.

The authenticated admin-view `GET /config/field/info?field_name=<key>` reads
stored settings and can fail for an absent field. It is not a loaded-value
read. `GET /config/list?config_type=general_settings` reports loaded settings
but falls back to the database when the loaded value is `None`.
Its `stored_in_db` flag describes presence, not proof of successful application.
Use the owner's private authenticated administration surface for these GETs;
retain only these three fields, not the full response. Neither endpoint is an
unconditional observation of the cleanup task in every running worker.

**Effective runtime policy can remain unknown.** The mounted-file and SQL
results prove inputs at their recorded times. They do not prove that each worker
loaded the same inputs, that a database change was applied, that a scheduler
ran, or that deletion succeeded. To claim an effective policy, the LiteLLM owner
must supply a versioned read-only observation procedure bound to each relevant
Pod/process and observation time. It must identify the loaded values, their
parsed seconds or disabled/error result, the scheduled cleanup state, and any
change between the input reads. Stop at this boundary if that observation is
unavailable or conflicts with the inputs. Keep both dumps and mark the effective
policy `unknown`; do not restart, change retention, or delete rows to make the
observations agree.

The tool verifies the snapshot checksum, size and RDB format before creating the
new directory. It loads RDB with AOF disabled on loopback using a random temporary
password, enables AOF, waits for rewrite, persists configuration, then shuts down.
It removes the loaded RDB from the destination and verifies a second startup
from AOF, `appendfsync always` and `noeviction`, followed by clean shutdown.
The input RDB remains unchanged. `REDIS_MIGRATION_MAXIMUM_SECONDS` defaults to
600. Each server start gets a fresh timeout; polling also checks a shared
deadline. This is not a whole-command deadline. Snapshot hashing, RDB checking,
copying, final hashing and synchronization run outside that server timeout.
`REDIS_MIGRATION_MAXIMUM_BYTES` defaults to 21,474,836,480. It bounds input size,
the server's individual file-growth limit and a final aggregate destination check.
It does not cap total temporary disk use during conversion. Reserve headroom
for source, destination, rewrite and temporary files. If the maintenance window
requires a total deadline or capacity ceiling, the owner must supply an
independently bounded procedure and preserve interrupted-state evidence.

Success prints the new directory and produces `migration-receipt.txt` with
`state=aof-restart-verified` and `cutover=not-performed`, plus `SHA256SUMS` for
AOF files and the receipt. Preserve the initial output and verify checksums.
Existing destination, invalid/mismatched checksum, wrong selected version,
invalid RDB, deadline, size, rewrite or restart failure is a stop condition.
An interrupted directory remains visibly incomplete; the tool refuses to
silently overwrite or resume it. Preserve it for diagnosis and choose a fresh
absent destination only after resolving the failure. No source credentials,
Kubernetes mutation or client switch belong to this offline command.

The Redis owner must separately provision and isolate a compatible target,
copy and verify the full AOF manifest/files into a fresh correctly owned volume,
retain the external password authority, and verify the selected server version,
streams/groups/pending state, original absolute dedup expiries, lost-ACK replay
without an extra entry, and a target restart. Render client endpoints and
network policies for the selected release before opening access. Switch clients
last with the old source fenced. Before new target writes, a compatible restore
of the retained snapshot may support rollback; after new writes it is stale.
Fence and capture the new authoritative dataset or fix forward instead of
starting both writers or downgrading AOF in place. A copied directory, checksum
or offline receipt proves neither Kubernetes/CSI durability nor a complete
live restore. Stop before cluster install/cutover without the owners' bound
provisioning, security, verification and rollback procedure.
