### LiteLLM row retention

The [checked-in gateway YAML selects no row-retention policy](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/my-values/infra/litellm-config.yaml#L1-L14).
Both selected LiteLLM revisions can schedule deletion of old request-cost
records (spend logs), request-routing sessions (autorouter sessions), and
health-check records when their effective retention settings enable cleanup.
[Direct scheduling](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L9588-L9629)
and [GitOps scheduling](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L10008-L10049)
are conditional. Database-stored settings can change and reschedule this job;
see [direct setting application](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L6805-L6825)
and [GitOps setting application](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L7162-L7182).
The cleanup implementation [deletes aged rows in bounded batches](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/db/db_transaction_queue/spend_log_cleanup.py#L308-L336)
from [these record tables](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/db/db_transaction_queue/spend_log_cleanup.py#L456-L505).

Before assuming indefinite retention, identify the mounted configuration and
database-stored values of `maximum_spend_logs_retention_period`,
`maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period`, and
`maximum_health_check_retention_period`. Cleanup can remove aged diagnostic or
accounting rows before a later backup. A retained earlier dump can still contain
those rows. Preserve the dumps and determine the effective policy before treating
this difference as corruption. These settings do not define a common expiry for
models, keys, or budgets, and do not delete retained backup groups.

#### Read retention inputs without changing the service

This procedure applies to the two [selected LiteLLM revisions](#selected-litellm-source-and-image-boundary).
Run it from the bound independent administration machine. It reads one running
LiteLLM Pod and its database; it does not change retention or start cleanup.
Use `kubectl`, Python 3 with PyYAML in the selected container, and `psql` on the
administration machine. Do not install tools into the running container.

Before starting, the LiteLLM and database owners must identify the deployed
profile, immutable image, upstream revision, database service and database
name, applied schema-change history, and the exact Pod/container. They must
supply an authorized read-only database connection profile privately. It must
select that instance and a role with only the necessary read access. Use a
libpq service file and password file through their private paths; never put a
credential URL or password in a command, record, or shell trace. Cluster access
must permit reading the selected Pod and executing this file-read command.
The owners must confirm that the deployed `LiteLLM_Config` table is in `public`,
with `param_name` as its unique text key and `param_value` as JSON or JSONB.
The [direct schema](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/schema.prisma#L618-L623)
and [GitOps schema](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/schema.prisma#L621-L626)
describe the selected schema, but do not prove that live migrations completed.
Stop if this instance, schema, read-only access, or tool selection is unverified.

1. Bind the cluster as specified in [Bind Cluster Authority](../use/install.md#bind-cluster-authority).
   Set `LITELLM_POD` to the owner's exact running Pod name and
   `LITELLM_POD_UID` to its recorded UID. Keep its non-secret owner/image/mount
   record with the observation time. Both repository profiles mount
   `/app/config.yaml`; confirm that this is the selected container's actual
   configuration file. The [direct mount](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/my-values/infra/litellm-deployment.yaml#L60-L74)
   and [GitOps mount](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/gitops/platform/litellm/resources.yaml#L40-L50)
   use `subPath`. A ConfigMap alone is insufficient: the `subPath` mount
   can keep older bytes after a ConfigMap change.

```bash
assert_cluster_binding || exit 126
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
test "$(kubectl --context "$EXPECTED_CONTEXT" -n "$NAMESPACE" get pod \
  "$LITELLM_POD" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}')" = "$LITELLM_POD_UID"
kubectl --context "$EXPECTED_CONTEXT" -n "$NAMESPACE" exec -i \
  "$LITELLM_POD" -c litellm -- python - <<'PY'
try:
    import hashlib, json, re, yaml
    raw = open('/app/config.yaml', 'rb').read()
    config = yaml.safe_load(raw)
    if not isinstance(config, dict):
        raise ValueError()
    g = config.get('general_settings', {})
    if not isinstance(g, dict):
        raise ValueError()
    keys = ('maximum_spend_logs_retention_period',
            'maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period',
            'maximum_health_check_retention_period')
    def safe(v):
        if v is None or type(v) is int:
            return v
        if type(v) is str and re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]+(s|m|h|d|w|mo)', v):
            return v
        return {'uninterpreted_type': type(v).__name__, 'value_withheld': True}
    print(json.dumps({'mounted_file_sha256': hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
        'settings': {k: {'present': k in g, 'value': safe(g.get(k))} for k in keys}}))
except Exception:
    raise SystemExit('LITELLM_RETENTION_CONFIG_READ_FAILED') from None
PY
```

Expected result: one mounted-file digest and exactly three setting records.
`present: false` differs from an explicit YAML null. The output withholds
unexpected values instead of exposing arbitrary configuration strings.
A missing Pod, changed UID, file-read failure, unavailable Python/PyYAML, or
unexpected value stops this identification. File-read, import, parse, and
mapping-shape failures return nonzero with only
`LITELLM_RETENTION_CONFIG_READ_FAILED`; raw YAML, exception text and tracebacks
are withheld. An empty/null document or a nonmapping `general_settings` is
rejected. Keep this constant failure record and ask the owner to diagnose the
configuration privately. Obtain a versioned owner procedure
that exports only these fields and the exact mounted-file identity if this
read command is unavailable. Do not dump the configuration or environment.

2. In a dedicated query shell, set `PGSERVICE`, `PGSERVICEFILE`, and
   `PGPASSFILE` to the owner's read-only service name and absolute private
   service-file and password-file paths. Ordinary shell assignments are not
   inherited by `psql`; the command block below explicitly exports them.
   The owner must confirm that this service name exists in that exact file,
   selects the verified source host/address, port, database and read-only user,
   and contains the approved transport and authentication settings. The files
   must be privately owned and readable; the password file must deny group and
   other access. The service section must contain neither a `password` nor a
   `passfile` setting for this password-file procedure. Do not print file
   contents or selector values.

   A [service-file field](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/libpq-pgservice.html)
   overrides its corresponding environment value. A field omitted from the
   service can still use an inherited variable or a built-in default. A direct
   connection argument overrides the service. Therefore the block rejects
   every other `PG*` shell input and supplies no host, user, database, password
   or connection-string argument. In particular, inherited `PGPASSWORD` can
   supply a password before the [password file](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/libpq-pgpass.html)
   is considered. Reject it instead of silently using it. The selected service
   must define all target identity and required security fields; owners must
   approve any deliberately omitted default. Selector export and a clean
   environment do not by themselves prove which server accepted a connection.

   If the guard rejects an inherited input, stop and ask the owner for a clean
   query shell with the same approved files. Do not dump the environment,
   inspect secrets, or remove an input to guess a connection. Run this exact
   projection only after the live schema and instance checks above:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
for pg_input in ${!PG@}; do
  case "$pg_input" in
    PGSERVICE|PGSERVICEFILE|PGPASSFILE) ;;
    *) printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_INPUT_REJECTED' >&2; exit 126 ;;
  esac
done
if test -z "${PGSERVICE-}" || test -z "${PGSERVICEFILE-}" || test -z "${PGPASSFILE-}"; then
  printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_INPUT_MISSING' >&2
  exit 126
fi
for profile_path in "$PGSERVICEFILE" "$PGPASSFILE"; do
  case "$profile_path" in
    /*) ;;
    *) printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_PATH_INVALID' >&2; exit 126 ;;
  esac
  if ! test -f "$profile_path" || ! test -r "$profile_path"; then
    printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_FILE_UNAVAILABLE' >&2
    exit 126
  fi
done
export PGSERVICE PGSERVICEFILE PGPASSFILE
psql --no-psqlrc --set=ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY;
SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5s';
SHOW transaction_read_only;
WITH keys(key) AS (VALUES
 ('maximum_spend_logs_retention_period'),
 ('maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period'),
 ('maximum_health_check_retention_period')),
settings AS (
 SELECT param_value::jsonb AS value FROM public."LiteLLM_Config"
 WHERE param_name = 'general_settings'
)
SELECT keys.key, settings.value IS NOT NULL AS record_has_value,
       jsonb_typeof(settings.value) AS record_type,
       COALESCE(settings.value ? keys.key, false) AS key_present,
       jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) AS value_type,
       CASE
         WHEN jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) = 'null' THEN 'null'
         WHEN jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) = 'number'
           AND (settings.value ->> keys.key) ~ '^-?[0-9]+$'
           THEN settings.value ->> keys.key
         WHEN jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) = 'string'
           AND (settings.value ->> keys.key) ~ '^[0-9]+(s|m|h|d|w|mo)$'
           THEN settings.value ->> keys.key
         ELSE '[absent or withheld]'
       END AS retention_value
FROM keys LEFT JOIN settings ON true ORDER BY keys.key;
ROLLBACK;
SQL
```

Expected result: `transaction_read_only` is `on`, three rows and `ROLLBACK`.
`record_type` must be `object` or null; stop for any other record shape.
The query reads only the three retention fields from the `general_settings`
record. A missing record, SQL null record, absent key and JSON null key are
not an enabled policy. An unexpected type or withheld value needs owner
interpretation against the selected parser. Do not broaden the query to whole
records, Secrets, provider credentials, or key tables. On connection, schema,
permission, timeout, or shape failure, stop; preserve the safe error and obtain
the database owner's corrected read-only procedure. Do not try a write-capable
profile or run a migration.

3. Compare the mounted and stored observations with these rules.

| Input or observation | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Key absent from initial mounted settings and not applied from the database | No retention period for that record type; deletion is disabled. There is no built-in number of retention days for these three keys. |
| Database key present and applied by the selected process | It overwrites the loaded value even when YAML also supplied that key. A changed value, including null, reschedules cleanup. |
| Database key absent | The setter does not assign that key. It does not prove that the process has forgotten an earlier stored value or now equals the mounted file. |
| Applied null, or a string that raises `ValueError` in the retention parser | The corresponding deletion path is disabled. Other unexpected types can fail parsing; do not call them a safe disabled policy without owner investigation. |
| Integer | The retention parser treats it as days. Use an explicit string such as `7d` when the owner later changes policy. |
| Explicit duration string | `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, `w`, and `mo` mean seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, and calendar months. Zero can parse; do not assume zero disables deletion. Calendar-month seconds depend on parsing time. |

Spend retention applies to `LiteLLM_SpendLogs.startTime` and its derived
`LiteLLM_SpendLogToolIndex.start_time` rows. Autorouter retention applies to
`LiteLLM_AutoRouterSession.last_turn_at`; health retention applies to
`LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable.checked_at`. Each uses its own cutoff. These are
current-database deletions, not changes to previously published backup groups.

The authenticated admin-view `GET /config/field/info?field_name=<key>` reads
stored settings and can fail for an absent field. It is not a loaded-value
read. `GET /config/list?config_type=general_settings` reports loaded settings
but falls back to the database when the loaded value is `None`.
Its `stored_in_db` flag describes presence, not proof of successful application.
Use the owner's private authenticated administration surface for these GETs;
retain only these three fields, not the full response. Neither endpoint is an
unconditional observation of the cleanup task in every running worker.

**Effective runtime policy can remain unknown.** The mounted-file and SQL
results prove inputs at their recorded times. They do not prove that each worker
loaded the same inputs, that a database change was applied, that a scheduler
ran, or that deletion succeeded. To claim an effective policy, the LiteLLM owner
must supply a versioned read-only observation procedure bound to each relevant
Pod/process and observation time. It must identify the loaded values, their
parsed seconds or disabled/error result, the scheduled cleanup state, and any
change between the input reads. Stop at this boundary if that observation is
unavailable or conflicts with the inputs. Keep both dumps and mark the effective
policy `unknown`; do not restart, change retention, or delete rows to make the
observations agree.

## Prepare a Redis RDB as a fresh AOF dataset

The supported repository primitive is **offline RDB-to-AOF preparation**, not

directory for the selected Redis version. Keep the original release, volume,
source snapshot, independent password authority and consumer configuration.
Do not run this tool against the only retained copy or a destination in use.

and reconciliation that could restart them. Preserve streams, consumer groups,
pending deliveries and absolute dedup expiries. Obtain the RDB with the selected
authenticated snapshot transport while source writes remain fenced. The existing
migration procedure uses `CLIENT PAUSE 600000 WRITE`, a bounded 240-second

A pause alone is temporary, not an enduring fence. If the owner cannot prove
that no newer source writes occurred, discard the candidate for cutover and
repeat capture after restoring the fence. Retain the RDB/checksum outside the
source-volume failure domain. An old source PVC is not proof of the latest state.

```bash

export REDIS_CLI=/absolute/selected/redis-cli
export REDIS_CHECK_RDB=/absolute/selected/redis-check-rdb

(cd "$NEW_DATA_DIRECTORY" && sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS)
```

An interrupted directory remains visibly incomplete; the tool refuses to

Status: implemented with stated retention and disaster-recovery limits
Audience: platform operator, runtime developer, data owner, incident responder
Owner: state-owning component maintainers

Applies to: current file stores, Prism PostgreSQL, LiteLLM PostgreSQL, Redis, and content-addressed artifacts
Last verified: code, schema, chart, values, recovery-script, and focused-test inspection on 2026-09-20 State/Wait operation sections source-reviewed 2026-10-22; original other-scope dates and execution limits unchanged.

### LiteLLM row retention

The [checked-in gateway YAML selects no row-retention policy](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/my-values/infra/litellm-config.yaml#L1-L14).
Both selected LiteLLM revisions can schedule deletion of old request-cost
records (spend logs), request-routing sessions (autorouter sessions), and
health-check records when their effective retention settings enable cleanup.
[Direct scheduling](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L9588-L9629)
and [GitOps scheduling](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L10008-L10049)
are conditional. Database-stored settings can change and reschedule this job;
see [direct setting application](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L6805-L6825)
and [GitOps setting application](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L7162-L7182).
The cleanup implementation [deletes aged rows in bounded batches](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/db/db_transaction_queue/spend_log_cleanup.py#L308-L336)
from [these record tables](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/db/db_transaction_queue/spend_log_cleanup.py#L456-L505).

Before assuming indefinite retention, identify the mounted configuration and
database-stored values of `maximum_spend_logs_retention_period`,
`maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period`, and
`maximum_health_check_retention_period`. Cleanup can remove aged diagnostic or
accounting rows before a later backup. A retained earlier dump can still contain
those rows. Preserve the dumps and determine the effective policy before treating
this difference as corruption. These settings do not define a common expiry for
models, keys, or budgets, and do not delete retained backup groups.

#### Read retention inputs without changing the service

This procedure applies to the two [selected LiteLLM revisions](#selected-litellm-source-and-image-boundary).
Run it from the bound independent administration machine. It reads one running
LiteLLM Pod and its database; it does not change retention or start cleanup.
Use `kubectl`, Python 3 with PyYAML in the selected container, and `psql` on the
administration machine. Do not install tools into the running container.

Before starting, the LiteLLM and database owners must identify the deployed
profile, immutable image, upstream revision, database service and database
name, applied schema-change history, and the exact Pod/container. They must
supply an authorized read-only database connection profile privately. It must
select that instance and a role with only the necessary read access. Use a
libpq service file and password file through their private paths; never put a
credential URL or password in a command, record, or shell trace. Cluster access
must permit reading the selected Pod and executing this file-read command.
The owners must confirm that the deployed `LiteLLM_Config` table is in `public`,
with `param_name` as its unique text key and `param_value` as JSON or JSONB.
The [direct schema](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/schema.prisma#L618-L623)
and [GitOps schema](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/16f6d924530c1cf2dc94b3e83c86a4632aefb7c0/schema.prisma#L621-L626)
describe the selected schema, but do not prove that live migrations completed.
Stop if this instance, schema, read-only access, or tool selection is unverified.

1. Bind the cluster as specified in [Bind Cluster Authority](../use/install.md#bind-cluster-authority).
   Set `LITELLM_POD` to the owner's exact running Pod name and
   `LITELLM_POD_UID` to its recorded UID. Keep its non-secret owner/image/mount
   record with the observation time. Both repository profiles mount
   `/app/config.yaml`; confirm that this is the selected container's actual
   configuration file. The [direct mount](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/my-values/infra/litellm-deployment.yaml#L60-L74)
   and [GitOps mount](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ebcc04066d42c94b4a4e0fc85e3393dae3d61f78/gitops/platform/litellm/resources.yaml#L40-L50)
   use `subPath`. A ConfigMap alone is insufficient: the `subPath` mount
   can keep older bytes after a ConfigMap change.

```bash
assert_cluster_binding || exit 126
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
test "$(kubectl --context "$EXPECTED_CONTEXT" -n "$NAMESPACE" get pod \
  "$LITELLM_POD" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.uid}')" = "$LITELLM_POD_UID"
kubectl --context "$EXPECTED_CONTEXT" -n "$NAMESPACE" exec -i \
  "$LITELLM_POD" -c litellm -- python - <<'PY'
try:
    import hashlib, json, re, yaml
    raw = open('/app/config.yaml', 'rb').read()
    config = yaml.safe_load(raw)
    if not isinstance(config, dict):
        raise ValueError()
    g = config.get('general_settings', {})
    if not isinstance(g, dict):
        raise ValueError()
    keys = ('maximum_spend_logs_retention_period',
            'maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period',
            'maximum_health_check_retention_period')
    def safe(v):
        if v is None or type(v) is int:
            return v
        if type(v) is str and re.fullmatch(r'[0-9]+(s|m|h|d|w|mo)', v):
            return v
        return {'uninterpreted_type': type(v).__name__, 'value_withheld': True}
    print(json.dumps({'mounted_file_sha256': hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
        'settings': {k: {'present': k in g, 'value': safe(g.get(k))} for k in keys}}))
except Exception:
    raise SystemExit('LITELLM_RETENTION_CONFIG_READ_FAILED') from None
PY
```

Expected result: one mounted-file digest and exactly three setting records.
`present: false` differs from an explicit YAML null. The output withholds
unexpected values instead of exposing arbitrary configuration strings.
A missing Pod, changed UID, file-read failure, unavailable Python/PyYAML, or
unexpected value stops this identification. File-read, import, parse, and
mapping-shape failures return nonzero with only
`LITELLM_RETENTION_CONFIG_READ_FAILED`; raw YAML, exception text and tracebacks
are withheld. An empty/null document or a nonmapping `general_settings` is
rejected. Keep this constant failure record and ask the owner to diagnose the
configuration privately. Obtain a versioned owner procedure
that exports only these fields and the exact mounted-file identity if this
read command is unavailable. Do not dump the configuration or environment.

2. In a dedicated query shell, set `PGSERVICE`, `PGSERVICEFILE`, and
   `PGPASSFILE` to the owner's read-only service name and absolute private
   service-file and password-file paths. Ordinary shell assignments are not
   inherited by `psql`; the command block below explicitly exports them.
   The owner must confirm that this service name exists in that exact file,
   selects the verified source host/address, port, database and read-only user,
   and contains the approved transport and authentication settings. The files
   must be privately owned and readable; the password file must deny group and
   other access. The service section must contain neither a `password` nor a
   `passfile` setting for this password-file procedure. Do not print file
   contents or selector values.

   A [service-file field](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/libpq-pgservice.html)
   overrides its corresponding environment value. A field omitted from the
   service can still use an inherited variable or a built-in default. A direct
   connection argument overrides the service. Therefore the block rejects
   every other `PG*` shell input and supplies no host, user, database, password
   or connection-string argument. In particular, inherited `PGPASSWORD` can
   supply a password before the [password file](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/libpq-pgpass.html)
   is considered. Reject it instead of silently using it. The selected service
   must define all target identity and required security fields; owners must
   approve any deliberately omitted default. Selector export and a clean
   environment do not by themselves prove which server accepted a connection.

   If the guard rejects an inherited input, stop and ask the owner for a clean
   query shell with the same approved files. Do not dump the environment,
   inspect secrets, or remove an input to guess a connection. Run this exact
   projection only after the live schema and instance checks above:

```bash
set -euo pipefail
umask 077
for pg_input in ${!PG@}; do
  case "$pg_input" in
    PGSERVICE|PGSERVICEFILE|PGPASSFILE) ;;
    *) printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_INPUT_REJECTED' >&2; exit 126 ;;
  esac
done
if test -z "${PGSERVICE-}" || test -z "${PGSERVICEFILE-}" || test -z "${PGPASSFILE-}"; then
  printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_INPUT_MISSING' >&2
  exit 126
fi
for profile_path in "$PGSERVICEFILE" "$PGPASSFILE"; do
  case "$profile_path" in
    /*) ;;
    *) printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_PATH_INVALID' >&2; exit 126 ;;
  esac
  if ! test -f "$profile_path" || ! test -r "$profile_path"; then
    printf '%s\n' 'LITELLM_RETENTION_PROFILE_FILE_UNAVAILABLE' >&2
    exit 126
  fi
done
export PGSERVICE PGSERVICEFILE PGPASSFILE
psql --no-psqlrc --set=ON_ERROR_STOP=1 <<'SQL'
BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY;
SET LOCAL statement_timeout = '5s';
SHOW transaction_read_only;
WITH keys(key) AS (VALUES
 ('maximum_spend_logs_retention_period'),
 ('maximum_autorouter_session_retention_period'),
 ('maximum_health_check_retention_period')),
settings AS (
 SELECT param_value::jsonb AS value FROM public."LiteLLM_Config"
 WHERE param_name = 'general_settings'
)
SELECT keys.key, settings.value IS NOT NULL AS record_has_value,
       jsonb_typeof(settings.value) AS record_type,
       COALESCE(settings.value ? keys.key, false) AS key_present,
       jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) AS value_type,
       CASE
         WHEN jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) = 'null' THEN 'null'
         WHEN jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) = 'number'
           AND (settings.value ->> keys.key) ~ '^-?[0-9]+$'
           THEN settings.value ->> keys.key
         WHEN jsonb_typeof(settings.value -> keys.key) = 'string'
           AND (settings.value ->> keys.key) ~ '^[0-9]+(s|m|h|d|w|mo)$'
           THEN settings.value ->> keys.key
         ELSE '[absent or withheld]'
       END AS retention_value
FROM keys LEFT JOIN settings ON true ORDER BY keys.key;
ROLLBACK;
SQL
```

Expected result: `transaction_read_only` is `on`, three rows and `ROLLBACK`.
`record_type` must be `object` or null; stop for any other record shape.
The query reads only the three retention fields from the `general_settings`
record. A missing record, SQL null record, absent key and JSON null key are
not an enabled policy. An unexpected type or withheld value needs owner
interpretation against the selected parser. Do not broaden the query to whole
records, Secrets, provider credentials, or key tables. On connection, schema,
permission, timeout, or shape failure, stop; preserve the safe error and obtain
the database owner's corrected read-only procedure. Do not try a write-capable
profile or run a migration.

3. Compare the mounted and stored observations with these rules.

| Input or observation | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| Key absent from initial mounted settings and not applied from the database | No retention period for that record type; deletion is disabled. There is no built-in number of retention days for these three keys. |
| Database key present and applied by the selected process | It overwrites the loaded value even when YAML also supplied that key. A changed value, including null, reschedules cleanup. |
| Database key absent | The setter does not assign that key. It does not prove that the process has forgotten an earlier stored value or now equals the mounted file. |
| Applied null, or a string that raises `ValueError` in the retention parser | The corresponding deletion path is disabled. Other unexpected types can fail parsing; do not call them a safe disabled policy without owner investigation. |
| Integer | The retention parser treats it as days. Use an explicit string such as `7d` when the owner later changes policy. |
| Explicit duration string | `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, `w`, and `mo` mean seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, and calendar months. Zero can parse; do not assume zero disables deletion. Calendar-month seconds depend on parsing time. |

Spend retention applies to `LiteLLM_SpendLogs.startTime` and its derived
`LiteLLM_SpendLogToolIndex.start_time` rows. Autorouter retention applies to
`LiteLLM_AutoRouterSession.last_turn_at`; health retention applies to
`LiteLLM_HealthCheckTable.checked_at`. Each uses its own cutoff. These are
current-database deletions, not changes to previously published backup groups.

The authenticated admin-view `GET /config/field/info?field_name=<key>` reads
stored settings and can fail for an absent field. It is not a loaded-value
read. `GET /config/list?config_type=general_settings` reports loaded settings
but falls back to the database when the loaded value is `None`.
Its `stored_in_db` flag describes presence, not proof of successful application.
Use the owner's private authenticated administration surface for these GETs;
retain only these three fields, not the full response. Neither endpoint is an
unconditional observation of the cleanup task in every running worker.

**Effective runtime policy can remain unknown.** The mounted-file and SQL
results prove inputs at their recorded times. They do not prove that each worker
loaded the same inputs, that a database change was applied, that a scheduler
ran, or that deletion succeeded. To claim an effective policy, the LiteLLM owner
must supply a versioned read-only observation procedure bound to each relevant
Pod/process and observation time. It must identify the loaded values, their
parsed seconds or disabled/error result, the scheduled cleanup state, and any
change between the input reads. Stop at this boundary if that observation is
unavailable or conflicts with the inputs. Keep both dumps and mark the effective
policy `unknown`; do not restart, change retention, or delete rows to make the
observations agree.

> **Source evidence — retention identification and its limit**
>
> Claim: database application overwrites present retention keys; the parser and
> table-specific deletion paths determine cleanup, while administration reads
> have the limits stated above.
>
> Implementation: [direct setter](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/proxy_server.py#L6805-L6825),

> [table cutoffs](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/blob/7d5b6456baaf8be6ac1a60db2b710566b5344adf/litellm/proxy/db/db_transaction_queue/spend_log_cleanup.py#L456-L505),

## Prepare a Redis RDB as a fresh AOF dataset

The supported repository primitive is **offline RDB-to-AOF preparation**, not
an arbitrary AOF restore or an automatic cluster cutover. Its input is one
checksum-bound RDB from a fenced source; its output is a new private local
directory for the selected Redis version. Keep the original release, volume,
source snapshot, independent password authority and consumer configuration.
Do not run this tool against the only retained copy or a destination in use.

Before capture, the Redis owner must inventory and stop publishers, schedulers
and reconciliation that could restart them. Preserve streams, consumer groups,
pending deliveries and absolute dedup expiries. Obtain the RDB with the selected
authenticated snapshot transport while source writes remain fenced. The existing
migration procedure uses `CLIENT PAUSE 600000 WRITE`, a bounded 240-second
`redis-cli --rdb` capture, then stops the source within that pause window.
A pause alone is temporary, not an enduring fence. If the owner cannot prove
that no newer source writes occurred, discard the candidate for cutover and
repeat capture after restoring the fence. Retain the RDB/checksum outside the
source-volume failure domain. An old source PVC is not proof of the latest state.

For the **offline step**, use a Linux maintenance host with Bash, Node.js and
locked repository dependencies (`js-yaml`), coreutils, `setsid`, `timeout`, and
the actual native `redis-server`, `redis-cli` and `redis-check-rdb` binaries.
`versions.json` selects the destination server version; a different server
version fails admission. Supply these private, explicitly selected paths:

```bash
set -eu
export REDIS_SERVER=/absolute/selected/redis-server
export REDIS_CLI=/absolute/selected/redis-cli
export REDIS_CHECK_RDB=/absolute/selected/redis-check-rdb
# Set SNAPSHOT to the retained absolute RDB path and RDB_SHA256 to its recorded hash.
# NEW_DATA_DIRECTORY must be an absolute canonical path that does not yet exist.
bash scripts/redis-prepare-migration.sh "$SNAPSHOT" "$RDB_SHA256" "$NEW_DATA_DIRECTORY"
(cd "$NEW_DATA_DIRECTORY" && sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS)
```

The tool verifies the snapshot checksum, size and RDB format before creating the
new directory. It loads RDB with AOF disabled on loopback using a random temporary
password, enables AOF, waits for rewrite, persists configuration, then shuts down.
It removes the loaded RDB from the destination and verifies a second startup
from AOF, `appendfsync always` and `noeviction`, followed by clean shutdown.
The input RDB remains unchanged. `REDIS_MIGRATION_MAXIMUM_SECONDS` defaults to
600. Each server start gets a fresh timeout; polling also checks a shared
deadline. This is not a whole-command deadline. Snapshot hashing, RDB checking,
copying, final hashing and synchronization run outside that server timeout.
`REDIS_MIGRATION_MAXIMUM_BYTES` defaults to 21,474,836,480. It bounds input size,
the server's individual file-growth limit and a final aggregate destination check.
It does not cap total temporary disk use during conversion. Reserve headroom
for source, destination, rewrite and temporary files. If the maintenance window
requires a total deadline or capacity ceiling, the owner must supply an
independently bounded procedure and preserve interrupted-state evidence.

Success prints the new directory and produces `migration-receipt.txt` with
`state=aof-restart-verified` and `cutover=not-performed`, plus `SHA256SUMS` for
AOF files and the receipt. Preserve the initial output and verify checksums.
Existing destination, invalid/mismatched checksum, wrong selected version,
invalid RDB, deadline, size, rewrite or restart failure is a stop condition.
An interrupted directory remains visibly incomplete; the tool refuses to
silently overwrite or resume it. Preserve it for diagnosis and choose a fresh
absent destination only after resolving the failure. No source credentials,
Kubernetes mutation or client switch belong to this offline command.

The Redis owner must separately provision and isolate a compatible target,
copy and verify the full AOF manifest/files into a fresh correctly owned volume,
retain the external password authority, and verify the selected server version,
streams/groups/pending state, original absolute dedup expiries, lost-ACK replay
without an extra entry, and a target restart. Render client endpoints and
network policies for the selected release before opening access. Switch clients
last with the old source fenced. Before new target writes, a compatible restore
of the retained snapshot may support rollback; after new writes it is stale.
Fence and capture the new authoritative dataset or fix forward instead of
starting both writers or downgrading AOF in place. A copied directory, checksum
or offline receipt proves neither Kubernetes/CSI durability nor a complete
live restore. Stop before cluster install/cutover without the owners' bound
provisioning, security, verification and rollback procedure.

[selected version](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1e60f5d34c9a599a334a414987a754c95dc3543f/versions.json#L96-L114).

[persistence policy](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1e60f5d34c9a599a334a414987a754c95dc3543f/my-values/infra/redis-values.yaml#L1-L29).

[verification fixture](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1e60f5d34c9a599a334a414987a754c95dc3543f/tests/verification/reliability/redis-migration.test.mts#L1-L61).

## Purpose

This page maps the software boundaries to running workloads.
It explains identity, network, storage, permissions, observability, and failure domains.

It does not treat supporting services as an unnamed infrastructure box.
[Pipeline Dependencies](pipeline-dependencies.md) explains the Git, Redis, PostgreSQL, BuildKit, registry, mirror, and Tailscale paths.

A rendered chart proves intended Kubernetes resources.
It does not prove that a live cluster applies or enforces them.
Use the linked operations checks for that proof.

## Runtime Roles and Workloads

A runtime role is a packaging boundary.
It declares the packages and plugins available to one purpose.

| Role or workload | Main responsibility | Included authority | Excluded authority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nova role | Compile and control pipeline runs. | Lifecycle state, stage leases, configured adapters. | Worker execution semantics and specialist judgment. |
| Buster role | Run fixed test plans. | Test providers, evidence, Worker Core controls. | Canonical pipeline decisions. |
| Prism role | Host the OpenClaw Prism integration. | Prism engine and selected shared adapters. | Nova lifecycle authority. |
| Prism Control | Own Prism operations and durable application state. | Revision, operation, approval, and artifact coordination. | Native host process authority. |
| Prism Worker | Run bounded native Prism operations. | Worker Core attempt and process controls. | Product approval and public entry. |
| Prism Studio | Give humans the application interface. | User-facing requests through Control. | Direct database or worker authority. |
| Prism Ingestion | Fetch and quarantine optional external input. | Narrow outbound fetch path. | Control state ownership. |
| PostgreSQL | Store Prism relational state. | Database persistence only. | Pipeline and product decisions. |
| Prism agent bridge | Translate authenticated dispatch into a durable Control request and run one claimed OpenClaw job. | The claimed job ID, fence, and local process lifecycle. | Prism documents, approval, and Nova lifecycle authority. |
| Prism OpenClaw gateway | Perform the external design-agent session and expose fenced Prism tools. | Its gateway session, configured model route, and tool invocation. | Durable Control job/result authority. |
| LiteLLM | Supply the configured OpenClaw memory embedding route. | Gateway routing and its separate database state. | Agent reasoning route, Prism state, and pipeline lifecycle. |
| Managed OpenAI provider | Supply the model selected by an OpenClaw agent session. | Provider response and external account controls. | OpenClaw session, Control job, and pipeline lifecycle authority. |
| Discord | Carry enabled Nova and Buster bot traffic and configured webhook notifications. | External message transport and Discord account controls. | User authorization beyond configured allowlists, pipeline state, and domain results. |

Forge and Echo do not appear as current role manifests.
Nova reaches them through configured runtime dispatch.
Their actual process location depends on that runtime configuration.

## Why Role Bundles Exist

A single large image could contain every engine and plugin.
That image would make accidental authority easier and review harder.

Role bundles make the intended content explicit.
Nova does not need the Buster engine to control a Buster job.
Buster does not need Nova Core to execute a test provider.

The bundle is only the first limit.
Activation selects a smaller set of registrations.
Capability grants reduce each invocation again.
Network policy and workload identity limit process-to-process access.

These limits overlap on purpose.
One incorrect setting must not silently grant every other permission.

## Four Independent Trust Questions

Before one component trusts another, it asks four questions.

1. **Who connected?** SPIFFE gives the workload an identity.
2. **Was the route protected?** Envoy authenticates and encrypts the connection with mutual TLS.
3. **May this identity call this service?** Worker code checks the exact expected SPIFFE ID.
4. **Can packets reach the port?** Kubernetes NetworkPolicy limits pods, namespaces, and ports.

Nova-to-Buster source transfer adds another question:
does this archive match the source identity that Nova signed?

**Historical reason:** Unknown. **Current rationale (inference):** Network
location is not an identity. A Pod IP can change, and another Pod can exist in
the same namespace. Exact workload identity plus application authorization
keeps those cases distinct.

**Cost:** SPIRE, its CSI driver, Envoy configuration, and network-policy enforcement become service dependencies.
Protected routes fail closed when those dependencies fail.

**Status and reconsideration:** The secured chart profile contains the SPIFFE
and Envoy path. Live issuance and denial remain separate acceptance.
Reconsider the layers only if a replacement proves exact workload identity,
encrypted peer authentication, application allowlists, rotation, and both
positive and negative route behavior without trusting a caller-supplied header.

> **Source evidence — application identity check**
>
> **Claim:** Application identity checks require trusted proxy origin and an exact allowed workload peer.
>
> **Implementation:** Worker trust and separate configured Prism caller identities below define this application boundary.
>
>
> [Worker Core parses and authorizes proxied SPIFFE identities](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/worker/core/worker/trust.ts#L1-L52).
>

>
> [Worker Trust gives the complete certificate and proxy path](worker-trust.md).
>
> **Contract or setting:** A valid forwarded URI still requires loopback origin and membership in the selected allowlist.
>
> **Test evidence:** No live forged-header, missing-SVID or wrong-peer rejection is established by these source links.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`. Source bindings, not execution receipts.
>
> **Limit:** A caller-supplied identity header or valid unrelated SVID cannot grant service authority.
>

## Identity Boundaries

Each Prism workload has its own Kubernetes ServiceAccount.
The chart disables automatic service-account token mounting.
SPIRE derives the workload identity from namespace and ServiceAccount.

The expected identity has this form:

```text
spiffe://kubeclaw.internal/ns/<namespace>/sa/<service-account>
```

The application cannot select another identity through a normal environment variable.
Envoy receives the short-lived certificate from the SPIRE Workload API.

Human identity remains separate. Keycloak is an unimplemented architectural
option: this repository does not deploy it, configure a client, connect Prism
session exchange to it, or provide a live acceptance procedure. If a future
deployment selects Keycloak, it could authenticate a human and supply
application roles; it still would not provide workload identity or artifact
signatures. Current operators must use only the implemented human-authentication
path described by the selected application procedure.

> **Source evidence — separate service accounts**
>
> **Claim:** Prism workloads use separate ServiceAccounts for their declared responsibilities.
>
> **Implementation:** The account template below declares the Control, Studio, Worker, Ingestion, Backup and test-runner identities.
>
>
> [The Prism chart creates Control, Studio, Worker, Ingestion, Backup, and test-runner accounts](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/charts/prism/templates/serviceaccounts.yaml#L1-L7).
>
> **Contract or setting:** Namespace/ServiceAccount identity feeds workload attestation; human authentication remains a separate application path.
>
> **Test evidence:** No deployed account selection or SVID issuance test execution is established by this template.
>

>
> **Limit:** An account declaration does not deploy Keycloak, grant human roles or prove token isolation.
>

## Network Boundaries

The Prism chart first denies ingress and egress for its named workloads.
It then adds only the required paths.

Important paths include:

| Caller | Destination | Port or route | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prism Studio | Prism Control | HTTP 8080 | Human application actions. |
| Nova | Prism agent Envoy | Nova loopback 28080 to agent Service 8080 and Envoy 18082 | Authenticate and deliver design dispatch to the loopback bridge. |
| Prism agent bridge and OpenClaw tool | Prism Control | Agent loopback 28080 to Control mTLS Service 8443 | Persist dispatch, claim jobs, and commit fenced designs or revisions. |
| Prism Control | Prism Worker | mTLS service 8443 when enabled | Bounded native operation. |
| Prism Control and Worker | PostgreSQL | TCP 5432 | Prism state. |
| Prism Control | Prism Ingestion | HTTP 8080 | Optional controlled ingestion. |
| Prism Ingestion | Approved external source | HTTPS 443 only | Bounded acquisition into temporary quarantine. |
| Prism OpenClaw agent | LiteLLM | HTTP 4000 | Remote memory-search embeddings only. |
| LiteLLM | Vertex AI | HTTPS 443 | The configured `gemini-embedding-001` route and no reasoning traffic. |
| Nova, Buster, and Prism OpenClaw | Managed OpenAI provider | External HTTPS owned by the pinned OpenClaw runtime | Agent reasoning under the configured model allowlist. |
| Discord service | Nova and Buster OpenClaw gateways | External bot gateway and HTTPS APIs | Enabled allowlisted human messages and bot replies. |
| Nova or Buster notification path | Discord webhook | Secret-selected HTTPS destination | Optional notification delivery; never lifecycle authority. |
| Nova | Buster | mTLS worker route | Plan submission, status, result, evidence, cancellation. |

The Service sends protected traffic to the Envoy sidecar.
The sidecar sends accepted local traffic to the application port.
The runtime port is not the public worker endpoint.

Prism Studio is different.
It is an application entry point and can use a private Tailscale ingress.
It does not use the internal worker route for browser traffic.

The checked-in policy set and Hubble observation path require Cilium in the
current supported secured deployment. The architecture does not bind Nova Core
to Cilium, but the repository has no implemented and proved Flannel equivalent
for these policies. Do not label Flannel as a supported secured fallback until
positive and negative route tests pass with equivalent policy and evidence.

This statement has two evidence levels. The repository proves that selected
manifests contain Cilium resources, that installation checks target Cilium, and
that Ops can query Hubble. It does not prove that a particular live cluster
enforces a deny rule. That proof needs an allowed request, a denied request, and
the matching live flow evidence. The repository has no equivalent Flannel
manifest set or recorded fallback proof, so “CNI-neutral Core” must not be read
as “secured Flannel profile available.”

## Capability Grants

Network access does not authorize a plugin operation.
A stage lease contains explicit capability grants.

A grant names the capability, its selected provider, and resource constraints.
Examples include allowed repository roots, artifact namespaces, secret names, agents, and network origins.

The plugin context denies a capability that has no grant.
The authorization code then checks the requested resource against the grant.

**Why this design exists:** A review plugin needs repository read access.
It does not need repository write access or every secret.

**Cost:** Each new operation needs a defined capability, constraints, an adapter, and platform configuration.
This work is intentional security review, not incidental wiring.

> **Source evidence — least authority**
>
> **Claim:** A leased capability grant constrains each invocation independently of network reachability.
>
> **Implementation:** Context grant lookup and authorization predicates below validate permitted resources.
>
>
> [`createPluginInvocationContext()` creates the grant map and denies missing grants](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/nova/core/execution/context.ts#L34-L58).
>
> [Capability authorization checks paths, namespaces, names, targets, and sources](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/nova/core/execution/authorization.ts#L39-L93) and [checks origins, commands, and signals](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/nova/core/execution/authorization.ts#L94-L130).
>
> **Contract or setting:** Paths, namespaces, names, targets, origins, commands and signals must satisfy the selected grant.
>
> **Test evidence:** No fresh missing-grant or out-of-range resource rejection test execution is claimed here.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`. Source bindings, not execution receipts.
>
> **Limit:** A configured adapter or reachable endpoint does not expand the granted operation/resource range.
>

## Process Isolation

Trusted first-party registrations can load in the host process after import audit and digest checks.
An external stage or observer runs through the isolation runner.

The isolated process receives a bounded context protocol.
It requests capabilities through the parent instead of obtaining host authority.
The runner limits readable paths and disables native add-ons.

External capability adapters need a persistent isolated adapter runtime.
The current activation path rejects them without that boundary.

Native Worker Core adds another process boundary.
It writes admission before launch, applies host resource limits, captures bounded output, and seals the result.

**Why this design exists:** A manifest declaration is not a process sandbox.
The runtime must also constrain how untrusted code reaches the host.

> **Source evidence — trust-dependent activation**
>
> **Claim:** Package trust selects direct import or bounded isolation; external adapters require their own persistent boundary.
>
> **Implementation:** Activation loading and isolation-runner policy below define the selected execution path.
>
>
> [`load()` selects direct import or isolated invocation from the package trust scope](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/registry/activation.ts#L47-L100).
>
> [The isolation runner grants only selected file reads and disables add-ons](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/isolation/runner.ts#L33-L52).
>
> **Contract or setting:** Selected file-read permissions, disabled add-ons, import audit and package integrity limit different forms of execution.
>
> **Test evidence:** No fresh malicious-package or host-isolation exercise ran for this source summary.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`. Source bindings, not execution receipts.
>
> **Limit:** A manifest alone is not a sandbox; trusted in-process code still shares host authority.

## Storage Boundaries

The main durable stores have different owners and recovery needs.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Nova[Nova] --> NovaStore[(Run snapshots, journals, signals, and imports)]
    Buster[Buster] --> BusterStore[(Jobs, source archives, results, and evidence)]
    Control[Prism Control] --> Database[(PostgreSQL state)]
    Control --> Artifacts[(Content-addressed artifact PVC)]
    Worker[Prism Worker] --> Native[(Native ownership and process journal)]
    Roles[Applicable role deployments] --> OpenClaw[(OpenClaw state PVCs)]
    Database --> Backup[Matched Prism backup group]
    Artifacts --> Backup
    Backup --> Restore[Restore and digest verification]
    Restore --> Database
    Restore --> Artifacts
```

Text version: Nova owns its run records, and Buster owns its remote-job and evidence records.
Prism Control owns relational state and content-addressed artifacts.
Prism Worker keeps separate native ownership and process records.
Applicable role deployments also keep separate OpenClaw state.
Prism backup and restore must treat its database and artifacts as one matched group.
Restore verification must complete before Prism enables new writes.

The Prism artifact PVC uses `ReadWriteOnce`.
The current chart therefore requires one Control replica.
This protects one-writer behavior but creates a Control availability limit.

Backups must keep the Prism database and content-addressed artifacts as one recovery group.
Database-only restore can create references to missing artifacts.

>

>

>

>

## Observability Boundary

Nova writes canonical lifecycle events before observers deliver derived views.
Observers can send telemetry, notifications, or agent event records.
They cannot rewrite the lifecycle journal.

Delivery can fail after the lifecycle event is durable.
The observability layer therefore tracks delivery attempts separately.
An observer failure must not create a second pipeline authority.

Logs help diagnosis, but a raw log does not prove a lifecycle transition.
Use the ordered event, effect receipt, artifact digest, or remote result record as authoritative evidence.

> **Source evidence — committed events before delivery**
>
> **Claim:** Observers project committed events without becoming a second lifecycle authority.
>
> **Implementation:** The prepared runner and serialized observer drainer below separate pipeline state from event delivery.
>
>
> [`executePrepared()` creates a serialized observer drainer around the pipeline runner](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/nova/core/execution/engine-run.ts#L21-L34).
>
> [ADR-011 explains immutable observer input and independent delivery](../decisions/core-and-plugins.md#adr-011-observers-consume-immutable-events-without-lifecycle-mutation).
>
> **Contract or setting:** Committed event identity and owner-specific observer delivery state govern replay, not raw diagnostic logs.
>
> **Test evidence:** No fresh observer-outage or delivery-recovery execution is established by these links.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`. Source bindings, not execution receipts.
>
> **Limit:** Delivery failure does not erase canonical events or authorize manufacturing lifecycle history.
>

## Failure Domains

One failure does not always stop every surface.
The table shows the expected boundary.

| Failure | Direct effect | What remains available | Required response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nova process stops | No new canonical pipeline decisions. | Durable run records and independent services. | Recover the same run from pinned state. |
| Buster stops during a job | Test outcome can remain unknown. | Nova journal and other independent stages. | Reconnect by job identity; do not submit a changed duplicate. |
| Prism Control stops | Studio operations and worker coordination stop. | Stored database and artifacts, if storage is healthy. | Restore Control and reconcile operation records. |
| Prism agent bridge or OpenClaw stops before claim | Accepted job remains in PostgreSQL. | Control, Studio, native Worker, and the unclaimed job. | Restore the agent Pod and let one runner claim the same job. |
| Prism agent bridge or OpenClaw stops after claim | External outcome can be unknown; job becomes `needs_nova` at expiry or errored completion. | Control's job, fence, request digest, and any already committed result. | Reconcile the job and fenced result. Do not launch a replacement agent automatically. |
| Prism Worker stops | Native Prism attempt can be interrupted. | Control state, Studio, and stored artifacts. | Use Worker Core ownership and journal recovery. |
| Prism PostgreSQL stops | Prism state operations and new agent admission stop. | Nova, Buster, and any durable off-database evidence. | Restore the matched Prism database and artifact recovery group before Prism work. |
| LiteLLM PostgreSQL or LiteLLM stops | OpenClaw memory embedding fails. | Agent session, Control state, and reasoning route can remain separate. | Restore gateway state and credentials, then prove one authenticated embedding. |
| Managed OpenAI route stops | The affected OpenClaw reasoning step can remain incomplete or have an uncertain external result. | Control's durable job, Nova's journal, and already committed domain state. | Reconcile the same agent session or job; repair provider access; prove one bounded model request before new work. |
| Discord stops | Enabled bot entry, replies, approvals, or webhook notices can stop. | Core execution and every durable owner store. | Restore the exact bot or webhook identity and target. Prove the affected path without inferring pipeline state from message delivery. |
| Prism Ingestion stops | New corpus acquisition and cleanup stop. | Existing active corpus and other Prism operations. | Reconcile quarantine and inactive revision state before resubmission. |
| Artifact PVC fails | Prism content becomes unavailable. | Relational records can remain. | Restore the matched database-and-artifact backup group. |
| SPIRE or Envoy fails | Protected worker routes fail closed. | Local durable state and unrelated public paths. | Restore identity service and verify exact peer routes. |
| Observer destination fails | Derived telemetry becomes delayed. | Canonical lifecycle journal. | Replay durable observer delivery. |
| Redis fails | Configured transport and status projections can stop. | File-backed canonical Nova state. | Restore Redis and reconcile projections; do not infer lifecycle loss. |

## Infrastructure Dependency Order

The safe order follows data and identity dependencies.

1. Provide Kubernetes, storage classes, DNS, and Cilium policy enforcement for
   the current supported secured deployment.
2. Provide required secrets without placing secret values in documentation or logs.
3. Provide SPIRE, its CSI driver, and workload registration when worker trust is enabled.
4. Provide shared data services, such as Redis and PostgreSQL.
5. Run database migration and storage preparation jobs.
6. Deploy Prism Control, Worker, optional Ingestion, and its database migration.
7. Deploy the Prism OpenClaw agent and its bridge, then Nova and Buster roles.
8. Wait for application and Envoy readiness.
9. Verify permitted and denied identity paths, including both Prism mTLS hops.
10. Verify durable writes, one fenced Prism result, and restore inputs.
11. Enable independent user entry only after internal checks succeed.

**Why this order exists:** An application can look ready before its identity sidecar or durable store is ready.
The ordered checks prevent that partial state from becoming an acceptance claim.

## Independent Access

Operator and human access must not depend on an active agent conversation.
Prism Studio uses a private Tailscale route in the complete showcase topology.
Operational access uses its own controlled path and credentials.

This separation helps during an incident.
An operator can inspect or repair the platform when a specialist runtime is unavailable.

Independent access is not anonymous access.
The entry route still needs human authentication, authorization, and network controls.

## Current Limits

- Live SPIRE, mTLS, and denial proof remains a separate acceptance scope.
- Prism results do not currently use durable Ed25519 artifact provenance.
- A runtime role does not prove activation or reachability in a target cluster.
- Prism Control currently has a single-replica limit for its `ReadWriteOnce` artifact volume.
- Some Buster native-runner and fixture-lifetime integration remains in the open implementation issues.
- The operations track supplies backup, restore, upgrade, incident, and daily-operation procedures.

## Continue With Operations

- [Pipeline Dependencies](pipeline-dependencies.md) explains every direct and conditional pipeline service.
- [Platform and Operations Architecture](platform-and-operations.md) explains the surrounding platform and optional operations tool.
- [Operate Worker Trust](../use/worker-trust.md) gives the deployment and live proof procedure.
- [Operate KubeClaw](../use/README.md) is the operations entry point.
- [Current status](../status/current.md) separates source implementation from live acceptance.
- [Open issues](../status/open-issues.md) lists remaining implementation work.
- [Request, State, and Recovery](request-state-recovery.md) explains how these failures affect a run.

## Purpose

This page maps the software boundaries to running workloads.
It explains identity, network, storage, permissions, observability, and failure domains.

It does not treat supporting services as an unnamed infrastructure box.
[Pipeline Dependencies](pipeline-dependencies.md) explains the Git, Redis, PostgreSQL, BuildKit, registry, mirror, and Tailscale paths.
[Platform and Operations Architecture](platform-and-operations.md) explains K3s, Cilium, Argo CD, and the optional Ops Pod.

A rendered chart proves intended Kubernetes resources.
It does not prove that a live cluster applies or enforces them.
Use the linked operations checks for that proof.

## Deployment Map

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    User[Human user] -->|private application route| Studio[Prism Studio]
    Studio -->|HTTP 8080| Control[Prism Control]
    Nova[Nova role] -->|Envoy and SPIFFE mTLS| Buster[Buster role]
    Nova -->|loopback Envoy 28080 and SPIFFE mTLS| AgentProxy[Prism agent Envoy 18082]
    AgentProxy -->|loopback 18080| Bridge[Prism agent bridge]
    Bridge -->|loopback Envoy 28080 and SPIFFE mTLS| Control
    Bridge -->|durable job launch| OpenClaw[Prism OpenClaw gateway]
    OpenClaw -->|fenced tool result| Control
    OpenClaw -->|memory embedding| LiteLLM[LiteLLM]
    LiteLLM -->|provider request| Vertex[Vertex AI]
    OpenClaw -->|managed reasoning| OpenAI[OpenAI provider]
    Control -->|Envoy and SPIFFE mTLS| PWorker[Prism Worker]
    Control -->|bearer HTTP| Ingestion[Optional Prism Ingestion]
    Control --> DB[(Prism PostgreSQL)]
    Control --> Artifacts[(Prism artifact PVC)]
    Nova --> RunStore[(Nova run storage)]
    Buster --> BStore[(Buster job and evidence storage)]
    Discord[Discord users and service] -->|enabled bot channels| Nova
    Discord -->|enabled bot channels| Buster
    Nova -. event delivery .-> Telemetry[Telemetry and observers]
```

Text version: Nova calls Buster through its protected route. For Prism, Nova
first reaches the `agent-prism` Envoy and loopback bridge. The bridge reaches
Control through a second protected route. Control persists an agent job before
the bridge launches OpenClaw. OpenClaw commits a fenced result back to Control.
Studio calls Control through the application route. Control can call the native
Worker, optional Ingestion workload, and Prism PostgreSQL.
The selected SPIFFE Worker does not construct the HMAC nonce database.
The separate HMAC mode uses PostgreSQL for authentication nonces and readiness. The Prism OpenClaw
gateway can call LiteLLM for memory embeddings. Nova, Buster, Prism, OpenClaw,
and LiteLLM keep different owner state. Observers receive committed events only
after Nova writes them. Managed OpenAI reasoning, Vertex embeddings through
LiteLLM, and the enabled Nova and Buster Discord channels are external paths;
none of them owns pipeline or Prism state.

## Runtime Roles and Workloads

A runtime role is a packaging boundary.
It declares the packages and plugins available to one purpose.

| Role or workload | Main responsibility | Included authority | Excluded authority |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nova role | Compile and control pipeline runs. | Lifecycle state, stage leases, configured adapters. | Worker execution semantics and specialist judgment. |
| Buster role | Run fixed test plans. | Test providers, evidence, Worker Core controls. | Canonical pipeline decisions. |
| Prism role | Host the OpenClaw Prism integration. | Prism engine and selected shared adapters. | Nova lifecycle authority. |
| Prism Control | Own Prism operations and durable application state. | Revision, operation, approval, and artifact coordination. | Native host process authority. |
| Prism Worker | Run bounded native Prism operations. | Worker Core attempt and process controls. | Product approval and public entry. |
| Prism Studio | Give humans the application interface. | User-facing requests through Control. | Direct database or worker authority. |
| Prism Ingestion | Fetch and quarantine optional external input. | Narrow outbound fetch path. | Control state ownership. |
| PostgreSQL | Store Prism relational state. | Database persistence only. | Pipeline and product decisions. |
| Prism agent bridge | Translate authenticated dispatch into a durable Control request and run one claimed OpenClaw job. | The claimed job ID, fence, and local process lifecycle. | Prism documents, approval, and Nova lifecycle authority. |
| Prism OpenClaw gateway | Perform the external design-agent session and expose fenced Prism tools. | Its gateway session, configured model route, and tool invocation. | Durable Control job/result authority. |
| LiteLLM | Supply the configured OpenClaw memory embedding route. | Gateway routing and its separate database state. | Agent reasoning route, Prism state, and pipeline lifecycle. |
| Managed OpenAI provider | Supply the model selected by an OpenClaw agent session. | Provider response and external account controls. | OpenClaw session, Control job, and pipeline lifecycle authority. |
| Discord | Carry enabled Nova and Buster bot traffic and configured webhook notifications. | External message transport and Discord account controls. | User authorization beyond configured allowlists, pipeline state, and domain results. |

Forge and Echo do not appear as current role manifests.
Nova reaches them through configured runtime dispatch.
Their actual process location depends on that runtime configuration.
