## Why Role Bundles Exist

A single large image could contain every engine and plugin.
That image would make accidental authority easier and review harder.

Role bundles make the intended content explicit.
Nova does not need the Buster engine to control a Buster job.
Buster does not need Nova Core to execute a test provider.

The bundle is only the first limit.
Activation selects a smaller set of registrations.
Capability grants reduce each invocation again.
Network policy and workload identity limit process-to-process access.

These limits overlap on purpose.
One incorrect setting must not silently grant every other permission.

## Four Independent Trust Questions

Before one component trusts another, it asks four questions.

1. **Who connected?** SPIFFE gives the workload an identity.
2. **Was the route protected?** Envoy authenticates and encrypts the connection with mutual TLS.
3. **May this identity call this service?** Worker code checks the exact expected SPIFFE ID.
4. **Can packets reach the port?** Kubernetes NetworkPolicy limits pods, namespaces, and ports.

Nova-to-Buster source transfer adds another question:
does this archive match the source identity that Nova signed?

**Historical reason:** Unknown. **Current rationale (inference):** Network
location is not an identity. A Pod IP can change, and another Pod can exist in
the same namespace. Exact workload identity plus application authorization
keeps those cases distinct.

**Cost:** SPIRE, its CSI driver, Envoy configuration, and network-policy enforcement become service dependencies.
Protected routes fail closed when those dependencies fail.

**Status and reconsideration:** The secured chart profile contains the SPIFFE
and Envoy path. Live issuance and denial remain separate acceptance.
Reconsider the layers only if a replacement proves exact workload identity,
encrypted peer authentication, application allowlists, rotation, and both
positive and negative route behavior without trusting a caller-supplied header.

> **Source evidence — application identity check**
>
> **Claim:** Application identity checks require trusted proxy origin and an exact allowed workload peer.
>
> **Implementation:** Worker trust and separate configured Prism caller identities below define this application boundary.
>
>
> [Worker Core parses and authorizes proxied SPIFFE identities](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/worker/core/worker/trust.ts#L1-L52).
>
> [Prism workloads receive separate trusted caller identities](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/charts/prism/templates/workloads.yaml#L127-L138).
>
> [Worker Trust gives the complete certificate and proxy path](worker-trust.md).
>
> **Contract or setting:** A valid forwarded URI still requires loopback origin and membership in the selected allowlist.
>
> **Test evidence:** No live forged-header, missing-SVID or wrong-peer rejection is established by these source links.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`. Source bindings, not execution receipts.
>
> **Limit:** A caller-supplied identity header or valid unrelated SVID cannot grant service authority.
>

## Identity Boundaries

Each Prism workload has its own Kubernetes ServiceAccount.
The chart disables automatic service-account token mounting.
SPIRE derives the workload identity from namespace and ServiceAccount.

The expected identity has this form:

```text
spiffe://kubeclaw.internal/ns/<namespace>/sa/<service-account>
```

The application cannot select another identity through a normal environment variable.
Envoy receives the short-lived certificate from the SPIRE Workload API.

Human identity remains separate. Keycloak is an unimplemented architectural
option: this repository does not deploy it, configure a client, connect Prism
session exchange to it, or provide a live acceptance procedure. If a future
deployment selects Keycloak, it could authenticate a human and supply
application roles; it still would not provide workload identity or artifact
signatures. Current operators must use only the implemented human-authentication
path described by the selected application procedure.

> **Source evidence — separate service accounts**
>
> **Claim:** Prism workloads use separate ServiceAccounts for their declared responsibilities.
>
> **Implementation:** The account template below declares the Control, Studio, Worker, Ingestion, Backup and test-runner identities.
>
>
> [The Prism chart creates Control, Studio, Worker, Ingestion, Backup, and test-runner accounts](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/charts/prism/templates/serviceaccounts.yaml#L1-L7).
>
> **Contract or setting:** Namespace/ServiceAccount identity feeds workload attestation; human authentication remains a separate application path.
>
> **Test evidence:** No deployed account selection or SVID issuance test execution is established by this template.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`. Source bindings, not execution receipts.
>
> **Limit:** An account declaration does not deploy Keycloak, grant human roles or prove token isolation.
>

## Network Boundaries

The Prism chart first denies ingress and egress for its named workloads.
It then adds only the required paths.

Important paths include:

| Caller | Destination | Port or route | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Prism Studio | Prism Control | HTTP 8080 | Human application actions. |
| Nova | Prism agent Envoy | Nova loopback 28080 to agent Service 8080 and Envoy 18082 | Authenticate and deliver design dispatch to the loopback bridge. |
| Prism agent bridge and OpenClaw tool | Prism Control | Agent loopback 28080 to Control mTLS Service 8443 | Persist dispatch, claim jobs, and commit fenced designs or revisions. |
| Prism Control | Prism Worker | mTLS service 8443 when enabled | Bounded native operation. |
| Prism Control and Worker | PostgreSQL | TCP 5432 | Prism state. |
| Prism Control | Prism Ingestion | HTTP 8080 | Optional controlled ingestion. |
| Prism Ingestion | Approved external source | HTTPS 443 only | Bounded acquisition into temporary quarantine. |
| Prism OpenClaw agent | LiteLLM | HTTP 4000 | Remote memory-search embeddings only. |
| LiteLLM | Vertex AI | HTTPS 443 | The configured `gemini-embedding-001` route and no reasoning traffic. |
| Nova, Buster, and Prism OpenClaw | Managed OpenAI provider | External HTTPS owned by the pinned OpenClaw runtime | Agent reasoning under the configured model allowlist. |
| Discord service | Nova and Buster OpenClaw gateways | External bot gateway and HTTPS APIs | Enabled allowlisted human messages and bot replies. |
| Nova or Buster notification path | Discord webhook | Secret-selected HTTPS destination | Optional notification delivery; never lifecycle authority. |
| Nova | Buster | mTLS worker route | Plan submission, status, result, evidence, cancellation. |

The Service sends protected traffic to the Envoy sidecar.
The sidecar sends accepted local traffic to the application port.
The runtime port is not the public worker endpoint.

Prism Studio is different.
It is an application entry point and can use a private Tailscale ingress.
It does not use the internal worker route for browser traffic.

The checked-in policy set and Hubble observation path require Cilium in the
current supported secured deployment. The architecture does not bind Nova Core
to Cilium, but the repository has no implemented and proved Flannel equivalent
for these policies. Do not label Flannel as a supported secured fallback until
positive and negative route tests pass with equivalent policy and evidence.

This statement has two evidence levels. The repository proves that selected
manifests contain Cilium resources, that installation checks target Cilium, and
that Ops can query Hubble. It does not prove that a particular live cluster
enforces a deny rule. That proof needs an allowed request, a denied request, and
the matching live flow evidence. The repository has no equivalent Flannel
manifest set or recorded fallback proof, so “CNI-neutral Core” must not be read
as “secured Flannel profile available.”

> **Source evidence — default deny and allowed paths**
>
> **Claim:** Selected Prism policies separate default deny, DNS and explicit application/service routes.
>
> **Implementation:** Policy and Service definitions below bind callers, destinations, ports and the protected sidecar target.
>
>
> [The Prism default-deny and DNS policies](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/charts/prism/templates/networkpolicy.yaml#L1-L22).
>
> [The Prism application paths name allowed callers, destinations, and ports](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/charts/prism/templates/networkpolicy.yaml#L24-L59).
>
> [Internal Prism services target the mTLS sidecar port](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/charts/prism/templates/services.yaml#L8-L29).
>
> [The Prism agent policy permits dispatch, Control, LiteLLM, and managed-provider paths](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/charts/prism/templates/networkpolicy.yaml#L95-L121).
>
> [Optional Ingestion permits only Control ingress and public HTTPS egress](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/charts/prism/templates/networkpolicy.yaml#L150-L165).
>
> **Contract or setting:** Cilium enforcement and matching positive/negative route evidence remain prerequisites for the supported secured deployment.
>
> **Test evidence:** No live deny/allow matrix or equivalent Flannel enforcement exercise is established by these manifests.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`. Historical policy excerpt; current source also adds Redis egress.
>
> **Limit:** The historical policy excerpt is not the current full egress set or live enforcement proof.
>

**Decision status:** A CNI-neutral application boundary is an architecture
direction; Cilium is the implemented and currently supported secured deployment.
**Historical reason:** Unknown. **Current rationale (inference):** Cilium supplies
the checked-in identity-aware policies and Hubble evidence. The cost is a larger
platform dependency and a guarded CNI lifecycle. Reconsider Cilium only after a
replacement enforces the complete route matrix and supplies equivalent incident
evidence in live positive-and-negative tests.

## Capability Grants

Network access does not authorize a plugin operation.
A stage lease contains explicit capability grants.

A grant names the capability, its selected provider, and resource constraints.
Examples include allowed repository roots, artifact namespaces, secret names, agents, and network origins.

The plugin context denies a capability that has no grant.
The authorization code then checks the requested resource against the grant.

**Why this design exists:** A review plugin needs repository read access.
It does not need repository write access or every secret.

**Cost:** Each new operation needs a defined capability, constraints, an adapter, and platform configuration.
This work is intentional security review, not incidental wiring.

> **Source evidence — least authority**
>
> **Claim:** A leased capability grant constrains each invocation independently of network reachability.
>
> **Implementation:** Context grant lookup and authorization predicates below validate permitted resources.
>
>
> [`createPluginInvocationContext()` creates the grant map and denies missing grants](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/nova/core/execution/context.ts#L34-L58).
>
> [Capability authorization checks paths, namespaces, names, targets, and sources](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/nova/core/execution/authorization.ts#L39-L93) and [checks origins, commands, and signals](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/nova/core/execution/authorization.ts#L94-L130).
>
> **Contract or setting:** Paths, namespaces, names, targets, origins, commands and signals must satisfy the selected grant.
>
> **Test evidence:** No fresh missing-grant or out-of-range resource rejection test execution is claimed here.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`. Source bindings, not execution receipts.
>
> **Limit:** A configured adapter or reachable endpoint does not expand the granted operation/resource range.
>

## Process Isolation

Trusted first-party registrations can load in the host process after import audit and digest checks.
An external stage or observer runs through the isolation runner.

The isolated process receives a bounded context protocol.
It requests capabilities through the parent instead of obtaining host authority.
The runner limits readable paths and disables native add-ons.

External capability adapters need a persistent isolated adapter runtime.
The current activation path rejects them without that boundary.

Native Worker Core adds another process boundary.
It writes admission before launch, applies host resource limits, captures bounded output, and seals the result.

**Why this design exists:** A manifest declaration is not a process sandbox.
The runtime must also constrain how untrusted code reaches the host.

> **Source evidence — trust-dependent activation**
>
> **Claim:** Package trust selects direct import or bounded isolation; external adapters require their own persistent boundary.
>
> **Implementation:** Activation loading and isolation-runner policy below define the selected execution path.
>
>
> [`load()` selects direct import or isolated invocation from the package trust scope](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/registry/activation.ts#L47-L100).
>
> [The isolation runner grants only selected file reads and disables add-ons](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/isolation/runner.ts#L33-L52).
>
> **Contract or setting:** Selected file-read permissions, disabled add-ons, import audit and package integrity limit different forms of execution.
>
> **Test evidence:** No fresh malicious-package or host-isolation exercise ran for this source summary.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`. Source bindings, not execution receipts.
>
> **Limit:** A manifest alone is not a sandbox; trusted in-process code still shares host authority.
>

## Storage Boundaries

The main durable stores have different owners and recovery needs.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Nova[Nova] --> NovaStore[(Run snapshots, journals, signals, and imports)]
    Buster[Buster] --> BusterStore[(Jobs, source archives, results, and evidence)]
    Control[Prism Control] --> Database[(PostgreSQL state)]
    Control --> Artifacts[(Content-addressed artifact PVC)]
    Worker[Prism Worker] --> Native[(Native ownership and process journal)]
    Roles[Applicable role deployments] --> OpenClaw[(OpenClaw state PVCs)]
    Database --> Backup[Matched Prism backup group]
    Artifacts --> Backup
    Backup --> Restore[Restore and digest verification]
    Restore --> Database
    Restore --> Artifacts
```

Text version: Nova owns its run records, and Buster owns its remote-job and evidence records.
Prism Control owns relational state and content-addressed artifacts.
Prism Worker keeps separate native ownership and process records.
Applicable role deployments also keep separate OpenClaw state.
Prism backup and restore must treat its database and artifacts as one matched group.
Restore verification must complete before Prism enables new writes.

**Text alternative to the diagram**

Each row names a directed connection. Labels preserve the diagram’s conditions or handoffs; dotted relationships are identified explicitly.

| From | Relationship | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nova | Directed connection | Run snapshots, journals, signals, and imports |
| Buster | Directed connection | Jobs, source archives, results, and evidence |
| Prism Control | Directed connection | PostgreSQL state |
| Prism Control | Directed connection | Content-addressed artifact PVC |
| Prism Worker | Directed connection | Native ownership and process journal |
| Applicable role deployments | Directed connection | OpenClaw state PVCs |
| PostgreSQL state | Directed connection | Matched Prism backup group |
| Content-addressed artifact PVC | Directed connection | Matched Prism backup group |
| Matched Prism backup group | Directed connection | Restore and digest verification |
| Restore and digest verification | Directed connection | PostgreSQL state |
| Restore and digest verification | Directed connection | Content-addressed artifact PVC |

| Store | Owner | Data | Failure effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nova run storage | Nova | Snapshots, events, effects, signals, decisions, imports. | Nova cannot safely recover or prove prior authority. |
| Buster runtime storage | Buster | Job admission, source archive, result, and evidence. | Nova can lose remote reconciliation and evidence import. |
| Prism PostgreSQL | Prism Control and bounded clients | Projects, revisions, operations, preferences, and approvals. | Prism cannot reconstruct current application state. |
| Prism artifact PVC | Prism Control | Content-addressed design and operation artifacts. | Database references can point to unavailable content. |
| Prism native host state | Prism Worker supervisor | Ownership, journal, policy, and resource-pool identity. | Native admission must fence rather than guess ownership. |
| OpenClaw state PVC | Each applicable role deployment | Gateway and host-integration state. | Agent sessions and host configuration can fail independently. |

The Prism artifact PVC uses `ReadWriteOnce`.
The current chart therefore requires one Control replica.
This protects one-writer behavior but creates a Control availability limit.

Backups must keep the Prism database and content-addressed artifacts as one recovery group.
Database-only restore can create references to missing artifacts.

> **Source evidence — Prism persistence**
>
> **Claim:** Prism keeps relational state and immutable artifact bytes in one matched recovery group.
>
> **Implementation:** Control replica/PVC rules and backup group construction below define the selected storage boundary.
>
>
> [The chart enforces one Control replica and mounts the artifact PVC only there](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/charts/prism/templates/workloads.yaml#L1-L6).
>
> [The retained artifact PVC uses `ReadWriteOnce`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/charts/prism/templates/workloads.yaml#L217-L230).
>
> [The backup script defines one database-and-artifact group](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/charts/prism/files/prism-backup.sh#L54-L105).
>
> **Contract or setting:** Single Control writer, retained ReadWriteOnce storage and matched database/artifact identities constrain recovery.
>
> **Test evidence:** No deployed volume-loss, matched restore or live application-recovery exercise is established here.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`. Historical backup excerpt; current script additionally gates database readiness.
>
> **Limit:** A PVC declaration or database-only restore cannot prove artifact availability or complete disaster recovery.
>

## Observability Boundary

Nova writes canonical lifecycle events before observers deliver derived views.
Observers can send telemetry, notifications, or agent event records.
They cannot rewrite the lifecycle journal.

Delivery can fail after the lifecycle event is durable.
The observability layer therefore tracks delivery attempts separately.
An observer failure must not create a second pipeline authority.

Logs help diagnosis, but a raw log does not prove a lifecycle transition.
Use the ordered event, effect receipt, artifact digest, or remote result record as authoritative evidence.

> **Source evidence — committed events before delivery**
>
> **Claim:** Observers project committed events without becoming a second lifecycle authority.
>
> **Implementation:** The prepared runner and serialized observer drainer below separate pipeline state from event delivery.
>
>
> [`executePrepared()` creates a serialized observer drainer around the pipeline runner](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/nova/core/execution/engine-run.ts#L21-L34).
>
> [ADR-011 explains immutable observer input and independent delivery](../decisions/core-and-plugins.md#adr-011-observers-consume-immutable-events-without-lifecycle-mutation).
>
> **Contract or setting:** Committed event identity and owner-specific observer delivery state govern replay, not raw diagnostic logs.
>
> **Test evidence:** No fresh observer-outage or delivery-recovery execution is established by these links.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`. Source bindings, not execution receipts.
>
> **Limit:** Delivery failure does not erase canonical events or authorize manufacturing lifecycle history.
>

## Failure Domains

One failure does not always stop every surface.
The table shows the expected boundary.

| Failure | Direct effect | What remains available | Required response |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nova process stops | No new canonical pipeline decisions. | Durable run records and independent services. | Recover the same run from pinned state. |
| Buster stops during a job | Test outcome can remain unknown. | Nova journal and other independent stages. | Reconnect by job identity; do not submit a changed duplicate. |
| Prism Control stops | Studio operations and worker coordination stop. | Stored database and artifacts, if storage is healthy. | Restore Control and reconcile operation records. |
| Prism agent bridge or OpenClaw stops before claim | Accepted job remains in PostgreSQL. | Control, Studio, native Worker, and the unclaimed job. | Restore the agent Pod and let one runner claim the same job. |
| Prism agent bridge or OpenClaw stops after claim | External outcome can be unknown; job becomes `needs_nova` at expiry or errored completion. | Control's job, fence, request digest, and any already committed result. | Reconcile the job and fenced result. Do not launch a replacement agent automatically. |
| Prism Worker stops | Native Prism attempt can be interrupted. | Control state, Studio, and stored artifacts. | Use Worker Core ownership and journal recovery. |
| Prism PostgreSQL stops | Prism state operations and new agent admission stop. | Nova, Buster, and any durable off-database evidence. | Restore the matched Prism database and artifact recovery group before Prism work. |
| LiteLLM PostgreSQL or LiteLLM stops | OpenClaw memory embedding fails. | Agent session, Control state, and reasoning route can remain separate. | Restore gateway state and credentials, then prove one authenticated embedding. |
| Managed OpenAI route stops | The affected OpenClaw reasoning step can remain incomplete or have an uncertain external result. | Control's durable job, Nova's journal, and already committed domain state. | Reconcile the same agent session or job; repair provider access; prove one bounded model request before new work. |
| Discord stops | Enabled bot entry, replies, approvals, or webhook notices can stop. | Core execution and every durable owner store. | Restore the exact bot or webhook identity and target. Prove the affected path without inferring pipeline state from message delivery. |
| Prism Ingestion stops | New corpus acquisition and cleanup stop. | Existing active corpus and other Prism operations. | Reconcile quarantine and inactive revision state before resubmission. |
| Artifact PVC fails | Prism content becomes unavailable. | Relational records can remain. | Restore the matched database-and-artifact backup group. |
| SPIRE or Envoy fails | Protected worker routes fail closed. | Local durable state and unrelated public paths. | Restore identity service and verify exact peer routes. |
| Observer destination fails | Derived telemetry becomes delayed. | Canonical lifecycle journal. | Replay durable observer delivery. |
| Redis fails | Configured transport and status projections can stop. | File-backed canonical Nova state. | Restore Redis and reconcile projections; do not infer lifecycle loss. |

## Infrastructure Dependency Order

The safe order follows data and identity dependencies.

1. Provide Kubernetes, storage classes, DNS, and Cilium policy enforcement for
   the current supported secured deployment.
2. Provide required secrets without placing secret values in documentation or logs.
3. Provide SPIRE, its CSI driver, and workload registration when worker trust is enabled.
4. Provide shared data services, such as Redis and PostgreSQL.
5. Run database migration and storage preparation jobs.
6. Deploy Prism Control, Worker, optional Ingestion, and its database migration.
7. Deploy the Prism OpenClaw agent and its bridge, then Nova and Buster roles.
8. Wait for application and Envoy readiness.
9. Verify permitted and denied identity paths, including both Prism mTLS hops.
10. Verify durable writes, one fenced Prism result, and restore inputs.
11. Enable independent user entry only after internal checks succeed.

**Why this order exists:** An application can look ready before its identity sidecar or durable store is ready.
The ordered checks prevent that partial state from becoming an acceptance claim.

## Independent Access

Operator and human access must not depend on an active agent conversation.
Prism Studio uses a private Tailscale route in the complete showcase topology.
Operational access uses its own controlled path and credentials.

This separation helps during an incident.
An operator can inspect or repair the platform when a specialist runtime is unavailable.

Independent access is not anonymous access.
The entry route still needs human authentication, authorization, and network controls.

## Current Limits

- Live SPIRE, mTLS, and denial proof remains a separate acceptance scope.
- Prism results do not currently use durable Ed25519 artifact provenance.
- A runtime role does not prove activation or reachability in a target cluster.
- Prism Control currently has a single-replica limit for its `ReadWriteOnce` artifact volume.
- Some Buster native-runner and fixture-lifetime integration remains in the open implementation issues.
- The operations track supplies backup, restore, upgrade, incident, and daily-operation procedures.

## Supervised Repository-review Operator Path

Use the root package's `review:supervise`, `review:status`,
`review:status:format` and optional `runtime:preflight` commands for long reviews.
They are operator tools around the existing pipeline, not new review stages or
approval authority. These procedures are Source-reviewed, not newly executed.

### Prepare one owned run and its control files

Start from the supported [locked dependency installation](../use/quickstart.md#locked-dependency-installation).
Use the repository's supported Node runtime with direct TypeScript support,
installed npm dependencies and the root package scripts. Supervision additionally
needs Linux `/proc` and `/usr/bin/flock`. Resource samples use cgroup-v2 files;
unavailable readings are observation errors, not zero resource use. Put `npm`
on the supervisor's `PATH`; its child runs from `--workdir`. The child inherits
the operator environment, including runtime, credential and service selections;
the supervisor does not sanitize or provision it.

Supply a valid explicit platform and pipeline graph. The platform must expose
its `storageRoot` and artifact-store adapter's `artifactRoot` to the status
reader, as well as the actual installed providers, grants and review target
needed by the pipeline. A readable status snapshot does not validate the whole
platform or authorize dispatch. Prepare the frozen repository subject, review
profile, permitted artifact namespaces and configured model/controller identity
before starting. Keep these inputs and the same run ID through recovery.

Choose absolute, operator-owned paths for the platform, graph and control
files. The run ID permits 1–256 characters, starting with a letter or digit;
the remainder can contain letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:`, or `-`. The run-root
reader uses the same ID's SHA-256-based `runs/v2-<digest>` location. The run-root reader accepts a legacy
colon-to-underscore location only with matching journal identity;
do not rename or guess a run directory.

The following placeholders must be replaced with real paths and an admitted
run ID. Create the control directory before opening its append-only pipeline log:

```sh
cd /absolute/path/to/kubeclaw
CONTROL=/absolute/path/to/review-control
PLATFORM=/absolute/path/to/platform.json
GRAPH=/absolute/path/to/repository-review-pipeline.json
RUN_ID=repository-review-001
mkdir -p "$CONTROL"
npm run review:supervise -- \
  --workdir "$PWD" --platform "$PLATFORM" --graph "$GRAPH" \
  --run-id "$RUN_ID" --heartbeat "$CONTROL/heartbeat.json" \
  --resource-log "$CONTROL/resources.jsonl" \
  --diagnostic-dir "$CONTROL/diagnostics" --log "$CONTROL/pipeline.log" \
  --lease "$CONTROL/supervisor.lease" --initial-mode auto --max-recoveries 5
```

All eight path/run options shown before `--lease` are required. The lease
otherwise defaults to `<heartbeat>.lease`; `--max-recoveries` accepts 0–100,
default 5. `auto` starts when no run journal exists and otherwise recovers;
explicit `start` and `recover` are also supported. This tool accepts an explicit
graph, not a project-compilation or human-signal command. Use the separate
[wait/resume workflow](../use/workflows/wait-resume.md) for authorized signals.

Before launching, the supervisor acquires its lease and reads current status.
An already terminal run returns that status without another child. A confirmed
live heartbeat PID is adopted only when its procfs command contains `pipeline`
and the run ID; unreadable or mismatched live ownership stops admission. This
is a process-ownership check, not proof of the repository/model semantics.

The lease uses a stable `<lease>.lock` inode with an exclusive flock transaction
and a one-second lock-acquisition timeout. A live supervisor owner refuses a
contender. Malformed lease JSON or a semantically invalid lease is an error.
Malformed heartbeat JSON also errors, but its reader does not validate a closed
heartbeat schema; none of these errors permits replacing a live owner. A dead lease owner
can be replaced under that lock. A late release cannot remove a successor's
lease because release checks its instance ID. Never unlink the permanent lock
inode to bypass contention.

### Observe, stop and recover without inventing completion

Each new attempt launches detached `npm run pipeline` with the supplied
platform/graph and either `--run-id` or `--recover` for the **same** ID. Its
stdout/stderr append to the log. Initial and 15-second serialized heartbeat
work appends resource samples then atomically replaces the heartbeat. Samples
contain cgroup CPU/memory/OOM counters, pipeline RSS/liveness and a two-second
Gateway `/healthz` probe. The default probe is `http://127.0.0.1:18789`;
`--gateway-url` changes this observation, not the pipeline's transport target.

After actual child exit and queued heartbeat I/O settle, the supervisor writes
a final stopped heartbeat and `diagnostics/attempt-<n>-exit.json` containing the
exit code/signal, stop state, sample and any launch/process/heartbeat error.
Heartbeat or diagnostic failures are visible errors, not successful monitoring.
The diagnostic's child exit is not itself the canonical run outcome.

| Observation or stop | Meaning and safe next action |
| --- | --- |
| Status is `succeeded` | Supervisor prints the status and exits 0. Inspect final report, completeness and subject bindings before claiming review coverage. |
| Status is `failed`, `blocked` or `cancelled` | Prints terminal status and exits 1; it does not automatically reopen that terminal run. Follow its owning error/wait/reconciliation procedure. |
| Child exited but status remains `running` | After a five-second delay it can invoke `--recover` for the same ID, within the declared maximum. Exhaustion exits 75, not success. Preserve log/diagnostic and inspect before another authorized recovery. |
| SIGINT/SIGTERM during a child owned by this supervisor | Requests process-group SIGTERM with child fallback, then waits for actual exit and heartbeat I/O; returns 130. There is no kill-after-grace escalation here. An unresponsive child can keep the supervisor waiting. |
| Stop while observing an adopted live pipeline | Stops supervision; it does not signal that adopted pipeline. Confirm its actual state separately before replacing or recovering it. |
| Lease, status/artifact read, procfs ownership, heartbeat or diagnostic error | Stop; retain the original error and inputs. Correct access/data/path dependencies without deleting locks or rewriting retained evidence to force admission. |

Use read-only observations independently of a supervisor:

```sh
npm run review:status -- --platform "$PLATFORM" --run-id "$RUN_ID" \
  --heartbeat "$CONTROL/heartbeat.json" --resource-log "$CONTROL/resources.jsonl" \
  --stale-after-seconds 120
npm run review:status:format -- --workdir "$PWD" \
  --platform "$PLATFORM" --run-id "$RUN_ID" \
  --heartbeat "$CONTROL/heartbeat.json" --resource-log "$CONTROL/resources.jsonl" \
  --controller-session-key agent:main:nova-review-controller \
  --configured-concurrency 10
```

The status command reads the compact artifact index and referenced prepared,
cache and report blobs. Its event tail is bounded to 1 MiB; resource history is
bounded to 8 MiB. It is not full journal replay or an audit/proof-repair command.
Inspect `status`, stage states, last durable event, `liveness`, heartbeat age,
`health`, active runtime locks, requested dispatches, recent lock expiry/failure,
and primary/expansion/verification checkpoint counts. Heartbeat freshness
(default 120 seconds) and a live-process flag distinguish active from stale;
terminal events override liveness. Tail-derived counts or missing old events
cannot certify full run history. `planReport` is not executed review;
`finalReport` presence does not replace its coverage/completeness checks.

The formatter also invokes the installed `openclaw` CLI against Gateway's

## Supervised Repository-review Operator Path

Use the root package's `review:supervise`, `review:status`,
`review:status:format` and optional `runtime:preflight` commands for long reviews.
They are operator tools around the existing pipeline, not new review stages or
approval authority. These procedures are Source-reviewed, not newly executed.

### Prepare one owned run and its control files

Start from the supported [locked dependency installation](../use/quickstart.md#locked-dependency-installation).
Use the repository's supported Node runtime with direct TypeScript support,
installed npm dependencies and the root package scripts. Supervision additionally
needs Linux `/proc` and `/usr/bin/flock`. Resource samples use cgroup-v2 files;
unavailable readings are observation errors, not zero resource use. Put `npm`
on the supervisor's `PATH`; its child runs from `--workdir`. The child inherits
the operator environment, including runtime, credential and service selections;
the supervisor does not sanitize or provision it.

Supply a valid explicit platform and pipeline graph. The platform must expose
its `storageRoot` and artifact-store adapter's `artifactRoot` to the status
reader, as well as the actual installed providers, grants and review target
needed by the pipeline. A readable status snapshot does not validate the whole
platform or authorize dispatch. Prepare the frozen repository subject, review
profile, permitted artifact namespaces and configured model/controller identity
before starting. Keep these inputs and the same run ID through recovery.

Choose absolute, operator-owned paths for the platform, graph and control
files. The run ID permits 1–256 characters, starting with a letter or digit;
the remainder can contain letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:`, or `-`. The run-root
reader uses the same ID's SHA-256-based `runs/v2-<digest>` location. The run-root reader accepts a legacy
colon-to-underscore location only with matching journal identity;
do not rename or guess a run directory.

The following placeholders must be replaced with real paths and an admitted
run ID. Create the control directory before opening its append-only pipeline log:

```sh
cd /absolute/path/to/kubeclaw
CONTROL=/absolute/path/to/review-control
PLATFORM=/absolute/path/to/platform.json
GRAPH=/absolute/path/to/repository-review-pipeline.json

mkdir -p "$CONTROL"
npm run review:supervise -- \
  --workdir "$PWD" --platform "$PLATFORM" --graph "$GRAPH" \
  --run-id "$RUN_ID" --heartbeat "$CONTROL/heartbeat.json" \
  --resource-log "$CONTROL/resources.jsonl" \
  --diagnostic-dir "$CONTROL/diagnostics" --log "$CONTROL/pipeline.log" \
  --lease "$CONTROL/supervisor.lease" --initial-mode auto --max-recoveries 5
```

otherwise defaults to `<heartbeat>.lease`; `--max-recoveries` accepts 0–100,
default 5. `auto` starts when no run journal exists and otherwise recovers;
explicit `start` and `recover` are also supported. This tool accepts an explicit
graph, not a project-compilation or human-signal command. Use the separate
[wait/resume workflow](../use/workflows/wait-resume.md) for authorized signals.

Before launching, the supervisor acquires its lease and reads current status.
An already terminal run returns that status without another child. A confirmed
live heartbeat PID is adopted only when its procfs command contains `pipeline`
and the run ID; unreadable or mismatched live ownership stops admission. This
is a process-ownership check, not proof of the repository/model semantics.

The lease uses a stable `<lease>.lock` inode with an exclusive flock transaction
and a one-second lock-acquisition timeout. A live supervisor owner refuses a
contender. Malformed lease JSON or a semantically invalid lease is an error.
Malformed heartbeat JSON also errors, but its reader does not validate a closed
heartbeat schema; none of these errors permits replacing a live owner. A dead lease owner
can be replaced under that lock. A late release cannot remove a successor's
lease because release checks its instance ID. Never unlink the permanent lock
inode to bypass contention.

Each new attempt launches detached `npm run pipeline` with the supplied

| --- | --- |

| Stop while observing an adopted live pipeline | Stops supervision; it does not signal that adopted pipeline. Confirm its actual state separately before replacing or recovering it. |

## Supervised Repository-review Operator Path

Use the root package's `review:supervise`, `review:status`,
`review:status:format` and optional `runtime:preflight` commands for long reviews.
They are operator tools around the existing pipeline, not new review stages or
approval authority. These procedures are Source-reviewed, not newly executed.

### Prepare one owned run and its control files

Start from the supported [locked dependency installation](../use/quickstart.md#locked-dependency-installation).
Use the repository's supported Node runtime with direct TypeScript support,
installed npm dependencies and the root package scripts. Supervision additionally
needs Linux `/proc` and `/usr/bin/flock`. Resource samples use cgroup-v2 files;
unavailable readings are observation errors, not zero resource use. Put `npm`
on the supervisor's `PATH`; its child runs from `--workdir`. The child inherits
the operator environment, including runtime, credential and service selections;
the supervisor does not sanitize or provision it.

Supply a valid explicit platform and pipeline graph. The platform must expose
its `storageRoot` and artifact-store adapter's `artifactRoot` to the status
reader, as well as the actual installed providers, grants and review target
needed by the pipeline. A readable status snapshot does not validate the whole
platform or authorize dispatch. Prepare the frozen repository subject, review
profile, permitted artifact namespaces and configured model/controller identity
before starting. Keep these inputs and the same run ID through recovery.

Choose absolute, operator-owned paths for the platform, graph and control
files. The run ID permits 1–256 characters, starting with a letter or digit;
the remainder can contain letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:`, or `-`. The run-root
reader uses the same ID's SHA-256-based `runs/v2-<digest>` location. The run-root reader accepts a legacy
colon-to-underscore location only with matching journal identity;
do not rename or guess a run directory.

The following placeholders must be replaced with real paths and an admitted
run ID. Create the control directory before opening its append-only pipeline log:

```sh
cd /absolute/path/to/kubeclaw
CONTROL=/absolute/path/to/review-control
PLATFORM=/absolute/path/to/platform.json
GRAPH=/absolute/path/to/repository-review-pipeline.json
RUN_ID=repository-review-001
mkdir -p "$CONTROL"
npm run review:supervise -- \
  --workdir "$PWD" --platform "$PLATFORM" --graph "$GRAPH" \
  --run-id "$RUN_ID" --heartbeat "$CONTROL/heartbeat.json" \
  --resource-log "$CONTROL/resources.jsonl" \
  --diagnostic-dir "$CONTROL/diagnostics" --log "$CONTROL/pipeline.log" \
  --lease "$CONTROL/supervisor.lease" --initial-mode auto --max-recoveries 5
```

All eight path/run options shown before `--lease` are required. The lease
otherwise defaults to `<heartbeat>.lease`; `--max-recoveries` accepts 0–100,
default 5. `auto` starts when no run journal exists and otherwise recovers;
explicit `start` and `recover` are also supported. This tool accepts an explicit
graph, not a project-compilation or human-signal command. Use the separate
[wait/resume workflow](../use/workflows/wait-resume.md) for authorized signals.

Before launching, the supervisor acquires its lease and reads current status.
An already terminal run returns that status without another child. A confirmed
live heartbeat PID is adopted only when its procfs command contains `pipeline`
and the run ID; unreadable or mismatched live ownership stops admission. This
is a process-ownership check, not proof of the repository/model semantics.

The lease uses a stable `<lease>.lock` inode with an exclusive flock transaction
and a one-second lock-acquisition timeout. A live supervisor owner refuses a
contender. Malformed lease JSON or a semantically invalid lease is an error.
Malformed heartbeat JSON also errors, but its reader does not validate a closed
heartbeat schema; none of these errors permits replacing a live owner. A dead lease owner
can be replaced under that lock. A late release cannot remove a successor's
lease because release checks its instance ID. Never unlink the permanent lock
inode to bypass contention.

### Observe, stop and recover without inventing completion

Each new attempt launches detached `npm run pipeline` with the supplied
platform/graph and either `--run-id` or `--recover` for the **same** ID. Its
stdout/stderr append to the log. Initial and 15-second serialized heartbeat
work appends resource samples then atomically replaces the heartbeat. Samples
contain cgroup CPU/memory/OOM counters, pipeline RSS/liveness and a two-second
Gateway `/healthz` probe. The default probe is `http://127.0.0.1:18789`;
`--gateway-url` changes this observation, not the pipeline's transport target.

After actual child exit and queued heartbeat I/O settle, the supervisor writes
a final stopped heartbeat and `diagnostics/attempt-<n>-exit.json` containing the
exit code/signal, stop state, sample and any launch/process/heartbeat error.
Heartbeat or diagnostic failures are visible errors, not successful monitoring.
The diagnostic's child exit is not itself the canonical run outcome.

| Observation or stop | Meaning and safe next action |
| --- | --- |
| Status is `succeeded` | Supervisor prints the status and exits 0. Inspect final report, completeness and subject bindings before claiming review coverage. |
| Status is `failed`, `blocked` or `cancelled` | Prints terminal status and exits 1; it does not automatically reopen that terminal run. Follow its owning error/wait/reconciliation procedure. |
| Child exited but status remains `running` | After a five-second delay it can invoke `--recover` for the same ID, within the declared maximum. Exhaustion exits 75, not success. Preserve log/diagnostic and inspect before another authorized recovery. |
| SIGINT/SIGTERM during a child owned by this supervisor | Requests process-group SIGTERM with child fallback, then waits for actual exit and heartbeat I/O; returns 130. There is no kill-after-grace escalation here. An unresponsive child can keep the supervisor waiting. |
| Stop while observing an adopted live pipeline | Stops supervision; it does not signal that adopted pipeline. Confirm its actual state separately before replacing or recovering it. |
| Lease, status/artifact read, procfs ownership, heartbeat or diagnostic error | Stop; retain the original error and inputs. Correct access/data/path dependencies without deleting locks or rewriting retained evidence to force admission. |

```sh

  --heartbeat "$CONTROL/heartbeat.json" --resource-log "$CONTROL/resources.jsonl" \
  --stale-after-seconds 120

  --platform "$PLATFORM" --run-id "$RUN_ID" \
  --heartbeat "$CONTROL/heartbeat.json" --resource-log "$CONTROL/resources.jsonl" \
  --controller-session-key agent:main:nova-review-controller \
  --configured-concurrency 10
```

cache and report blobs. Its event tail is bounded to 1 MiB; resource history is
bounded to 8 MiB. It is not full journal replay or an audit/proof-repair command.

(default 120 seconds) and a live-process flag distinguish active from stale;
terminal events override liveness. Tail-derived counts or missing old events
cannot certify full run history. `planReport` is not executed review;
`finalReport` presence does not replace its coverage/completeness checks.

review target. `--openclaw-bin` selects another executable; the tool does not
create credentials. Its displayed configured concurrency (default 10) is a
label, not a control change. Active tasks/locks are observations, not completed
batches. Actual reviewer token usage remains explicitly unavailable; estimated
input tokens and budget reservations are not billed usage.

cadence/next-check text does not install a scheduler. Optional `--reopen-status`

agent/model/thinking selection and sufficient controller capacity. It can incur
model work and retain child sessions. Use it only when this live check is
intended; it is not free static parsing or a prerequisite for reading status.

  --collector-mode true --spawn-interval-ms 1500 --timeout-ms 180000

`cleanup: keep` and no thread; collector mode additionally selects collect and

submits concurrently; a positive interval spaces spawn requests. The prompt

completed counts and selected identity. It exits without error only after admission and successful terminal observation
of every requested child. Admission

task IDs from a list and using settled cancellation requests. Cancellation is
not terminal cleanup proof; list/transport failure can also obstruct cleanup.

Choose absolute, operator-owned paths for the platform, graph and control
files. The run ID permits 1–256 characters, starting with a letter or digit;
the remainder can contain letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `:`, or `-`. The run-root
reader uses the same ID's SHA-256-based `runs/v2-<digest>` location. The run-root reader accepts a legacy
colon-to-underscore location only with matching journal identity;
do not rename or guess a run directory.

The following placeholders must be replaced with real paths and an admitted
run ID. Create the control directory before opening its append-only pipeline log:

```sh
cd /absolute/path/to/kubeclaw
CONTROL=/absolute/path/to/review-control
PLATFORM=/absolute/path/to/platform.json
GRAPH=/absolute/path/to/repository-review-pipeline.json
RUN_ID=repository-review-001
mkdir -p "$CONTROL"
npm run review:supervise -- \
  --workdir "$PWD" --platform "$PLATFORM" --graph "$GRAPH" \
  --run-id "$RUN_ID" --heartbeat "$CONTROL/heartbeat.json" \
  --resource-log "$CONTROL/resources.jsonl" \
  --diagnostic-dir "$CONTROL/diagnostics" --log "$CONTROL/pipeline.log" \
  --lease "$CONTROL/supervisor.lease" --initial-mode auto --max-recoveries 5
```

All eight path/run options shown before `--lease` are required. The lease
otherwise defaults to `<heartbeat>.lease`; `--max-recoveries` accepts 0–100,
default 5. `auto` starts when no run journal exists and otherwise recovers;
explicit `start` and `recover` are also supported. This tool accepts an explicit
graph, not a project-compilation or human-signal command. Use the separate
[wait/resume workflow](../use/workflows/wait-resume.md) for authorized signals.

Before launching, the supervisor acquires its lease and reads current status.
An already terminal run returns that status without another child. A confirmed
live heartbeat PID is adopted only when its procfs command contains `pipeline`
and the run ID; unreadable or mismatched live ownership stops admission. This
is a process-ownership check, not proof of the repository/model semantics.

The lease uses a stable `<lease>.lock` inode with an exclusive flock transaction
and a one-second lock-acquisition timeout. A live supervisor owner refuses a
contender. Malformed lease JSON or a semantically invalid lease is an error.
Malformed heartbeat JSON also errors, but its reader does not validate a closed
heartbeat schema; none of these errors permits replacing a live owner. A dead lease owner
can be replaced under that lock. A late release cannot remove a successor's
lease because release checks its instance ID. Never unlink the permanent lock
inode to bypass contention.

### Observe, stop and recover without inventing completion

Each new attempt launches detached `npm run pipeline` with the supplied
platform/graph and either `--run-id` or `--recover` for the **same** ID. Its
stdout/stderr append to the log. Initial and 15-second serialized heartbeat
work appends resource samples then atomically replaces the heartbeat. Samples
contain cgroup CPU/memory/OOM counters, pipeline RSS/liveness and a two-second
Gateway `/healthz` probe. The default probe is `http://127.0.0.1:18789`;
`--gateway-url` changes this observation, not the pipeline's transport target.

After actual child exit and queued heartbeat I/O settle, the supervisor writes
a final stopped heartbeat and `diagnostics/attempt-<n>-exit.json` containing the
exit code/signal, stop state, sample and any launch/process/heartbeat error.
Heartbeat or diagnostic failures are visible errors, not successful monitoring.
The diagnostic's child exit is not itself the canonical run outcome.

| Observation or stop | Meaning and safe next action |
| --- | --- |
| Status is `succeeded` | Supervisor prints the status and exits 0. Inspect final report, completeness and subject bindings before claiming review coverage. |
| Status is `failed`, `blocked` or `cancelled` | Prints terminal status and exits 1; it does not automatically reopen that terminal run. Follow its owning error/wait/reconciliation procedure. |
| Child exited but status remains `running` | After a five-second delay it can invoke `--recover` for the same ID, within the declared maximum. Exhaustion exits 75, not success. Preserve log/diagnostic and inspect before another authorized recovery. |
| SIGINT/SIGTERM during a child owned by this supervisor | Requests process-group SIGTERM with child fallback, then waits for actual exit and heartbeat I/O; returns 130. There is no kill-after-grace escalation here. An unresponsive child can keep the supervisor waiting. |
| Stop while observing an adopted live pipeline | Stops supervision; it does not signal that adopted pipeline. Confirm its actual state separately before replacing or recovering it. |
| Lease, status/artifact read, procfs ownership, heartbeat or diagnostic error | Stop; retain the original error and inputs. Correct access/data/path dependencies without deleting locks or rewriting retained evidence to force admission. |

Use read-only observations independently of a supervisor:

```sh
npm run review:status -- --platform "$PLATFORM" --run-id "$RUN_ID" \
  --heartbeat "$CONTROL/heartbeat.json" --resource-log "$CONTROL/resources.jsonl" \
  --stale-after-seconds 120
npm run review:status:format -- --workdir "$PWD" \
  --platform "$PLATFORM" --run-id "$RUN_ID" \
  --heartbeat "$CONTROL/heartbeat.json" --resource-log "$CONTROL/resources.jsonl" \
  --controller-session-key agent:main:nova-review-controller \
  --configured-concurrency 10
```

The status command reads the compact artifact index and referenced prepared,
cache and report blobs. Its event tail is bounded to 1 MiB; resource history is
bounded to 8 MiB. It is not full journal replay or an audit/proof-repair command.
Inspect `status`, stage states, last durable event, `liveness`, heartbeat age,
`health`, active runtime locks, requested dispatches, recent lock expiry/failure,
and primary/expansion/verification checkpoint counts. Heartbeat freshness
(default 120 seconds) and a live-process flag distinguish active from stale;
terminal events override liveness. Tail-derived counts or missing old events
cannot certify full run history. `planReport` is not executed review;
`finalReport` presence does not replace its coverage/completeness checks.

The formatter also invokes the installed `openclaw` CLI against Gateway's
`subagents` list for the specified controller session. Configure that CLI's
actual Gateway connection/authentication and select the controller used by the
review target. `--openclaw-bin` selects another executable; the tool does not
create credentials. Its displayed configured concurrency (default 10) is a
label, not a control change. Active tasks/locks are observations, not completed
batches. Actual reviewer token usage remains explicitly unavailable; estimated
input tokens and budget reservations are not billed usage.

Current CPU is calculated from adjacent cgroup samples; peak CPU/RAM reflects
the retained resource tail, while cgroup lifetime peak RAM is a distinct field.
Stale current CPU/RAM/Gateway readings remain stale or unavailable, not current
healthy capacity. A healthy probe is connectivity, not model admission. Formatter
cadence/next-check text does not install a scheduler. Optional `--reopen-status`
only reads another controller's JSON; it does not authorize or perform reopen.

### Optional live capacity preflight

`runtime:preflight` is **effectful**: it requests real OpenClaw model children.
It needs an authenticated, authorized installed `openclaw` CLI/Gateway, a valid
agent/model/thinking selection and sufficient controller capacity. It can incur
model work and retain child sessions. Use it only when this live check is
intended; it is not free static parsing or a prerequisite for reading status.

```sh
npm run runtime:preflight -- --concurrency 2 --model '<admitted-model>' \
  --thinking high --session-key agent:main:nova-review-controller \
  --collector-mode true --spawn-interval-ms 1500 --timeout-ms 180000
```

Standalone defaults are concurrency 1 (maximum 100), timeout 120000 ms
(maximum 3600000), agent `main`, thinking `high`, collector false and interval
1500 ms (range 0–60000). A model is required. Requests use subagent/run,
`cleanup: keep` and no thread; collector mode additionally selects collect and
waits through `agents_wait`. Otherwise it polls `subagents` lists. Interval 0
submits concurrently; a positive interval spaces spawn requests. The prompt
asks children to return `PREFLIGHT_OK`, but the script counts successful terminal
status rather than validating the returned text.

Passed JSON `openclaw-concurrency-preflight.v1` records requested/accepted/
completed counts and selected identity. It exits without error only after admission and successful terminal observation
of every requested child. Admission
rejection, failed child, transport error or completion deadline rejects the
check. The error path attempts cancellation of accepted tasks, resolving missing
task IDs from a list and using settled cancellation requests. Cancellation is
not terminal cleanup proof; list/transport failure can also obstruct cleanup.
Retain available session/run/task identities and reconcile actual remaining
children through the owning OpenClaw procedure before another preflight.

The supervisor can opt into preflight with **both** `--preflight-concurrency`
and `--preflight-model`; only its start path runs it. Its defaults differ:
timeout 180000 ms, thinking high, collector false, interval 1500 ms and the same
dedicated controller key. It calls this preflight synchronously before the
pipeline child, with a 240-second wrapper timeout. Timeout or supervisor
SIGINT/SIGTERM handling is not a cancellation protocol
for these model sessions. Omit both flags to avoid that extra live operation.
Passing capacity now is not a guarantee of later review/model quality or cleanup.

### Retain evidence and change the mechanism coherently

After a run, keep the append-only pipeline/resource logs, final heartbeat,
attempt diagnostics, platform/graph identity, run journal and referenced
artifact blobs while recovery or review consumers need them. Normal release
removes only this supervisor's lease, not the stable lock inode or run data.
A crash can leave lease, heartbeat temporary files or partial logs; neither a
stale timestamp nor a dead supervisor proves the pipeline or model tasks ended.
Do not delete shared artifact/journal storage to clear monitoring errors.
Apply the [shared plugin lifecycle](../use/plugins.md) and
[OpenClaw reconciliation](openclaw.md) before disposal or redispatch.

Changes to supervision/status/preflight must coordinate CLI flags, pipeline
receiver, run-root identity, FileMutex/lease, heartbeat/resource schema, status
reader and formatter, Gateway tool protocol and owning tests. Do not add a
retry or cleanup promise only to the monitor's prose.

> **Source evidence — supervisor ownership and recovery**
>
> **Claim:** The supervisor launches or adopts one run, retains attempt observations and only recovers nonterminal work under an exclusive lease.
>
> **Implementation:** [Launch, signal and serialized final observation](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/supervise-repository-review.mjs#L97-L149), [same-run bounded recovery](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/supervise-repository-review.mjs#L188-L215) and [lease/adoption/initial status](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/supervise-repository-review.mjs#L216-L256).
>
> **Contract or setting:** [Lease ownership and stable lock](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/lib/repository-review-supervisor-state.mjs#L23-L63); [original kernel-lock receiver](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/skills/nova/core/state/file-mutex.ts#L1-L24). Required paths, initial mode and maximum recoveries select this wrapper; Core retains run-state authority.
>
> **Test evidence:** [Actual lease ownership and stale-release assertions](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/tests/repository-review-supervisor-state.test.mjs#L12-L58); [terminal/error status assertions](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/tests/repository-review-supervisor-status.test.mjs#L9-L46); [stop-during-recovery assertions](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/tests/integration/repository-review-supervisor-stop.test.mjs#L38-L75). Assertions were read as Source, not run for this addition. They do not prove a deployed model review.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`; every linked whole file matches current Source.
>
> **Limit:** No new supervisor, native fixture, model, Gateway or production execution is asserted; stopping this monitor is not proof all external work ended.

> **Source evidence — status and resources are observations**
>
> **Claim:** Status and formatter expose bounded checkpoint/liveness/resource observations without granting lifecycle, full-history or token-usage authority.
>
> **Implementation:** [Artifact/checkpoint and bounded-tail status](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/repository-review-status.mjs#L86-L145), [freshness, locks and returned counters](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/repository-review-status.mjs#L146-L184) and [formatter freshness and unavailable usage](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/format-repository-review-status.mjs#L53-L105).
>
> **Contract or setting:** [Resource sampling and heartbeat commit order](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/lib/repository-review-supervisor-heartbeat.mjs#L38-L71); [bounded run-root identity](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/lib/repository-review-run-root.mjs#L53-L65). Status uses the platform's storage/artifact roots; formatter queries its selected OpenClaw controller, not a new approval issuer.
>
> **Test evidence:** [Unreadable status/artifact and terminal-status assertions](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/tests/repository-review-supervisor-status.test.mjs#L9-L46). These assertions were read, not run; no new full-history, formatter/model or resource-capacity execution proof is claimed.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`; every linked whole file matches current Source.
>
> **Limit:** Bounded tails and current Gateway observations cannot certify full run history, requested coverage or actual provider usage.

> **Source evidence — capacity preflight starts real children**
>
> **Claim:** Optional preflight checks actual child admission/completion and attempts cancellation after failure; it is not static configuration validation.
>
> **Implementation:** [Actual model spawn and admission checks](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/openclaw-concurrency-preflight.mjs#L110-L149) and [terminal observation and failed-check cancellation](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/openclaw-concurrency-preflight.mjs#L150-L192).
>
> **Contract or setting:** [Cancellation receiver and standalone settings](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/openclaw-concurrency-preflight.mjs#L95-L122); [supervisor opt-in and distinct defaults](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5/scripts/supervise-repository-review.mjs#L79-L96). Model/controller identity, concurrency, collector selection, spacing and timeouts govern this separate live operation.
>
> **Test evidence:** The linked original implementation was read, not executed. No capacity-preflight test run or terminal cancellation receipt is claimed for this documentation addition.
>
> **Revision:** `569f7b4933d4859cc67c80ddf40d5154ffd95ce5`; every linked whole file matches current Source.

prerequisites.statement:
The stage requires separate capabilities for dispatch, workspace creation and
removal, commit, merge, and artifact access. A grant for one action does not
imply another action. This is the implemented safety property. The source does
not record the historical reason for selecting this design. The current design
assessment is an inference: separate grants limit the effect of a compromised
specialist and keep lifecycle authority in Nova. The cost is more adapters,
fences, and reconciliation work. Reconsider this split only if a replacement
keeps per-effect authorization, fixed attempt identity, and uncertain-effect
reconciliation.

characters, identifiers to 128 characters, paths to 4,096 characters, and the
commit message to 4,096 characters. `headBefore` must be a 40- to 64-character
lowercase hexadecimal object ID. These bounds make admission deterministic and
stop an agent prompt from becoming an unbounded transport.

1. Nova replaces caller-supplied run and attempt values with the active lease.
2. The stage adds an attempt generation to the workspace path and branch. This
   keeps a repair attempt separate from an earlier attempt.
3. The `git.workspace.create` adapter creates the worktree at the requested
   base. A repair uses the current `HEAD`; an ordinary attempt uses `baseRef`.
4. The adapter returns a signed runtime workspace reference and a 40-character
   source revision. The stage checks the repository, path, branch, revision,
   and attempt owner before it dispatches Forge.
5. Forge works only in that referenced workspace and returns repository-relative
   changed paths plus the checks that it ran.
6. A ready result causes `git.commit` with an expected parent. This detects a
   changed baseline instead of committing on an unknown parent.
7. `git.merge` integrates that exact commit into the declared merge target.
8. The stage removes the workspace only after integration succeeds.

anchors.exactExcerpt:
Nova writes `run-snapshot.json` through a private temporary file.
It uses a no-replace hard link to publish the final file.
It synchronizes the file and directory before it removes the temporary name.
A reader therefore sees either no snapshot or one complete snapshot.

The generic file journal serializes one JSON record per line.
Each record has a sequence, previous hash, and current hash.
Append uses a cross-process file mutex and `fsync`.
Opening `FileJournal` creates an append-lock file and can truncate an
unterminated final line before parsing. This also applies to audit, recovery,
and resume, including a command that later rejects the run. Preserve raw bytes
with stopped writers before such inspection after interruption. Use
[Inspect a Run](../use/operate.md#inspect-a-run) for the canonical preservation
procedure and the pure parser that rejects incomplete bytes without repair.
After a reader loads records, it detects file-identity, size, and timestamp
changes and reloads the file. It accepts the reload when the previous records
remain the exact prefix of the new history. It rejects a shorter history or a
different prior hash chain. A new reader has no earlier prefix for comparison;
it cannot identify a clean rollback without an externally retained trusted
head.

cleanup.statement: Explaining the host/session protocol performs no dispatch. In the actual session path, cancel the owned subagent or send ACP stop, recover accepted session identity after uncertain spawn, and poll until terminal. anchors.exactExcerpt:
## Session Lifecycle

For a `subagent` target, the adapter spawns a labelled task, records its task
identity, polls the Gateway, and reads the terminal result. For an `acp` target,
it uses an ACP session. Poll delay grows to `maxPollMs`, and the entire session
is limited by `sessionTimeoutMs`. The adapter validates current MCP result
envelopes and legacy Gateway wrappers and rejects error statuses before it
parses success content.

Cancellation is not a local flag only. A subagent receives a `cancel` action.
An ACP session receives a stop message. After a failed or aborted spawn, cleanup
tries to recover the accepted session identity, sends cancellation, and polls
until terminal state. If it cannot prove terminal state, it returns
`OPENCLAW_SESSION_CLEANUP_UNRESOLVED`. This fail-closed result prevents Nova
from starting duplicate work after an uncertain response.

## State, Ordering, Retry, And Pressure

- One dispatch owns one OpenClaw session identity and one idempotency key.
- Poll results describe the same session. They are not independent attempts.
- Runtime dispatch does not treat a lost response as proof that spawn failed.
- Session cleanup must finish or remain explicitly unresolved before retry.
- The general adapter stores result bytes below the configured result prefix or
  reads them from the paired result endpoint. OpenClaw owns session history;
  the adapter does not create a second durable session database.
- Prism Control PostgreSQL is the authority for Prism jobs, fences, committed
  tool results, and reconciliation state. The OpenClaw session is execution
  state, not Prism product authority.
- Host hook queues are bounded by event count and bytes. Redis transport has
  separate retention and retry rules. Queue contents are lost on Gateway
  restart. Accepted Redis records follow Redis retention and durability; see
  [Communication](communication.md).
- Model output is untrusted until the Forge or Echo parser validates it.

| Failure | Observable result | Safe recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Host plugin is absent, incompatible, or not allowlisted | Its tools or hooks do not register. | Correct the package version, allowlist, and configuration, then restart the Gateway. Do not infer that observation or Prism writes occurred. |
| Prism tool response is lost | The model sees a tool failure or no result; Control may already have committed. | Query the durable job by `jobId`. Reuse only the identical fenced payload after the stored state proves that action safe. Escalate `needs_nova`. |
| General spawn response is lost | Cleanup tries to recover the label and accepted session. | Wait for terminal reconciliation. Do not dispatch another attempt while `OPENCLAW_SESSION_CLEANUP_UNRESOLVED` remains. |
| Session exceeds poll or wall limit | Adapter returns `OPENCLAW_SESSION_TIMEOUT` and enters cleanup. | Confirm cancellation and terminal state before Nova decides on a new attempt. |
| Result is absent, malformed, too large, or from another model | Result collection or specialist parsing fails closed. | Preserve session identity and result bytes, correct the producer or target, then create a new Nova attempt. |
| Observer queue or Redis write fails | Status counters and warning logs show rejection, write failure, or dead-letter failure. | Restore Redis or reduce event pressure. Lost in-memory events cannot be reconstructed from this plugin. |

The host tool client has an important limit: its `fetch` has no client timeout,
response-size limit, or retry. A process stop or network failure can therefore
leave the caller without a result after Prism Control committed the change. Do
not repeat the tool call because the client timed out or disconnected. First
read the durable Prism job by `jobId`. A matching job/fence and payload digest
returns the recorded result; a conflicting payload fails. If the job is
`needs_nova`, stop for reconciliation.

failure domains. Codex and Nova receive no Kubernetes token or kubeconfig.
