## Canonical Start, Readiness, and Observation Procedure
<!-- operator-task: start-readiness-observe -->

This section is the sole authority for `start-readiness-observe`. Start with an
installed source-bound release, explicit `<context>` and `<namespace>`, selected
component list, independent administration, and no active change. Run cluster
commands from the administration machine. Kubernetes owns process and Service
state; `scripts/deploy.sh` and the health program embedded by the chart own
component checks; a completed application transaction owns functional proof.

Before any cluster command on this page, complete
[Bind Cluster Authority](install.md#bind-cluster-authority). Keep the same bound
shell for the whole task. Every raw `kubectl`, Helm, or `scripts/deploy.sh`
command below must inherit its exported read-only `KUBECONFIG`; every shown
`<context>` must equal `EXPECTED_CONTEXT`. Run `assert_cluster_binding`
immediately before each command block. Stop on any mismatch and follow the
binding section's recovery; never fall back to the default kubeconfig.

Record source and release identities, context, namespace, time, and evidence
directory. Stop if the current context, selected images, or ownership differs
from the install record.

Observe the four levels in order:

1. **Process:**

   ```bash
   assert_cluster_binding
   kubectl --context "<context>" -n "<namespace>" rollout status deployment/agent-nova --timeout=300s
   kubectl --context "<context>" -n "<namespace>" rollout status deployment/agent-buster --timeout=300s
   kubectl --context "<context>" -n "<namespace>" get pods -o wide
   ```

   Expected observation: each selected Deployment completes rollout and every
   selected Pod is running without restart growth. Omit a role only when the
   install record says it is disabled.

2. **Service:**

   ```bash
   assert_cluster_binding
   kubectl --context "<context>" -n "<namespace>" get service agent-nova agent-buster
   kubectl --context "<context>" -n "<namespace>" get endpointslice \
     -l kubernetes.io/service-name=agent-nova
   kubectl --context "<context>" -n "<namespace>" get endpointslice \
     -l kubernetes.io/service-name=agent-buster
   ```

   Expected observation: each selected Service exists and has at least one
   ready endpoint. A Service without an endpoint is not ready.

3. **Dependency:**

   ```bash
   assert_cluster_binding
   bound_deploy smoke-agent nova
   bound_deploy smoke-agent buster
   ```

   Expected observation: each command exits zero after rollout, Pod readiness,
   gateway, startup record, Redis-aware readiness, code bundle, skills, and
   runtime configuration checks. These checks do not prove a user transaction.

4. **Functional:** execute the registered non-production
   [deployment success exercise](workflows/buster-suite.md#deployment-success-exercise)
   with its exact project, provider, receipt, and cleanup checks. Expected
   observation: the project returns terminal `succeeded`, the audit agrees, and
   all external effects have terminal receipts. This is technical proof; use
   [Deliver a Demo](demo-delivery.md#canonical-demo-delivery-procedure) for a
   separate human decision.

At any failure, stop at the first failed level. Use
[symptom diagnosis](diagnose.md#canonical-symptom-diagnosis-procedure); do not
restart all roles to hide a dependency or functional failure. Recovery is the
narrow owning-layer repair followed by all four levels again. Cleanup belongs
to the functional exercise. Retain every command, output, exit status, selected
image ID, events, audit, receipts, cleanup result, and blocked step.

## Canonical Run Control Procedure
<!-- operator-task: run-control -->

This page is the sole authority for `run-control`. The supported start state is
a `pipeline-platform.v2` and project or explicit graph at the original source
and package snapshot, with writable durable storage and a reconciled prior
effect state. Run from `<repository-root>` on the administration machine. Nova's
CLI and durable journal are authoritative; process state and plugin logs are
diagnostic only.

Complete [Validate Before Starting](#validate-before-starting),
[Start a Project Run](#start-a-project-run), [Inspect a Run](#inspect-a-run),
[Approve or Resume a Wait](#approve-or-resume-a-wait), and, after interruption,
[Recover After Interruption](#recover-after-interruption). The
[Cancellation Boundary](#cancellation-boundary) is mandatory. Stop on an
unknown run, changed graph/package digest, unresolved effect, stale or expired
wait, issuer mismatch, or terminal run. Retain input digests, output, audit,
wait and signal bytes, effects and receipts, failure, retry decision, and final
state. Follow [Evidence to Retain](#evidence-to-retain) for protected raw copies
and signal bytes; a digest alone does not authorize deletion.

## Before Each Operation

Run from `<repository-root>` unless a command states another location.
Set no implicit Kubernetes context.

The machine that runs Nova's CLI needs Linux file locking and `/usr/bin/flock`
with `--exclusive`, `--timeout`, and `--conflict-exit-code` support. Nova uses
that fixed executable to protect durable state updates. A BusyBox `flock` that
lacks these options is insufficient. Stop before a run or resume if this
interface is unavailable; a lock error does not prove that a signal was
accepted. Preserve the journal and diagnose the executable before retrying.
[Lock acquisition and release](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/425be378fa25d26835a5418d65bfd457e151cc16/skills/nova/core/state/file-mutex.ts#L4-L22).

Record these inputs:

- Full source commit.
- Platform configuration path and digest.
- Project or pipeline path and digest.
- Selected role and plugin package revisions.
- Operator identity for an approval or administrative decision.
- Durable storage root and its free capacity.

Do not start work while the project repository contains uncommitted changes.
The project command rejects a changed baseline or dirty worktree.

## Configure the Platform

The operator owns the platform configuration.
Project content cannot add trusted packages, providers, adapters, or grants.

The configuration must declare these groups:

| Group | Operator decision | Verification question |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `installationRoots` | Package locations that the registry may discover | Do all paths exist at the selected revision? |
| `trustedBuiltinRoots` | Package roots allowed as built-ins | Does each path belong to the reviewed release? |
| `externalTrust` | Allowed external source digests and attestations | Does each external package match its approved digest? |
| `providers` | One selected provider for each capability | Does the provider registration exist and activate? |
| `grants` | Resource limits for each registration and capability | Does each grant allow only the intended resource? |
| `adapters` | Adapter configuration | Do referenced endpoints and stores exist? |
| `activeAdapters` | Adapters that start in this runtime | Does every required capability have one active provider? |
| `observers` | Observer configuration | Is required delivery reachable and bounded? |
| `storageRoot` | Durable run storage | Is it persistent, writable, private, and monitored? |
| `shutdownTimeoutMs` | Bounded runtime shutdown interval | Does the interval allow the selected adapters and observers to settle? |
| issuer fields | Nova and administrative identities | Do resume signals use an authorized exact identity? |

Relative package and storage paths resolve from the platform file directory.
This prevents the shell working directory from changing their meaning.

> **Source evidence — platform authority**
>
> **Claim:** The operator-owned platform document selects trusted package roots, providers, grants, adapters, observers, durable storage, and decision issuers. Relative paths use the platform file directory.
>
> **Implementation:** The platform schema declares [its required fields, schema version, and installation roots](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/config/platform.schema.json#L5-L33).
> It also declares [trust, providers, and grants](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/config/platform.schema.json#L34-L68).
> It defines [adapter, observer, and storage authority](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/config/platform.schema.json#L69-L95).
> [The loader validates the document and resolves paths from its directory](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/config/platform.ts#L53-L69).
>
> **Contract or setting:** [`pipeline-platform.v2` is the required schema version](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/config/platform.schema.json#L20-L21).
>
> **Test evidence:** [The platform test checks path resolution, immutability, validation, and rejection of project-controlled installation roots](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/tests/verification/contracts/check-plugin-system-v2-platform-config.mjs#L32-L55). The test passed on 2026-09-16.
>
> **Revision:** `1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de`.
>
> **Limit:** Schema validation does not prove that a configured provider, adapter, observer, or storage service is reachable.

Keep credentials outside the JSON file.
Use adapter-supported secret references or the intended secret resolver.

## Start a Project Run

Starting condition:

- Project repository HEAD equals `baseRevision`.
- Project repository has no uncommitted file.
- Platform storage has enough monitored capacity.
- Required providers and adapters are reachable.
- No existing process owns the same intended run.

Start the run:

```bash
npm run pipeline -- \
  --platform "<platform.json>" \
  --project "<project.json>"
```

The CLI result is one JSON object. Npm can print lifecycle banners before it;
do not parse the entire npm output as one JSON document.
It includes `runId`, `status`, `completionScope`, `acceptanceReadiness`, and stage states.

Exit code zero means the returned run status is `succeeded`.
It does not mean human acceptance or complete live acceptance.

For an explicit graph, use:

```bash
npm run pipeline -- \
  --platform "<platform.json>" \
  --pipeline "<pipeline.json>" \
  --run-id "<new-run-id>"
```

Choose a new, unused run identity before this command.
Supply it through `--run-id`.
For later inspection or recovery, use the `runId` returned by the CLI.
Do not reuse a prior terminal run identity.

## Approve or Resume a Wait

The CLI uses a typed resume-signal file.
It does not provide a separate `approve` verb.

Before creating a signal, complete [Inspect a Run](#inspect-a-run). Use the
original platform, run ID, project or graph, package snapshot, storage root,
and runtime configuration from the retained start record. Confirm stopped run
and owning-adapter writers, preserve new verified raw run and adapter copies,
and require strict parsing of the copied journals. Read the active wait from
that preserved evidence. Stop on unknown ownership, changed identity, failed
copy verification, incomplete records, or a journal chain error. Copy no
identity from an earlier wait. There is no non-mutating live audit command
that can replace these prerequisites.

Read `waitId`, `signalType`,
`authorizedIssuer`, `expiresAt`, and the payload requirements from the active
`wait-request.v2` record. The signal must contain all eight fields in this
example:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": "resume-signal.v2",
  "signalId": "signal:approval-2026-09-17T120000Z",
  "idempotencyKey": "approval:wait-7:decision-1",
  "waitId": "wait:7",
  "signalType": "approval.resolved",
  "issuer": {
    "type": "operator",
    "id": "operator:release"
  },
  "issuedAt": "2026-09-17T12:00:00.000Z",
  "payload": {
    "decision": "approved",
    "issuer": {
      "type": "operator",
      "id": "operator:release"
    },
    "reason": "Approved the exact source and report in wait:7."
  }
}
```

This example is valid for the shared envelope schema. Its payload is the
approval payload used by the approval path. Another wait type can require a
different payload. Never copy this payload without checking the active wait.

The `issuer` object is **unsigned and self-asserted by the caller**. Nova checks
that its type and ID equal the active wait's `authorizedIssuer`, but the signal
schema contains no signature and the CLI does not authenticate the human or an
external identity provider. Protect access to signal creation and the CLI as
the effective authority. Do not describe issuer matching as identity proof.

Apply these matching rules:

- Create a new `signalId` for one decision event. Nova uses it as the cause of
  the `wait.resolved` event.
- Create one `idempotencyKey` for the exact signal content. Reuse that key only
  to retry the same bytes. Signal storage treats an identical stored record as
  a no-op and rejects the same key with different content. A retry after wait
  resolution is stale and stops before this storage check.
- Copy `waitId` and `signalType` from the active wait.
- Copy the authorized issuer type and ID. This satisfies runtime matching only;
  it does not authenticate who created the file.
- Set `issuedAt` to a valid date-time at or after creation of the active wait.
- Build `payload` from that wait's request and plugin contract. Include the
  current source, decision, or repair digest when that contract requires it.

Nova validates the closed envelope before recording the accepted signal and
its durable `wait.resolved` transition. It rejects unknown fields, a stale or
unknown wait, an expired wait, a mismatched type or issuer, and a signal issued
before wait creation. After Nova records one signal for a wait, a different
signal cannot resolve that wait again.

Storage can change before those checks. [Resume opens the administrative and
event journals before wait and signal validation](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/2025f36306636b2e0c2c426447bf137d0574e11f/skills/nova/core/execution/engine-run.ts#L81-L95),
and [run ownership acquires durable lock state first](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/2025f36306636b2e0c2c426447bf137d0574e11f/skills/nova/core/execution/run-mutation.ts#L7-L16).
Opening a journal can create an append lock or truncate an incomplete tail.
A rejected envelope, wrong issuer, stale wait, or terminal run therefore does
not prove that canonical files are unchanged. Preserve original raw bytes
through [Inspect a Run](#inspect-a-run) before every submission.

Use an operator-controlled signal file with restricted permissions. Before
**each** submission below, including a retry, replay check, or wrong-signal
check:

1. Reconfirm the original platform and run ID, project or graph bytes, package
   snapshot, storage root, and runtime configuration against the retained
   start record. `<original-project.json>` and `<original-pipeline.json>` mean
   those exact original inputs, not a new candidate.
2. Confirm the prior run owner has exited. Stop new writes to the run and its
   owning adapter stores. Unknown ownership stops the command; containment
   alone does not prove that an external effect completed.
3. Reconcile accepted external effects through their owning contracts. Stop
   while any outcome is unknown or no supported continuation exists.
4. Follow [Inspect a Run](#inspect-a-run) to make and verify a **new** complete
   raw run copy and new owning-adapter copies through their declared backup
   procedures, with writers stopped. Define its `preserve_run_state` helper
   and evidence-root inputs in this Bash shell.
5. Require successful strict parsing of every copied run journal. Retain raw
   bytes and stop on a copy, identity, incomplete-record, sequence, or hash
   failure. Do not use automatic tail truncation to make submission possible.
6. Verify that the signal still names that active unexpired wait. Retain the
   exact signal bytes, ID, issue time, and idempotency key. Submit one of the
   following forms, using the same original identities.

Project form:

```bash
preserve_run_state || exit 1
resume_status=0
npm run pipeline -- \
  --platform "$RUN_CONTROL_PLATFORM" \
  --project "<original-project.json>" \
  --signal "<resume-signal.json>" \
  > "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/resume.stdout" \
  2> "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/resume.stderr" || resume_status=$?
printf '%s\n' "$resume_status" > "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/resume.exit" || exit 1
```

For an explicit graph, supply the original run identity:

```bash
preserve_run_state || exit 1
resume_status=0
npm run pipeline -- \
  --platform "$RUN_CONTROL_PLATFORM" \
  --pipeline "<original-pipeline.json>" \
  --run-id "$RUN_CONTROL_RUN_ID" \
  --signal "<resume-signal.json>" \
  > "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/resume.stdout" \
  2> "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/resume.stderr" || resume_status=$?
printf '%s\n' "$resume_status" > "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/resume.exit" || exit 1
```

Expected observation: an accepted signal records one matching resolution, and
continued execution gives the resumed stage a new attempt identity. Exit zero
requires `succeeded`; a nonzero exit can contain a waiting, failed, blocked, or
rejected result. Retain stdout, stderr, and the actual exit status before any
follow-up. The command response alone does not prove adapter or external
process quiescence. If the response or exit status was lost, retain partial
output and record that result as `not observed`; do not invent an exit status.

After **every** submission, including rejection or a lost response, confirm
that the owner has exited and re-establish stopped run and adapter writers.
If ownership is unknown, retain the previous capture and command output and
stop; do not audit or submit again. Otherwise make new verified run and adapter
copies through [Inspect a Run](#inspect-a-run), require strict copied-journal
inspection, then capture its audit outputs and exit status. Keep the previous
captures and compare the new journal head, original identities, actual wait
transition, attempt budget, and external receipts with the submitted signal.
Do not reuse the pre-submission copy for this later audit.

Stop after an issuer mismatch, expired wait, digest mismatch, or stale signal.
Do not edit the journal or change the signal identity to force acceptance.
An exact retry needs the same bytes and key, a still-active wait, known effect
outcomes, and the complete fresh preservation sequence above. A replay after
resolution is stale or terminal and does not prove unchanged lock files.
Any later incident-owner-authorized canonical tail repair must retain the
verified original raw bytes and record the command and its actual changes.

> **Source evidence — signal contract and replay rules**
>
> **Claim:** A resume signal uses a closed eight-field envelope. Nova compares its caller-supplied issuer with the active wait. An identical retry has no second effect, and a conflicting retry fails.
>
> **Implementation:** [Nova validates wait identity, signal type, issuer, expiry, and issue time](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/nova/core/execution/engine-snapshots.ts#L137-L144). [Nova makes identical retries idempotent and permits only one recorded signal for each wait](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/nova/core/execution/engine-run.ts#L109-L122).
>
> **Contract or setting:** [The contract requires all eight envelope fields and rejects extra fields](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/common/plugin-runtime/contracts/plugin-system/v2/plugin-system-v2.schema.json#L777-L802).
>
> **Test evidence:** [The recovery test exercises accepted, repeated, stale, and expired signals](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/tests/verification/reliability/attempt-projection-recovery.test.mjs#L43-L76). The publication check also validates the example on this page against the canonical schema.
>
> **Revision:** `1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de`.
>
> **Limit:** The envelope has no signature. Its issuer is self-asserted by the
> caller, and repository checks do not authenticate the human or external
> identity provider.

## Recover After Interruption
<!-- operator-variant: run-control/recover-project -->
<!-- operator-variant: run-control/recover-explicit-graph -->
<!-- operator-variant: run-control/recovery-signal-required -->
<!-- operator-variant: run-control/recovery-terminal-run -->
<!-- operator-variant: run-control/recovery-cooldown-not-due -->
<!-- operator-variant: run-control/recovery-identity-mismatch -->
<!-- operator-variant: run-control/recovery-unresolved-effect -->
<!-- operator-variant: run-control/recovery-external-continuation -->

Recovery reopens durable state after a process interruption.
It does not approve a wait or resolve an uncertain external result.

Before every audit or recovery attempt after interruption, including a retry,
stop new admission, confirm that the prior owner has exited, and verify stopped
owning-adapter writers. Follow [Inspect a Run](#inspect-a-run) to preserve and
verify new raw run and adapter copies through their declared backup procedures.
Define its `preserve_run_state` helper and evidence-root inputs in this Bash
shell; require strict copied-journal parsing before the command. Stop
on an incomplete or corrupt journal. Audit can truncate an incomplete tail;
retain the original bytes before any permitted canonical repair. Confirm the
original platform, graph or project, package snapshot, run ID, storage root,
and configuration. Retain the audit output only after this preservation step. Reconcile every accepted
external effect that lacks a terminal receipt. Stop while any outcome remains
unknown.

Project form, with the original project bytes:

```bash
preserve_run_state || exit 1
recovery_status=0
npm run pipeline -- \
  --platform "$RUN_CONTROL_PLATFORM" \
  --project "<original-project.json>" \
  --recover "$RUN_CONTROL_RUN_ID" \
  > "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/recovery.stdout" \
  2> "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/recovery.stderr" || recovery_status=$?
printf '%s\n' "$recovery_status" > "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/recovery.exit" || exit 1
```

Explicit graph form:

```bash
preserve_run_state || exit 1
recovery_status=0
npm run pipeline -- \
  --platform "$RUN_CONTROL_PLATFORM" \
  --pipeline "<original-pipeline.json>" \
  --recover "$RUN_CONTROL_RUN_ID" \
  > "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/recovery.stdout" \
  2> "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/recovery.stderr" || recovery_status=$?
printf '%s\n' "$recovery_status" > "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/recovery.exit" || exit 1
```

Recovery must use the original graph and package snapshot.
Start a new run when governed configuration must change.

Expected observation: a permitted recovery writes one JSON result for the same
run ID. Exit code zero requires terminal status `succeeded`; retain a nonzero
result as a failed or blocked recovery, not as proof that restart completed.
[Recovery opens journals and can reconcile observer state before returning](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/2025f36306636b2e0c2c426447bf137d0574e11f/skills/nova/core/execution/engine-run.ts#L56-L68).
It can change journals, effects, observer state, and adapter stores, including
before a failed or blocked return. The pre-recovery capture
cannot prove the bytes that the next audit will open.

After **every** recovery attempt, including failure, rejection, or a lost
response:

1. Retain the pre-command raw copies, available command stdout/stderr, and
   actual exit status. Record a lost response or exit status as `not observed`.
   Confirm that the run owner has exited and re-establish stopped run
   and owning-adapter writers. Stop if ownership is unknown.
2. Reconfirm the original run, platform, project or graph, package, storage,
   and configuration identities. Make and verify new adapter-store copies
   through their declared backup procedures, then call `preserve_run_state`
   again through [Inspect a Run](#inspect-a-run). Require successful strict
   parsing of every copied run journal. Keep rejected bytes and stop on failure.
3. Only then run the audit block in [Inspect a Run](#inspect-a-run). It captures
   stdout, stderr, and the actual exit status in this new observation directory.
   Never reuse the pre-recovery copy or overwrite the earlier audit.
4. Compare the before/after audits, original graph and package identities,
   committed journal heads, external effects and receipts, and returned state.
   A successful recovery needs a final audit that agrees with terminal
   `succeeded` and contains no unexplained duplicate effect. A failed, waiting,
   blocked, or uncertain result remains that result.

Before any further recovery retry, repeat the original-identity, stopped-writer,
new raw run/adapter copy, and strict-inspection prerequisites. Later authorized
canonical tail repair retains the original bytes first and records its actual
changes; it does not turn an uncertain external outcome into success.

Use the exact failure before choosing the next action:

| Observation | Meaning | Safe action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RECOVERY_SIGNAL_REQUIRED:<wait-id>` | The run has an active wait; restart cannot invent its decision | Read the active wait and use [Approve or Resume a Wait](#approve-or-resume-a-wait) with one matching signal |
| `RECOVERY_RUN_TERMINAL` | The durable run already ended as succeeded, failed, blocked, or cancelled | Do not recover it; retain the audit and start a new governed run only for new work |
| `RECOVERY_COOLDOWN_NOT_DUE:<stage-id>:<time>` | A persisted retry time has not arrived | Do not bypass the clock; wait until the recorded time, then repeat the same recovery command with new stopped-writer raw run/adapter copies and strict inspection |
| `RECOVERY_GRAPH_*`, `RECOVERY_PIPELINE_ID_MISMATCH`, or `PROJECT_RECOVERY_RUN_MISMATCH` | The supplied graph, project, or run does not match durable state | Restore the original input bytes; never edit the snapshot or reuse the run ID for a changed graph |
| `RECOVERY_PINNED_PACKAGE_*`, `RECOVERY_PACKAGE_UPGRADE_*`, or `RECOVERY_REGISTRY_SNAPSHOT_INVALID` | Installed package identity differs from the recorded snapshot | Restore the recorded package set; use only the separate authorized package-upgrade procedure when its exact contract applies |
| `RECOVERY_RUNTIME_CONFIGURATION_MISMATCH` or `RECOVERY_DEPENDENCY_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` | Runtime configuration or dependency identity changed | Restore the recorded runtime configuration and dependency set, or start a new governed run |
| `RECOVERY_EFFECT_OUTCOME_UNRESOLVED:<effect-id>` | An accepted external request has no known receipt outcome | Query the external authority with the original identity and reconcile it before any recovery retry |
| `RECOVERY_EXTERNAL_CONTINUATION_REQUIRED:<effect-id>` | An external effect has a receipt, but its interrupted attempt needs explicit continuation | Follow the owning plugin or provider continuation contract; do not replay the effect through generic recovery |

Project recovery also validates the stored generated nodes and their encoding
selectors before it verifies the whole pinned graph. The implementation
authorities are
[`recovery.ts`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/nova/project/recovery.ts#L5-L50)
and
[`delivery-manifest.ts`](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/1c30980c132e3ff0b45dc8eeaf4b46a37d6d77de/skills/nova/project/delivery-manifest.ts#L6-L33).
These are operator-visible identity mismatches, not permissions to repair the
stored graph:

| Exact outcome | Failed stored authority | Safe action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PROJECT_RECOVERY_SOURCE_INVALID` | Exactly one generated `source-preflight` node is absent or has the wrong type | Stop; restore the original durable run bytes from the owning store or retain the run as unrecoverable |
| `PROJECT_RECOVERY_REVIEW_NODES_MISMATCH` | Generated Review node identities differ from the project compiler | Stop; use the original project/compiler/package snapshot |
| `PROJECT_RECOVERY_REVIEW_SEMANTICS_INVALID` | A stored Review semantic or report encoding is unsupported | Stop; restore the exact compatible package snapshot; never rewrite the node |
| `PROJECT_RECOVERY_REVIEW_SEMANTICS_MIXED` | Review nodes contain mixed semantic generations | Stop; treat the durable graph as inconsistent and preserve it for diagnosis |
| `PROJECT_RECOVERY_REPORT_ENCODING_INVALID` | A Review report encoding is unsupported | Stop; restore the compatible package snapshot |
| `PROJECT_RECOVERY_REPORT_ENCODING_MIXED` | Review nodes contain mixed report encodings | Stop; preserve the inconsistent graph; do not select a mode by majority |
| `PROJECT_RECOVERY_SUMMARY_NODE_INVALID` | The one required `project-summary` identity/type pairing is missing, duplicated, or inconsistent | Stop; restore the original durable graph bytes or retain the run as unrecoverable |
| `PROJECT_RECOVERY_DELIVERY_SELECTOR_FOREIGN` | A non-summary node owns `deliveryManifestEncoding` | Stop; do not move or delete the foreign selector in durable state |
| `PROJECT_RECOVERY_DELIVERY_MANIFEST_ENCODING_INVALID` | The stored summary selector shape or value is unsupported | Stop; restore the compatible project/package snapshot |
| `PROJECT_DELIVERY_MANIFEST_ENCODING_INVALID` | A caller supplied a delivery-manifest mode outside the supported legacy/current pair | Correct the caller configuration before compilation; do not mutate an existing run |

Recovery has no separate temporary runtime object to clean up. Preserve all
before/after raw run and adapter captures, manifests, partial or rejected tails,
audits, exact commands, output, exit status, effect queries and receipts, repair
changes, and the final decision under [Evidence to Retain](#evidence-to-retain).
Do not delete a `nova-raw-state.*` observation directory because its digest was
recorded or a later command passed. Only a successful recovery result plus the
matching final audit and reconciled external receipts proves the intended
recovery; containment or a completed audit alone does not prove success.

## Cancellation Boundary

The current pipeline CLI has no supported operator cancellation command.
Do not present process termination as durable run cancellation.

An internal abort signal can cancel active work during runtime shutdown.
That mechanism is not an external operator control surface.

When urgent containment is necessary:

1. Preserve available command, process, and component observations through
   supported paths. Do not audit while run or adapter writers remain active.
2. Stop new admission through the owning service boundary.
3. Use the approved incident process for workload containment.
4. Reconcile every accepted external effect.
5. After the owner has exited and run/adapter writers are stopped, complete
   [Inspect a Run](#inspect-a-run) before audit or another run-control command.
   Preserve new verified raw run/adapter copies and strictly inspect the copied
   journals. Unknown ownership or rejected bytes stops this inspection path.
6. Do not claim `cancelled` unless durable lifecycle evidence records it.

This is an implementation limit, not a documentation shortcut.

## Safe Retry Decision

Every permitted audit, recovery, or signal retry must first repeat the
original-identity, stopped run/adapter writer, new verified raw run/adapter copy,
and strict copied-journal inspection steps in [Inspect a Run](#inspect-a-run).
An earlier successful capture does not cover a later command's storage state.
Stop if a required check or owning-store backup procedure is unavailable.

| Condition | Next action |
| --- | --- |
| Command failed before durable request acceptance, with a verified complete journal and unchanged active authority | Correct the rejected input and review one submission |
| Durable request exists with a terminal failure | Follow its declared retry or repair decision |
| Request exists and provider outcome is absent | Inspect through a documented provider status operation; if the outcome remains uncertain, preserve evidence, stop, and escalate |
| Provider completed but local response was lost | Use an exact provider-specific idempotent import operation only when its contract documents one; otherwise preserve evidence, stop, and escalate |
| Wait remains active, unexpired, with complete history and no prior resolution | Follow [Approve or Resume a Wait](#approve-or-resume-a-wait), including new stopped-writer raw run/adapter copies and strict inspection before each submission; retain exact signal bytes and identities |
| Wait expired or resolved, or signal identity conflicts | Stop; preserve raw state before audit. Do not issue a new signal identity to force acceptance |
| Graph, package, or policy digest changed | Start a new governed run |
| Terminal run | Do not recover or resume it |

There is no generic Core operation that reconciles an uncertain external
effect and imports its result. See the
[current reconciliation boundary](../status/open-issues.md#uncertain-external-effects-have-no-supported-reconciliation-and-result-import-operation).
A provider-specific normal result import is safe only when that provider
documents the request identity, result identity, idempotency rule, authority,
and durable transition. External inspection alone does not authorize a retry,
resume, journal edit, or result import.

## Canonical Plugin Lifecycle Procedure
<!-- operator-task: plugin-lifecycle -->

This procedure operates Nova `pipeline-plugin-v2` registrations selected through
`pipeline-platform.v2`. It does not install or activate the OpenClaw extensions
`kubeclaw-agent-observer` and `kubeclaw-prism`, or the Codex plugin `kubeclaw-ops`.
Use the [packaged OpenClaw host route](../extend/testing.md#operate-the-packaged-openclaw-hosts)
and the [Codex host lifecycle boundary](../extend/testing.md#codex-host-lifecycle-boundary)
for their version, deployment controls, observations, disable/removal limits,
owners, and safe stops. Nova compile/start/audit cannot prove their host lifecycle.

`kubeclaw.openclaw-agent-events:source` belongs to this Nova procedure, but also
requires an actual compatible OpenClaw SDK event source in the Nova process.
Apply its [SDK readiness and host-event proof boundary](../extend/testing.md#nova-adapter-with-an-openclaw-sdk-dependency)
before claiming activation. Package discovery, injected SDK tests, and provider
selection do not prove configured real-host subscription.

### Supported start state, version, location, and authority

Start with a clean checkout at the exact source commit, an existing
`pipeline-platform.v2` file, an operator-supplied project or graph that uses the
plugin, and writable durable storage. Run commands from `<repository-root>` on
an administration machine with Node.js 24. The platform configuration owner,
not project content, controls installation roots, built-in trust, external
digests or attestations, providers, grants, adapters, observers, and storage.

The registry supports discovery and activation of packages already present in
approved installation roots. Internal APIs can copy or remove a local external
package, but the repository exposes no general operator CLI for those actions.
Do not turn an internal API or a filesystem copy into an undocumented operator
command.

### Preconditions

- Record the source commit and SHA-256 digest of `<platform.json>`.
- Identify exact package ID, registration ID, contract version, content digest,
  capability grants, dependencies, secret names, and every active run that pins
  the package.
- Complete the per-plugin external dependency matrix above and assign an owner to
  every required reachability check and failure response.
- Keep plugin code and schemas available for every nonterminal pinned run.
- Keep secret values only in the configured secret authority. Platform and
  project JSON may name secrets but must not contain their values.
- Prepare a controlled project or graph whose external effects are safe and
  whose success proves the selected registration.

Stop when a package identity is ambiguous, its digest or attestation is absent,
a dependency has no owner, a requested grant is wider than intended, or a
procedure would place a secret in evidence.

### 1. Discover and select

First complete the canonical
[Locked Dependency Installation](quickstart.md#locked-dependency-installation)
in the disposable checkout. Its retained evidence is part of this procedure's
evidence.

```bash
git status --short
git rev-parse HEAD
npm run plugin-system:inventory:check
npm run verify:plugin-packages
sha256sum "<platform.json>"
```

Expected observation: the worktree has no unexpected change, inventory and
package verification exit zero, and the recorded platform digest matches the
file to be used. Inspect the dynamic catalogue and select by exact IDs and
contract version, never by discovery order.

Check these platform fields together:

| Field | Operator decision |
| --- | --- |
| `installationRoots` | Canonical roots allowed for discovery |
| `trustedBuiltinRoots` | Which discovered roots are trusted built-ins |
| `externalTrust` | Exact source digest or verified-attestation binding |
| `providers` | One registration selected for each required capability |
| `grants` | The least capability scope for each registration |
| `adapters` and `activeAdapters` | Configuration and which adapters start |
| `observers` | Configuration for enabled observers |
| `storageRoot` | Persistent private run storage |

Relative roots resolve from the platform file, not the shell directory.

### 2. Validate a candidate configuration without starting work

Have the platform owner create `<candidate-platform.json>`. Then compile a
controlled project to a new output path:

```bash
test ! -e "<compiled-pipeline.json>"
npm run pipeline -- \
  --platform "<candidate-platform.json>" \
  --project "<controlled-project.json>" \
  --compile "<compiled-pipeline.json>"
sha256sum "<candidate-platform.json>" "<compiled-pipeline.json>"
```

Expected output is a JSON object with `status` equal to `compiled`, a run ID,
stage count, and definition digest. Compilation validates discovery, trust,
registrations, selected providers, schemas, configuration, and grants. It does
not prove an external endpoint, account, credential, or live dependency.

Distinguish failures before changing anything:

| Observation | Cause class | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Manifest/schema/digest error | Package or trust input | Reject the candidate package |
| Duplicate ID or provider ambiguity | Registry selection | Select one exact registration; do not depend on order |
| Missing grant or denied resource | Authority policy | Confirm intended need; do not widen the grant merely to pass |
| Missing secret name | Secret configuration | Provision through its owner, then retry validation |
| Trusted registration import error, or external adapter rejection | Trusted module admission or unsupported external adapter runtime | Reject the candidate; inspect the named module and trusted import audit. External stage/observer imports are deferred until controlled isolated invocation |
| Project requests uninstalled stage | Project/package mismatch | Correct the project or select an approved package |

### 3. Activate and prove health

Compilation checks enabled registrations, configuration, trust, and grants.
For each package containing an enabled registration, it audits every trusted
stage, observer, and adapter entry in that package, including disabled siblings.
The audit imports those modules in permission-restricted child processes and
checks their exports; a disabled trusted sibling can therefore fail compilation.
Only the subsequent activation load is limited to enabled registrations, whose
`trusted_first_party` modules are imported in the host. Trusted code can thus load
even though no pipeline work starts. External stage and
observer registrations receive isolated invocation wrappers instead: compilation
does not import their modules or prove that their runtime imports and exported
functions will resolve. Validate those through a controlled isolated invocation
and its terminal result before admitting real work. External capability adapters
are rejected because the persistent isolated adapter runtime is unsupported.
Compilation does not call adapter factories or adapter `ready()`, create a run,
or prove a live dependency. See the [trust-specific activation boundary](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/c8987b18b450bc27571d5037cb6ce3fb26e0cbd0/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/registry/activation.ts#L55-L89).

A run then starts adapters in dependency order and awaits each adapter's
`ready()` result. The host races each factory and readiness call against
`shutdownTimeoutMs`. A readiness failure first revokes the failing adapter's
context and awaits its shutdown. Only after that cleanup settles can the outer
startup rollback revoke the other started contexts and attempt their shutdown.
No partially started adapter set becomes the usable runtime.
Failed-readiness teardown and startup rollback abort their shutdown signal after
`shutdownTimeoutMs`, but still await the adapter's shutdown promise. An adapter
that ignores the signal can therefore leave run startup pending indefinitely.
Pending failed-readiness cleanup also delays the outer rollback, so the earlier
adapters' contexts have not yet been revoked by that rollback.
See [adapter startup and shutdown limits](../understand/plugin-runtime.md#activation-is-fail-closed).
This startup transaction cannot reverse an external effect already accepted by
a service. After compile succeeds, start the controlled project only during its
approved window:

```bash
npm run pipeline -- \
  --platform "<candidate-platform.json>" \
  --project "<controlled-project.json>"
```

Take `<run-id>` from the start command when it returns one. Before audit,
complete [Inspect a Run](operate.md#inspect-a-run) in the same Bash shell.
Use that original candidate-platform path and run ID, confirm the run owner
has exited, stop new run and owning-adapter writes, and preserve verified raw
run and adapter copies. Audit can create locks and truncate an incomplete
journal tail before parsing. Require successful strict parsing of the copied
journals; retain rejected bytes and stop on any failure. Define the canonical
`preserve_run_state` helper from that section before this block:

```bash
export RUN_CONTROL_PLATFORM="<candidate-platform.json>"
export RUN_CONTROL_RUN_ID="<run-id>"
preserve_run_state || exit 1
audit_status=0
npm --silent run pipeline -- \
  --platform "$RUN_CONTROL_PLATFORM" \
  --audit "$RUN_CONTROL_RUN_ID" \
  > "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/audit.json" \
  2> "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/audit.stderr" || audit_status=$?
printf '%s\n' "$audit_status" > "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/audit.exit" || exit 1
test "$audit_status" -eq 0 || exit 1
```

Retain the raw-copy path, manifests, audit stdout/stderr, and actual exit status.
If an owner later authorizes canonical tail repair, keep original bytes,
reconcile external effects, and record the command and actual file changes.
If startup remains active, ownership is unknown, or adapter stores cannot be
quiesced and copied, stop before audit. Keep the original command output and
use the component owner's supported observation path. Process containment does
not prove the controlled project succeeded.

Stop new admission on
adapter startup or readiness failure, or when startup remains pending after its
timeout. Retain the adapter ID, dependency, configuration digest, elapsed time,
available run identity, and known or unresolved shutdown outcome. Do not treat
the timeout or a process stop as proof that cleanup completed. The plugin-runtime
maintainers own a stuck startup; the adapter owner must establish cleanup and
remaining resource ownership. Restore the dependency through its owner and
reconcile any uncertain external effect before retry. A process start
proves only that the process exists; adapter readiness proves its declared
startup checks; the controlled project's terminal result proves the selected
business operation.

Expected observation: the selected
registration appears in the resolved graph and attempt evidence, its functional
result succeeds, and audit state agrees with the terminal command output.
Registry activation alone is not health; the controlled functional result is
the health proof.

For endpoint, account, or data failures, use the
[canonical symptom diagnosis procedure](diagnose.md#canonical-symptom-diagnosis-procedure).
Do not retry an accepted external effect until its request and receipt are
reconciled.

### 4. Drain and disable

Stop admission of new projects that select the registration. Inventory each
pinned run from its retained start record and supported component observations.
Let safe active work finish under its original owner. Do not run audit while
that run or its owning adapter stores have active writers.

For each run whose owner has exited, complete
[Inspect a Run](operate.md#inspect-a-run) before audit. Use its original
platform and run ID, verify stopped writers, and preserve verified raw run and
owning-adapter copies. Audit can change lock files and incomplete journal tails.
Require strict copied-journal inspection to succeed; preserve rejected raw
bytes and stop on failure. With the canonical helper defined in the same shell:

```bash
export RUN_CONTROL_PLATFORM="<original-platform.json>"
export RUN_CONTROL_RUN_ID="<run-id>"
preserve_run_state || exit 1
audit_status=0
npm --silent run pipeline -- --platform "$RUN_CONTROL_PLATFORM" --audit "$RUN_CONTROL_RUN_ID" \
  > "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/audit.json" \
  2> "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/audit.stderr" || audit_status=$?
printf '%s\n' "$audit_status" > "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT/audit.exit" || exit 1
test "$audit_status" -eq 0 || exit 1
```

Retain a separate raw-copy path, manifests, audit output, and exit status for
each run. If a writer remains active or its ownership cannot be established,
keep the plugin and dependencies available and stop disablement. This page
provides no non-mutating live audit command. An owner-supported containment
procedure can stop a process, but cannot establish terminal completion. Any
later authorized canonical repair retains original bytes and records actual
changes through [Inspect a Run](operate.md#inspect-a-run).

There is no supported operator cancel command. If a run remains active or
waiting, keep the plugin package, schema, configuration, secrets, and dependency
available. Urgent process containment does not make the durable run cancelled.

After every pinned run is terminal, have the platform owner create a candidate
that removes the registration from provider selection, active adapters,
observers, and grants. These configuration removals do not independently disable
stage registrations: every stage selected by a newly admitted pipeline is enabled
from the discovered registry. For a package containing stages, keep admission
stopped and remove the entire package from the candidate `installationRoots`
discovery set before treating its stages as disabled. This affects all of that
package's registrations; identify and requalify dependent projects rather than
assuming an isolated stage-disable toggle exists.

Repeat the compile procedure against the candidate package set. Verify the old
stage registration is absent from discovery; a definition still requiring its
stage type must fail admission when no explicitly intended replacement provides
that type. Verify a controlled project using retained registrations still compiles
with their original identities. Configuration removal alone is not proof of stage
disablement. [Pipeline stage selection enables discovered stage owners](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/7994a51e16bc752357c3a801190b12b7d6a191a4/skills/nova/core/execution/engine-runtime.ts#L29-L49).

### 5. Replace or remove

For replacement, stage the new exact package outside the active discovery roots.
Have the platform owner select a candidate package set containing only one package
for each manifest ID. For a same-ID replacement, its candidate `installationRoots`
must discover the new package instead of the old package, never both. Disabling
an adapter, observer, or grant does not remove its package from discovery.
[Registry construction rejects duplicate package IDs before activation](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f99aecbb00cb399b46dfbbeb3ddb375fba6218e7/skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/registry/build.ts#L276-L283)
with `REGISTRY_PACKAGE_DUPLICATE`.

Repeat the compile procedure against that candidate configuration and prove the
new functional path before changing new-run admission. Stop if discovery includes
both versions or the owner cannot isolate their package sets. Keep the previous
configuration and exact digest-bound packages available for old pinned runs and
recovery; do not move or delete packages they still reference. Drain those runs
before retiring old selection and grants. Existing runs do not adopt the new
package merely because new admission selects it.

For external package removal, stop after drain unless an approved operator tool
calls the owned removal API with authorization and a direct child of the
installation root. The repository currently supplies no such general command.
Manual filesystem deletion is unsupported. Preserve built-in package files in
the selected source tree; do not delete them from a live checkout. Remove their
platform activation where applicable, but do not treat that alone as retirement
of a built-in package containing stages. Its package must also be absent from
the candidate discovery roots used for new admission, with the stage-absence and
dependent-project checks above. If those roots cannot isolate the package from
other required built-ins, independent stage-package retirement is unsupported:
stop, retain the package, and keep the affected new-run admission closed rather
than claim it is disabled. This changes only the candidate discovery set, not
source-tree files or old pinned-run packages.

### Recovery, cleanup, and evidence

Before activation, recovery is to discard the candidate configuration. After a
new run begins, restore the previous compatible platform configuration only for
new admission; existing runs remain bound to their original graph and package
snapshot. Reconcile uncertain effects before another run.

Remove unused temporary compiled files and candidate files only after retaining
their hashes and final decision. Revoke a plugin secret only after all consumers
are drained and the old identity is proved unused. Retain source commit,
catalogue identity, package and platform digests, grants, dependency owners,
secret names, compile output, functional result, audit, drain inventory,
replacement proof, cleanup result, and exact blocked step.

## Try Studio with the local sample

Use this procedure to learn visual editing and preview without a cluster, Nova,
an agent, or a database. Run it on the machine with your checkout and browser.
The development server listens on loopback, `127.0.0.1`, at port `4190`.
Loopback means that the browser must run on that machine. This page does not
provide a remote tunnel or a publicly exposed development server.

This sample is **temporary browser state**, not a Control project. Development
mode loads the sample directly and does not start a session or load a document
from Control. Typed changes call `applyOperation` in the browser. They create
local revision numbers, not database history. Reloading the page loads the
original sample again. The sample has one Home screen, one `default` state,
no assets, and no flows.

The source implements this isolation; its historical design reason is unknown.
A current technical inference is that it lets you check the editor without
production credentials. The cost is that you cannot prove persistence,
permissions, agent work, evaluation, approval, publication, or Nova handoff.
Use the deployed procedure below when those are the task. Reconsider the sample
boundary only when a separate, supported local service procedure provides those
contracts and checks.

### Prepare the local checkout

Use Node.js 24, npm, and a current Chromium-based browser. No Kubernetes,
Helm, database account, Tailscale session, or Prism Secret is required for this
sample. You need permission to install the locked dependencies in a disposable
checkout, write its local cache, and start a loopback listener. Do not use a
checkout with another task's dependency tree. Package installation can need
network access to the approved npm registry.

From the repository root, complete
[Locked Dependency Installation](quickstart.md#locked-dependency-installation).
Studio also needs development dependencies. If `NODE_ENV=production` or npm's
omit policy excludes them, the package owner must include them in the same
locked installation. In the disposable checkout, use:

```bash
npm ci --ignore-scripts --include=dev
```

Record its exit status and check that `package-lock.json` did not change.
Require exit `0`. Stop on installation, integrity, disk, or permission errors.
Do not change package versions or the lockfile to clear an error. If npm's
cache is not writable, select an approved writable cache with npm's `--cache`
option and repeat the unchanged locked installation. Do not alter system paths.
This additional install replaces the dependency tree; it does not install
Playwright browsers or their operating-system libraries.

### Start and edit the sample

1. From the repository root, enter the Prism package and start Vite:

   ```bash
   cd skills/prism
   npm run dev:studio
   ```

   Keep this terminal open. Require the reported local address to be
   `http://127.0.0.1:4190/`. Vite can choose another port when `4190` is busy.
   Stop this instance with Ctrl+C if it reports another port. Identify the
   existing listener through the host owner; do not terminate an unknown
   process or assume that its page is this checkout.

2. Open `http://127.0.0.1:4190/` in the browser on that machine, without query
   parameters. Expect **Prism**, **Studio development**, **Revision 1**, and the
   **Home** screen. In the editor, the sample heading reads **Deployments**.
   No login prompt or project chooser is part of this development path.

3. On a desktop window wider than 800 CSS pixels, select **Edit text** in the
   right inspector. The initial selected node is the sample heading. Expect
   **Revision 2** and **Services**. This button is a fixed text toggle, not a
   free-text dialog. The inspector's **Content** field is read-only. Use the
   visual editor's property controls for arbitrary supported text.

4. Select **Insert action**. Expect the revision to advance and a button named
   **Inspect** to appear. This inserts a typed button at the end of the current
   screen's root. Select **Move last to top** to move it before the heading;
   expect another revision and the changed order. Wait for each result before
   the next action. The visual editor also supports insertion, removal,
   duplication, movement, and the properties it exposes. It does not expose
   responsive-property editing. Changing an existing block's node type is not
   supported. See [Typed visual edits](#typed-visual-edits) for copy limits.

5. Select **Preview**. Expect an iframe named **Isolated prototype preview**
   with **Services** and **Inspect** in the order you selected. Select the
   **Viewport** values **Compact**, **Regular**, and **Wide** to inspect the
   layout. These change preview/editor sizing; they do not add responsive
   patches to the document. The sample has no declared flow, so **Inspect**
   does not navigate to another screen. Select **Edit** to return to the editor.

6. Reload the browser page. Expect **Revision 1**, **Deployments**, and no
   inserted **Inspect** button. This reset is the final check for the local
   sample. It is expected data loss, not a failed database save.

At window widths of 800 CSS pixels or less, Studio hides the desktop navigator
and inspector. Use **Navigate** to open the screen sheet. Use **Insert**, then
**Insert action**, to add the sample button. The sheet does not close after
insertion; select **Close** before inspecting the preview. The desktop
**Edit text** and **Move last to top** controls are not in these sheets. Widen
the window for the desktop procedure. The top **Viewport** selector changes
the design viewport, not the browser width or this control visibility.

> **Source evidence — temporary development state**
>
> **Claim:** Development startup bypasses the Control session and loads a fresh
> sample; typed edits apply locally and reload discards them.
>
> **Implementation:** [`App` development startup](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/studio/app.tsx#L97-L104) ·
> [`commit` development branch](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/studio/app.tsx#L161-L168) ·
> [`applyOperation` validation and revision increment](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/domain/index.ts#L105-L114).
>
> **Contract or setting:** [`dev:studio` script](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/package.json#L23-L23) ·
> [Vite loopback and port](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/studio/vite.config.ts#L5-L9) ·
> [sample identity and revision](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/studio/dev-fixture.ts#L3-L12) ·
> [sample screen, states, assets, and flows](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/studio/dev-fixture.ts#L25-L52).
>
> **Test evidence:** The [maintained development browser tests](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/studio/tests/studio.spec.mjs#L3-L39)
> cover the desktop text toggle, preview, mobile insertion, and page width.
> Find their execution status in [Local Development and Verification](#local-development-and-verification).
>
> **Revision:** `f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f`.
>
> **Limit:** Local revision and preview behavior do not establish persistent
> state, authenticated access, worker execution, or a live Studio-to-Nova journey.

### Do not use service actions in the sample

Development mode does not provide a local substitute for every visible button.
Do not select **Check design**, **Approve**, or **Propose change** in this sample.
Evaluation and proposals need a document identity from the URL. Approval also
needs a project identity. These handlers have no development implementation.
With the plain local URL they show **Prism cannot open** with a missing-identity
error. Adding query parameters does not connect Vite to Control or enable these
operations.

**Revision history** does not return local undo history. **What Prism learned**
needs the preference service; it is not local learning. The sample contains no
directions or brief. Do not treat an empty history or preference panel as proof
that a service accepted a request.

> **Source evidence — service actions remain outside the sample**
>
> **Claim:** Evaluation, natural-language changes, history, preferences, and
> approval retain their service-client paths; the local sample supplies none
> of their authenticated results.
>
> **Implementation:** [`propose` requires a URL document ID](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/studio/app.tsx#L184-L197) ·
> [preference and history reads](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/studio/app.tsx#L199-L230) ·
> [`approve` identity guard](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/studio/app.tsx#L350-L360) ·
> [`evaluateDesign` document guard](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/studio/app.tsx#L406-L411) ·
> [failure screen](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/studio/app.tsx#L491-L499).
>
> **Contract or setting:** [Development startup returns before session setup](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/prism/studio/app.tsx#L97-L110).
>
> **Test evidence:** The maintained sample tests above do not prove service
> actions. No successful local evaluation, proposal, approval, or publication
> is established by this sample procedure.
>
> **Revision:** `f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f`.
>
> **Limit:** A visible control is not an available local service operation.
> Persistent use requires the deployed prerequisites and identities below.

### Stop, recover, and clean up the sample

| Observation | Check and safe action |
| --- | --- |
| `vite: not found` | Check whether the locked install included development dependencies. Stop the start command. Repeat the locked installation with `--include=dev` only in the disposable checkout. |
| Vite exits before reporting the address | Read the terminal error. Distinguish package loading, file access, and port errors. Stop before browser testing; do not change product files to bypass startup. |
| Another port is reported | Stop this Vite process. Have the host owner identify the listener on `4190`. Do not test an unknown existing server. |
| The page is blank or the sample does not appear | Record browser console and terminal errors, URL, and source revision. Confirm that this terminal owns the reported address. Reload once after fixing a known load failure; stop for Prism maintainers if it remains unknown. |
| **Prism cannot open** after a service action | Retain the error, then reload the plain local URL. This discards local edits and restores the sample. It is not recovery for a deployed pending request. |
| Edits disappear on reload | Expected in development mode. There is no local save, export, or history-restore procedure. Repeat the sample edits if wanted; do not infer lost production state. |
| Browser test cannot launch | Install the locked Playwright browser and approved host libraries. Stop that test on a failed prerequisite; do not replace its executable or test configuration. |

To abandon or finish the sample, close its browser tab and press Ctrl+C in its
own Vite terminal. Confirm that this process exits. A restart opens another
fresh sample; there is no pending design job to resume and no cluster state to
clean up. Do not delete any production project, approval, bundle, or database.
Keep the source revision, tool versions, local address, command output, observed
revision/preview/reset results, errors, and exit status as local evidence.
Exclude cookies, tokens, and private keys. Remove only this task's disposable
checkout and owned build/test output after its owner confirms retention.

The Prism maintainers own unresolved sample loading or editor failures. Closure
requires the unchanged supported start command to load the sample, complete the
edit/preview/reset steps at the affected window size, and stop its process
cleanly. This does not close deployment or service-action limitations.

## Canonical Prism and Studio Procedure
<!-- operator-task: prism-studio -->

This page is the sole authority for `prism-studio`. Choose the local sample above
for temporary editor practice. The deployed procedure below has two phases.
The local sample is not a prerequisite or evidence for either deployed phase.

For [deployment and health](#deploy-prism), start with an existing cluster that
passed install preflight, an exact selected Prism service/agent release,
prepared Secrets, the SPIRE identity service and its
[Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver](../reference/glossary.md#csi), native-worker dependencies, sufficient
database/artifact/backup capacity, and the required private-access configuration.
A Nova approval wait is not a deployment prerequisite. Run deployment commands
from `<repository-root>` on the administration machine.

For [the Studio journey](#the-complete-studio-journey), first complete deployment
and the selected service health checks. Before submitting design work, verify
[SPIFFE agent admission](#spiffe-agent-admission) on Control and the agent path,
including the exact trusted agent identity. SPIFFE identifies workloads; Control
also checks which identity may claim jobs and commit designs. A healthy HMAC
worker does not enable this journey. Verify the named human's private access.
Then use the original Nova run only when its selected notification provider has
verified compatibility with the Prism payload. Nova dispatches, stores a wait
record, and publishes the notification before returning its stage wait. The
installed messaging adapter blocks that return. Before a human changes or approves the design,
verify that original request and wait; stop if dispatch or wait creation is
missing or uncertain. Run Studio actions through that human's private browser
session. Release receipts, Prism Control state, immutable artifact bytes,
Studio approval, Nova wait state, and Nova audit are the authorities.

> Nova [dispatches the original architecture before it stores a wait record and attempts the notification](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/nova/plugins/prism-design/src/stage.ts#L21-L34).

Before any cluster command on this page, complete
[Bind Cluster Authority](install.md#bind-cluster-authority). Keep the same bound
shell for the whole Prism task. Every raw `kubectl`, Helm, or
`scripts/deploy.sh` command below must inherit its exported read-only
`KUBECONFIG`, `NAMESPACE`, and `PRISM_NAMESPACE`. The binding procedure validates
and freezes the independently supplied application and Prism namespace names.
Use `bound_kubectl`, `bound_helm`, and `bound_deploy` from that shell. The observed
resources, rendered namespaces, and mutated releases must all name the same
`PRISM_NAMESPACE`; each shown `<context>` must equal `EXPECTED_CONTEXT`. Run
`assert_cluster_binding` immediately before each command block. Stop on any
mismatch and follow the binding section's recovery; never fall back to the
default kubeconfig.

Before cluster mutation, run:

```bash
assert_cluster_binding
npm run verify:prism:deploy-script
node scripts/updates/materialize-release.mjs --family=runtime --check
bound_deploy render prism
```

The three verification/render commands must exit zero after the binding
assertion succeeds. At the recorded revision, `verify:prism:deploy-script`
passed its workflow, deploy-command contract, and Bash syntax checks.
At that recorded revision, `materialize-release.mjs --family=runtime --check`
stopped because `releases/runtime-images.json` was absent.
That historical checkout had no selected runtime release to deploy.
Retain that historical failure; it does not establish the release state of a later checkout.
Local script verification does not prove an installed Prism service.

For your selected checkout, use [Preflight Without Mutation](install.md#preflight-without-mutation).
A present receipt can still fail verification.
Any failed binding, selection, or render check stops deployment.
After the release owner supplies a valid selected runtime release, repeat every
preflight and render check. Complete [Before You Start](#before-you-start),
[Deploy Prism](#deploy-prism), [The Complete Studio Journey](#the-complete-studio-journey),
and [Completion Checklist](#completion-checklist) in order.
Stop on an unknown identity/digest, failed readiness level, superseded
architecture, uncertain agent job, revision conflict, blocking evaluation,
stale approval, bundle verification failure, mismatched/expired wait, or
incomplete cleanup. Do not create a replacement identity to clear a conflict.

Recovery uses [Safe Recovery Procedures](#safe-recovery-procedures) for the
same project and identities. Backup/restore uses the
[canonical recovery procedure](recovery.md#canonical-backup-and-restore-procedure),
upgrade uses the [canonical upgrade procedure](maintenance.md#canonical-upgrade-and-rollback-procedure),
and removal uses the [canonical decommission procedure](maintenance.md#canonical-decommission-procedure).
Retain release/configuration digests, commands and outputs, readiness, run and
wait IDs, project/architecture/round/document/revision/approval/bundle IDs,
preview/evaluation evidence, resume signal digest, final audit, recovery and
cleanup. Never retain session cookies, tokens, passwords, or private keys.

Use this page to:

- prepare and deploy Prism;
- find a project in Studio;
- compare and select a design direction;
- make visual or natural-language changes;
- inspect, restore, preview, evaluate, approve, and publish a revision;
- resume a Nova run only after verifying its active Core approval wait;
- diagnose a stopped or uncertain operation without creating duplicate work.

Prism is a design system, not an application generator.
Its approved output contains a structured Design Document, a design specification,
acceptance criteria, preview evidence, assets, checksums, and a manifest.
The implementation pipeline remains responsible for production code.

> **The important authority boundary**
>
> Studio attempts approval first and immutable publication second. Approval alone does not publish a bundle or resume Nova.
> For a run with a verified active Core approval wait, a separate operator-created Nova signal resumes the run. Its issuer is
> caller-supplied and unsigned; CLI access is the effective authority. Nova then asks Prism for
> the approved bundle and verifies all content before it accepts the handoff.
>
> [The Prism stage attempts wait creation and notification before returning its wait, and validates later approval guidance](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/skills/nova/plugins/prism-design/src/stage.ts#L8-L34).

## Before You Start

You need all of the following items:

1. A reviewed runtime release selection with Prism image digests.
2. A Kubernetes cluster with the required Prism namespace and image-pull Secret.
3. PostgreSQL storage and artifact storage with sufficient capacity.
4. The native worker host policy and its generated Prism values.
5. A registered SPIFFE CSI driver (`csi.spiffe.io`). The maintained Prism deploy command requires it for every deployment. The [unconditional guard](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/scripts/deploy.sh#L1739-L1742) calls the [driver-registration check](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/f88a8c5c56adc2098d73804c85c6f41d7d7a239f/scripts/deploy.sh#L951-L958). Registration alone does not prove the [socket delivery or workload identity](worker-trust.md#preconditions).
6. The Tailscale access configuration when Tailscale exposure is enabled. Verify actual private Studio access after deployment.
7. `gatewayToken-prism` in `openclaw-shared-secrets`.
8. A valid Prism code bundle URL and a commit that matches the selected runtime receipt.
9. The authorized operator issuer ID used by the Nova Prism stage.
10. SPIFFE-enabled Control and a matched agent trust path with the exact identity
    that Control permits. Complete [SPIFFE agent admission](#spiffe-agent-admission)
    before Nova dispatch, a child round, or a natural-language revision.

Stop if an identity, digest, Secret, or native host binding is unknown.
Do not replace an unknown value with a new value during an active run.
That action can make a durable request impossible to reconcile.

### SPIFFE agent admission

The governed journey requires SPIFFE mode on Control and the matched agent
connection. The bridge must claim a durable job before it starts external work.
Control requires the same trusted Prism Agent identity for job claim, job status,
job finish, direction commit, and natural-language revision commit. CSI driver
registration is a separate deployment prerequisite; it does not enable this
application trust mode or grant agent permission.

Before submitting design work, the release and workload-trust owners must verify:

1. The selected service values and rendered Control environment enable SPIFFE:
   `workerTrust.spiffe.enabled: true` produces `WORKER_TRUST_SPIFFE_ENABLED=true`.
2. Control's `PRISM_TRUSTED_AGENT_SPIFFE_ID` equals the agent's issued workload
   identity. The service chart constructs it as
   `spiffe://<trust-domain>/ns/<agent-namespace>/sa/<agent-service-account>` from
   the selected `workerTrust.spiffe` values. Each placeholder is that selected
   value, not a new identity chosen during diagnosis.
3. The selected agent release enables its SPIFFE path, receives its credential
   and Workload API socket, and reaches Control through the matched trust proxy.
   Follow [Worker Trust](worker-trust.md#canonical-worker-trust-procedure).
4. An authorized isolated agent exercise proves job claim, direction commit,
   and natural-language revision commit permission for that exact identity.
   Keep this evidence separate from health probes and from the production
   request's result.

The service chart defaults SPIFFE to `false`; the development agent overlay
enables it. Those inputs alone do not establish a matched selected release.
If this prerequisite is absent or unverified, stop before design submission.
The blocked step is the agent's job claim or result commit, even if Control can
store a request and a HMAC worker can pass health checks. The release and trust
owners must supply a matched configuration and prove the permissions above
before the journey opens. This page provides no generic command to repair trust.

If work was already admitted, preserve its original run, architecture, request,
round, instruction/base revision, key, and job/fence identities. Stop new work
and follow [Agent work blocked by trust](#agent-work-blocked-by-trust).
Do not replay an uncertain launch or switch trust mode to clear an active
worker error.

## Configuration Sources and Precedence

Prism has more than one configuration owner.
Do not treat all settings as equivalent.

### Deployment precedence

The effective service values use this order, from lowest to highest precedence:

1. Chart defaults in `charts/prism/values.yaml`.
2. Materialized selected values in `releases/values/prism.yaml`.
3. The optional private file named by `PRISM_VALUES_FILE` before the deploy script starts.
4. Deploy-script image, trust, namespace, and Secret overrides.

The Prism agent uses the same pattern:

1. The shared agent chart defaults.
2. Materialized selected values in `releases/values/prism-agent.yaml`.
3. The optional private file named by `PRISM_AGENT_VALUES_FILE` before the deploy script starts.
4. The generated code-bundle override and selected LiteLLM memory-search embedding endpoint.

The script saves the optional file names as overlays and then replaces the shell
variables with the materialized release paths. This detail explains why an
operator-supplied file adds private values but cannot replace selected release truth.

### Main Helm values

The [generated recursive value reference](../reference/helm-values.md#recursive-value-reference)

Apply these task rules to the selected values:

| Decision | Required operator proof and consequence |
| --- | --- |
| Service and agent images | Keep each repository with its receipt-selected immutable digest. An empty digest blocks deploy. A mutable tag does not establish release identity. |
| Native host binding | Use generated `worker.native` values. The node, pool namespace, and policy digest must match the prepared host policy; Pod resources do not replace native per-attempt limits. |
| Control and worker replicas | Keep each at exactly one. Control owns one ReadWriteOnce artifact claim; the worker owns one native pool. The chart rejects other counts. Studio replicas do not add canonical state or approval authority. |
| Worker shutdown | Keep `worker.native.closeTimeoutMs` inside `worker.shutdownTimeoutMs`, and keep the full shutdown inside `worker.terminationGracePeriodSeconds`. Too little time can leave ownership uncertain. |
| PostgreSQL | Keep chart-owned PostgreSQL enabled for this maintained deploy, smoke, migration, and backup procedure. Chart rendering without PostgreSQL does not provide an external-database workflow. |
| Database, artifacts, and backup | Size the independent claims from measured growth and restore time. Local backup and byte ceilings do not provide off-host recovery or automatic expiry. |
| Ingestion | Enable only with approved source policy and explicit positive CPU/memory requests and limits. Quarantine expiry does not delete published corpus or bundle data. |
| Private Studio access | Bind the selected Tailscale hostname and operator namespace to the approved private-access record. Prove authorized and unauthorized access separately. |
| SPIFFE trust | The governed agent journey requires SPIFFE-enabled Control and the exact trusted agent identity. Configure the trust domain, namespaces, service accounts, CSI socket, and proxy images as one policy; complete [agent admission](#spiffe-agent-admission) before submission. An incomplete identity set blocks startup. |
| Personal preference | Select only an existing authenticated Prism subject in `control.pipelinePreferenceSubject`. Empty disables personal preference binding for pipeline rounds. |
| Product decisions | Enable only with the separate operator, issuer, key, controller, CA, audience, and revision policy. This authority is distinct from design approval. |

The schema closes the top-level object and selected security-sensitive groups,
but some nested objects remain open. An unknown nested key can pass schema
validation while no template reads it. Compare the selected values with the
generated inventory's receiving source and the rendered manifests. Reject an
unconsumed override; schema acceptance alone does not prove an effect.
