## 1. Establish operator, target and client prerequisites

Complete [cluster/release binding and scoped authority](../install.md#bind-cluster-authority)
and the [Kubernetes fixture procedure](kubernetes-fixture.md). Use the canonical
[runtime capability reference](../../reference/buster-runtime-configuration.md)
and [exposure suite contract](../../reference/buster-suites.md#5-tailscale-exposure-suite)
for settings rather than maintaining a second field inventory here.

The platform owner must provide the official operator, `IngressClass/tailscale`,
the actual controller/fixture namespaces, a pullable digest-pinned application
image and selected Service/port/path. Its client needs the runtime's permitted
namespace prefix, allowed public host suffixes and scoped lease get/patch
permissions; the namespace fixture separately needs its own create/read/delete
authority. A grant in one namespace or capability does not grant the other.

The Tailnet owner must provide OAuth authority, approved operator/proxy tags,
MagicDNS/HTTPS readiness and the exact ACL/grant policy for this route. The
checked-in values leave OAuth credentials outside Git and select default tags
`tag:k8s-operator` and `tag:k8s`; private overlays can change that selection.
Record the selected policy and allowed client identities, not assumed defaults
or Secret values. A ready operator is not proof that the intended client may
reach the target.

Before a retained-route exercise, register one permitted and one deliberately
unpermitted client/device identity, the same target hostname/path/port, bounded
observation window, application authentication policy, and cleanup owner. The
Tailnet/policy owner must provide the actual client and policy-observation
controls. This repository supplies no universal Tailnet ACL edit, device-login
or policy-verdict CLI. Missing client or policy authority is a safe stop, not a
reason to expose the route publicly or disable authentication.

## 2. Allocate through a supported workflow

Use the actual project compile/start and stopped-writer observation commands in
[Run a Buster Suite](buster-suite.md#5-submit-and-observe-in-production).
The owning project supplies its resolved plan, grants, immutable image and
checked-manifest input. The exposure node consumes the Kubernetes deployment's
`deployment` value and the HTTP node consumes the exposure output. It is not a
standalone `tailscale expose` command or an arbitrary `kubectl Ingress` patch.

For the separately registered **ephemeral live preflight**, the supported
wrapper command is:

```bash
assert_cluster_binding || exit 126
export TAILSCALE_PROBE_IMAGE="<registry/repository>@sha256:<64-hex-digest>"
./scripts/deploy.sh nova-tailscale-preflight "$TAILSCALE_PROBE_IMAGE"
```

The linked install procedure defines the bound shell and selected checkout.
This command allocates real remote work and a route; it is not a dry run. Its
probe image must serve HTTP on container port 8080. The service maps port 80;
the plan uses a checked-manifest producer, deployment fixture, exposure fixture
and a blocking HTTP request. The optional expected-text setting belongs to that
preflight's existing configuration, not a new ad hoc URL substitution.

The preflight uses `release`, not `await-readiness`, and cleanup removes the
route before its wrapper returns. It is therefore not an opportunity to perform
later independent-client ACL probes against a still-retained route. For those
checks use a separately owned retained project route whose actual result and
expiry remain current. Do not rerun preflight to recover an unknown old lease.

## 3. Verify the current lease generation and endpoint

The exposure runtime first verifies the deployment lease's namespace, Service,
port, Ready phase and exact unexpired deadline. It patches the exposure under
an owner/request digest and resource version, then requires the controller's
current generation, matching owner and Ready exposure phase. A stale Ready
condition or a matching hostname alone is insufficient.

Read the typed result and original imported evidence. Keep lease name/namespace,
current lease UID/resource version/generation, owner/request identity, image and
manifest digest, selected Service/path, HTTPS URL/hostname, expiry and plan/job/
result/decision identities together. The ordinary deployment provider has a
weaker Ready/Rejected wait; use the exposure's stronger generation/owner
observation for this route, not the basic lease phase alone.

The returned URL must be HTTPS, have the selected path and a permitted host
suffix, with no userinfo or fragment. Its host must match controller status and
any requested hostname constraint. This validates the result shape and route
identity; DNS, TLS, ACL and the application response still require the actual
client path. Do not use an external public URL or a direct Service response to
replace that check.

For the ephemeral preflight, require all four remote nodes passed, status
`completed`, decision `passed`, matching complete imported evidence and zero
runner cleanup errors. The initial `nova-tailscale-production-preflight.v1`
receipt reports runner cleanup separately from cluster cleanup. The wrapper
waits for observed namespace and lease deletion, confirms absence, updates the
cleanup fields and signs/verifies the production receipt. Preserve its actual
terminal status and `dist/verification/tailscale-exposure-production-receipt.json`;
a signing or wrapper failure does not prove that no route existed.

## 4. Observe allowed access and a meaningful negative

For a still-owned retained route, have each registered client owner independently
verify its current device/user identity and use the **same retained HTTPS URL**
inside the approved window. Record client identity, route/lease generation,
policy version, UTC interval, DNS result, certificate/host validation and bounded
request outcome. Use its actual authorized application reader; a network
connection or generic HTTP 200 is not application correctness.

The unpermitted-client result must distinguish policy denial from DNS failure,
TLS failure, timeout, expired lease and an application authentication response.
Correlate it with the Tailnet owner's authoritative policy observation. A failed
curl or a client not connected to the Tailnet does not by itself prove an ACL
negative. Conversely, a fixture's successful Buster HTTP node proves that test
client path, not every permitted user or rejection of an unpermitted device.

If the application has authentication, test the declared missing/wrong credential
behavior separately through its protected client mechanism. Do not call an
application 401/403 a Tailnet ACL result. The simple preflight image is not a
demo-auth proof; use the owning application's actual security contract. Never
print session tokens or credentials to supply evidence.

If a required client/policy probe is unavailable, retain the exact missing
client/target/policy authority and safe stop. Do not fabricate a negative result
from successful DNS, an Ingress object or source tests.

## 5. Transfer readiness ownership without overwriting a successor

For `await-readiness`, the lease must have cleanup policy `retain`, a nonempty
UID, verified immutable image and manifest digest. The handoff binds that UID,
original exposure owner/request, expiry, image and manifest to a new readiness
owner and phase `awaiting-readiness`. The runtime patches the handoff with
resource-version protection, then requires the controller to observe the new
owner and current exposure generation before returning it.

Retain that exact `demo-exposure-handoff.v1` and its observed generation. The
old provider's cleanup is now superseded; it must not switch the successor's
route Off. A repeated original request can observe its existing exact handoff;
a changed source request, handoff record or generation is a conflict, not a
reason to overwrite annotations.

This is not committed demo readiness. The separate trusted producer verifies
live lease/Ingress, image/manifest, generated credentials and delivery evidence
before committing readiness. Follow the canonical demo procedure rather than
patching status or treating a notification receipt as approval. After commit,
its retained exposure snapshot/owner and deadline govern subsequent decisions.

## 6. Failure, release and cleanup

For an approved OAuth-rejection exercise, use
[Tailscale Authentication Rejected](../diagnose.md#tailscale-authentication-rejected)
with its bound namespace/Secret/deployment identities and secure restore source.
It allocates a new route because an old device can remain usable despite a bad
OAuth credential. Restore the original Secret/operator path and confirm cleanup
through that owning procedure; do not rotate a real credential casually or
leave its failure trap disarmed.

An RBAC denial, expired/mismatched lease, denied host, timeout, controller
failure or unresolved mutation is its actual failed boundary. Failed prepare
attempts a bounded owned rollback to Off; rollback can fail too. Preserve both
errors and current owner/generation. A stale attempt must neither report
success nor disable a newer exposure. Do not start a replacement route to hide
uncertain prior ownership.

Under `release`, provider cleanup invokes the actual exposure release; the
runtime sets purpose `gate`/provider `off` only while ownership still matches and
waits for current owner/generation Off. Superseded cleanup returns without
removing the successor's route. The returned `releaseAction` is an owner-tested
lease patch generated by this runtime, not an unconditional namespace delete.
Validate the original trusted result and current lease before an authorized
operator uses that action; do not blindly evaluate text from an unverified
receipt. Its JSON test checks the owner annotation, not an atomic lease-UID
precondition; never describe it as a universal UID-fenced delete command.

For a handed-off or committed route, use its **current** demo lifecycle owner,
release/decision/expiry procedure and retention policy. An old release action
can reject its changed owner; that rejection protects the successor and is not
permission to strip the owner test. Do not edit readiness/product status or
delete retained namespace/storage to force cleanup.

Observe actual exposure Off/Ingress absence, then the namespace fixture's
selected deletion or retained deadline. Keep distinct runner cleanup, API
observed absence and external Tailnet device/route retirement. The repository
wrapper checks cluster namespace/lease absence, not independent Tailnet device
inventory or every prior client's denial. The Tailnet owner must provide those
external retirement observations where required. TTL reaching its deadline
alone does not prove successful reconciliation or deletion.

Retain original source/plan/result evidence, exact route/lease/handoff identities,
positive and negative client observations, release/rollback failures and final
cleanup/retention authority. Do not delete canonical evidence or revoke a shared
OAuth identity as fixture cleanup.

## Input Set

Use these three files from the same checkout:

| Input | Exact file | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pipeline | [approval.pipeline.json](wait-resume/approval.pipeline.json) | One `approval` stage of type `kubeclaw.decision.human-approval`; no dependent stage or external product change. |
| Platform template | [platform.template.json](wait-resume/platform.template.json) | Exact registrations, grants, loopback receiver, secret selector, and storage placeholders. Materialize a private copy before use. |
| Signal template | [signal.template.json](wait-resume/signal.template.json) | All eight required envelope fields and the approval payload. Replace its identities and deliberately stale time from the new durable wait. Never submit the unchanged template. |

The wait-stage package is `skills/nova/plugins/human-approval/plugin.json`,
registration `kubeclaw.human-approval:approval`, module `src/stage.ts`, export
`execute`. This exercise uses the generic approval registration, not the
separate architecture approval registration. Generic approval accepts a summary
and an operator decision; it does not bind a source/report digest. Use a
separate contract when that binding is required.

The pipeline sets `maxAttempts: 2`, `maxRemediationCycles: 0`,
`timeoutMs: 10000`, and `timeoutMinutes: 60`. The initial waiting attempt consumes
one attempt. The resumed attempt consumes the second. Setting `maxAttempts: 1`
would exhaust the attempt budget when the stage tries to wait. The 60-minute
expiry limits when Core accepts the decision. It is distinct from the 10-second
stage execution limit. This guide schedules no retry or remediation.

The platform selects these providers and grants:

| Consumer | Capability and provider | Effective scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kubeclaw.human-approval:approval` | `signal.wait` → `kubeclaw.wait-store:waits` | `approval.resolved`, issuer ID `operator:local` |
| Same stage | `operator.request` → `kubeclaw.operator-messaging:operator` | Target `operators` |
| Operator adapter | `network.http` → `kubeclaw.network-http:http` | Loopback origin `http://127.0.0.1:18765`; POST, listed headers, and byte/time limits also enforced by adapter configuration |
| Operator adapter | `secrets.read` → `kubeclaw.secret-resolver:secrets` | Secret name `operator.webhook`, selected from environment variable `WAIT_REHEARSAL_WEBHOOK_KEY` |

The notification adapter signs its HTTP body with an HMAC key. That transport
signature authenticates the notification to this local receiver. The later
resume envelope is **unsigned**. Its issuer is self-asserted by the file's
creator. Restricted signal creation and CLI access are the effective operator
authority; issuer matching does not authenticate a person.

> **Source evidence — installed stage and budgets**
>
> **Claim:** Generic approval creates one wait and notification, then applies resumed guidance in a separate attempt.
>
> **Implementation:** [`execute` branches on guidance before creating effects](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ffb0b7a6393f7db44eb948f3ff8346b4b4b50f1a/skills/nova/plugins/human-approval/src/stage.ts#L13-L54). [The reducer counts completed attempts and stops an exhausted wait](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ffb0b7a6393f7db44eb948f3ff8346b4b4b50f1a/skills/nova/core/lifecycle/reducer.ts#L69-L72), [wait projection](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ffb0b7a6393f7db44eb948f3ff8346b4b4b50f1a/skills/nova/core/lifecycle/reducer.ts#L96-L101), [attempt count](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ffb0b7a6393f7db44eb948f3ff8346b4b4b50f1a/skills/nova/core/lifecycle/reducer.ts#L124-L128).
>

[`parseApprovalGuidance` validates decision, payload issuer, and reason](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ffb0b7a6393f7db44eb948f3ff8346b4b4b50f1a/skills/nova/plugins/human-approval/src/approval.ts#L102-L129).
>
> **Test evidence:** [The production-package local HTTP fixture asserts one notification and two causal attempts](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ffb0b7a6393f7db44eb948f3ff8346b4b4b50f1a/tests/verification/reliability/operator-retention-authority-fixture.test.mjs#L83-L125). Focused plugin boundary and guidance unit checks passed locally. These checks do not prove a completed lifecycle.

## Starting Conditions

Use an isolated Linux operator host with Node.js 24 and the paired npm version.
Complete [the canonical checkout and dependency setup](../quickstart.md#locked-dependency-installation).
Run all commands from that checkout, in Bash, as the same restricted operator.
Define `preserve_run_state` from [Inspect a Run](../operate.md#inspect-a-run) in
that terminal before starting. Its platform and run variables are bound below.
Keep this function available until the final audit.
The repository and installed packages must stay unchanged during the run.
Record the full commit and require a clean checkout before the measured run.
These instructions apply to the source revision above; a changed package or
graph requires a new governed run.

The host must have `/usr/bin/flock` with `--exclusive`, `--timeout`, and
`--conflict-exit-code`. Test the exact interface on a disposable file:

```bash
lock_probe=$(mktemp)
if /usr/bin/flock --exclusive --timeout 1 --conflict-exit-code 75 "$lock_probe" true; then
  rm "$lock_probe"
else
  probe_status=$?
  rm "$lock_probe"
  printf 'Stop: required flock interface failed, exit %s\n' "$probe_status" >&2
  exit 1
fi
```

Stop on failure. A `PATH` override cannot replace the fixed executable. Do not
disable locking or substitute a lock mock. Use a platform-approved operator
host that passes this exact prerequisite before continuing.

The local exercise needs an unused loopback port 18765, a new private directory
outside the checkout, capacity for Core/delivery/wait records, and permission to
start and stop the disposable receiver. It requires no cluster or live provider.
Stop on a bind error; do not use an unrelated service already on that port.

## Reject the Wrong Inputs, Then Resume Once

This helper invokes only the canonical explicit-graph resume command. It
retains each response and status. Run it in the original operator terminal.

```bash
resume_case() {
  case_name=$1
  signal_file=$2
  resume_status=0
  npm run pipeline -- \
    --platform "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/platform.json" \
    --pipeline "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/pipeline.json" \
    --run-id "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_RUN_ID" \
    --signal "$signal_file" \
    > "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/$case_name.stdout" 2> "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/$case_name.stderr" || resume_status=$?
  printf '%s\n' "$resume_status" > "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/$case_name.exit"
}
resume_case wrong-wait "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/wrong-wait.signal.json"
authority_snapshot after-wrong-wait before
```

Require exit 1 and `WAIT_UNKNOWN_OR_STALE:wait:wrong-rehearsal`. Compare the
five retained authority files with the before checksums; require unchanged
bytes and absent signal journal. Stop on any changed authority or other error.

Then test the wrong envelope issuer:

```bash
resume_case wrong-issuer "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/wrong-issuer.signal.json"
authority_snapshot after-wrong-issuer before
```

Require exit 1 and `WAIT_ISSUER_DENIED:operator:operator:wrong`. Require the same
unchanged authority files and absent signal journal. The payload issuer stays
unchanged in this negative case, so it tests Core's envelope issuer matching.
Do not correct a rejected signal by editing durable state.

Submit the reviewed valid bytes only after both negative checks pass:

```bash
resume_case valid "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/valid.signal.json"
```

Require valid exit 0 and `status: succeeded` before the final audit. If the
response is lost, nonzero, or uncertain, stop and use the preservation and
reconciliation steps in [Failure and Interruption](#failure-and-interruption).
After the command exits and all writers are stopped, preserve raw state again:

```bash
preserve_rehearsal_state || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT" > "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/final.raw-state.txt"
cp -R -- "$RUN_CONTROL_OBSERVATION_ROOT" "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/final.raw-state" || exit 1
npm run pipeline -- \
  --platform "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/platform.json" \
  --audit "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_RUN_ID" \
  > "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/final.audit.stdout" 2> "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/final.audit.stderr"
printf '%s\n' "$?" > "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/final.audit.exit"
authority_snapshot after-valid
```

Require valid exit 0, `status: succeeded`, stage `approval` succeeded,
`attemptsUsed: 2`, and audit exit 0. Require these causal observations:

1. The first `attempt.completed` result is `wait`.
2. Exactly one `wait.resolved` names this wait. Its `causationId` equals the
   signal's `signalId`, and its payload contains the exact submitted signal.
3. A second, different attempt ID completes with `passed`, after the resolution.
4. `signals.jsonl` contains one signal. The final journal records `run.succeeded`.
5. The wait store, delivery store, and receiver file are unchanged. There is
   still one HTTP notification and no second publish effect. No remediation
   cycle has been used.

Record the event, effect, and signal journal checksums at this point. The valid
decision has advanced durable state. There is no rollback operation that
restores the earlier wait. Preserve the completed run; use a new run for new work.

Replay the same file without changing a byte, time, ID, or key:

```bash
resume_case replay "$WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT/valid.signal.json"
authority_snapshot after-replay after-valid
```

Require exit 1 with `WAIT_RUN_TERMINAL` for this successful run. Other supported
stale-resolution paths can return `WAIT_ALREADY_RESOLVED` or
`WAIT_UNKNOWN_OR_STALE`; they are not a saved successful CLI response. Require
unchanged event, effect, signal, wait, delivery, and receiver files. Attempt
count stays two; resolution count stays one. An identical stored signal is
idempotent, but terminal/stale checks run before signal storage on this replay.

Check the retained causal chain with this read-only command:

```bash
node --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import fs from 'node:fs';
import path from 'node:path';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { parseHashJournal } from './skills/common/plugin-runtime/foundation/observability/hash-journal.ts';
const root = process.env.WAIT_REHEARSAL_ROOT;
const run = fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'run-root.txt'), 'utf8').trim();
const readJournal = name => {
  const file = path.join(run, name);
  return parseHashJournal(fs.readFileSync(file), file).map(record => record.entry);
};
const events = readJournal('events.jsonl');
const signal = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'valid.signal.json'), 'utf8'));
const completed = events.filter(e => e.type === 'attempt.completed');
const resolved = events.filter(e => e.type === 'wait.resolved');
assert.deepEqual(completed.map(e => e.payload.result.outcome), ['wait', 'passed']);
assert.equal(resolved.length, 1);
assert.equal(resolved[0].identity.waitId, signal.waitId);
assert.equal(resolved[0].causationId, signal.signalId);
assert.deepEqual(resolved[0].payload.signal, signal);
assert.notEqual(completed[0].identity.attemptId, completed[1].identity.attemptId);
assert(completed[0].sequence < resolved[0].sequence && resolved[0].sequence < completed[1].sequence);
assert.equal(events.filter(e => e.type === 'run.succeeded').length, 1);

const publish = effects.filter(e => e.type === 'requested' && e.request.capability === 'operator.request');
assert.equal(publish.length, 1);
const receipt = effects.find(e => e.type === 'completed' && e.receipt.idempotencyKey === publish[0].request.idempotencyKey);
assert.equal(receipt.receipt.result.accepted, true);
assert.equal(receipt.receipt.result.status, 202);
assert.equal(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'receiver.jsonl'), 'utf8').trim().split('\n').length, 1);

Available evidence does not establish successful execution of these lifecycle assertions. This test does not prove deployment behavior.

## Operator Delivery and Receipt Recovery

This section describes the installed `kubeclaw.operator-messaging:operator`
adapter beyond the disposable JSON receiver above. That receiver has no receipt
lookup endpoint; these contracts do not upgrade it or prove a deployed receiver.
For State/Wait API selection and responses, use
[State and Wait adapter operations](../../understand/data-and-state.md#state-and-wait-adapter-operations).

### Choose the transport before sending

`operator.request` supports `publish` to an allowed `operator.target` whose
canonical ID exactly names a configured target. It does not accept a caller's
arbitrary URL, method or headers. The target selects `format: json` (default) or
`discord_webhook`, one endpoint mode, and a payload byte limit (64 KiB default,
1 MiB maximum). The input is a closed, recursively bounded JSON envelope with
required `type`; only the admitted message/identity/presentation fields belong
in it. A schema field is not permission to send arbitrary JSON.

| Transport | Actual request body and success receipt | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `json` | The validated envelope, serialized with `JSON.stringify`. A successful 2xx response yields `{ accepted: true, target, status }` with optional `messageId` from response body `messageId` or `id`. | A 2xx is transport acceptance, not human approval, remote business success, or proof of durable receiver deduplication. |
| `discord_webhook` | A projected embed with `allowed_mentions.parse: []`; title/description/footer and field count have fixed display bounds. The endpoint gets exactly one `wait=true` parameter. | Success also requires the response body's actual `id` to be a positive decimal-string uint64, without leading zero. A generic `messageId` or empty 204 does not substitute. The returned `discord-delivery-receipt.v1` binds target, status, message ID, delivery ID and SHA-256 of the exact serialized projected body. |

Literal `endpoint` mode requires `tokenSecret`. The adapter resolves that secret
through `secrets.read` and signs the exact POST body with
`HMAC-SHA256(secret, deliveryId + "." + body)`. The fixed headers are
`content-type: application/json`, `idempotency-key: deliveryId`, and
`x-kubeclaw-signature: v1=<hex>`; it does not add Bearer authorization.

Alternatively, `endpointOrigin` plus `endpointSecret` selects a secret-held full
URL. Both fields must be present, without literal `endpoint`; the resolved URL
must match that configured origin and contain no URL userinfo or fragment.
The adapter sends this URL through confidential `network.http`, so a secret
webhook path **does cross the network boundary**. Do not apply a blanket
"no resolved secret ever enters a network request" rule to this mode. The
resolved secret also supplies the HMAC key; the ordinary effect journal is not
an approved place for it. Neither mode admits an arbitrary origin. Grant the
adapter's `secrets.read` names and `network.http` origin, methods, headers,
request/response bounds and timeout separately. JSON receiver recovery also
needs GET and `x-kubeclaw-signature`; configuring a receipt URL alone is not a
network grant.

> **Source evidence — operator transport and confidentiality**
>
> **Claim:** The adapter selects a bounded JSON or Discord body and keeps literal-token and confidential endpoint-URL modes distinct.
>
> **Implementation:** [POST construction and secret-endpoint branch](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/src/adapter.ts#L15-L70) [Discord presentation](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/src/discord-payload.ts#L1-L22) [Discord endpoint and receipt validation](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/src/discord-receipt.ts#L16-L47)
>
> **Contract or setting:** [Endpoint modes/origin/format](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/src/config.ts#L48-L80) [Target payload/URL bounds](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/src/config.ts#L30-L47) [Payload runtime checks](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/src/payload.ts#L98-L119)
>
> **Test evidence:** [Wire/HMAC/presentation and confidential endpoint assertions](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/tests/live-function.test.ts#L212-L270) [Journal exclusion assertions](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/tests/live-function.test.ts#L276-L297) Assertions cover exact HMAC/wire body. They cover Discord presentation, confidential endpoints and journal exclusion. They were inspected, not newly executed receiver or Discord service tests.
>
> **Revision:** `38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb`; the linked whole Source objects match this checkout.
>

### Preserve request, reservation and uncertainty

The stable external identity is `request.deliveryId`, falling back to the
idempotency key for legacy callers. The adapter first appends the request under
`notifications/<target>`, checks for an existing terminal receipt, and reserves
an attempt-specific terminal slot before resolving the secret or invoking the
receiver. New explicit delivery IDs produce owner-bound
`notification-delivery-request.v2` records with run, original stage and exact
transport-body string; legacy keys use v1 records. Do not rewrite one format
into the other to manufacture ownership.

The adapter transitions the reservation by expected payload digest into a
receipt or failure. It marks `sent=true` immediately **before** invoking the
POST, so a failure marked `possible` is conservative: it does not prove a
remote effect happened, and a local error/HTTP 5xx does not prove one did not.
An existing completed receipt can reconcile a concurrent failure. A local
reservation alone is not external exactly-once delivery; the compatible receiver
must deduplicate concurrent POSTs as well as retries.

For JSON only, optional `receiptEndpoint` must share the delivery endpoint's
origin. Before POST, the adapter makes a **fresh confidential GET**, not a cached
effect replay. Its query fields are `deliveryId` and `payloadDigest`, where the
digest is lowercase SHA-256 hex of the exact POST JSON bytes, without a
`sha256:` prefix. Its signature is
`HMAC-SHA256(secret, deliveryId + "." + payloadDigest)` in the same `v1=` header.
The receiver must respond HTTP 200 with a decoded JSON object:

```json
{
  "protocol": "kubeclaw.operator-delivery.v1",
  "deliveryId": "<exact requested deliveryId>",
  "payloadDigest": "<exact requested lowercase SHA-256 hex>",
  "status": "accepted",
  "messageId": "<nonempty receiver ID, at most 512 characters>"
}
```

Matching `accepted` completes the local receipt without another POST (its
recovered transport status is 200). Matching `absent` omits the need for
`messageId` and permits POST **only under the real receiver contract**. The
receiver must verify the corresponding signature and atomically retain delivery
ID, exact payload digest and accepted
result before ACK; return the same result without repeating an equal delivery;
reject changed content; retain deduplication until coordinated delivery
retirement; and make concurrent GET/POST observe that atomic state. A configured
URL or an arbitrary HTTP 200 does not implement any of those guarantees.

Without a compatible JSON receipt protocol, a retained reservation or
possible-send failure rejects another attempt with
`OPERATOR_DELIVERY_UNRESOLVED:receiver_receipt_required`. A missing, invalid or
unavailable receipt response does not authorize another POST. The adapter can record a failure known
before the send call as `not_sent`; the existing attempt's
terminal failure still fails, rather than silently retrying itself. Preserve
Core effect state, request body, delivery identity, attempt and adapter store.
Do not create a new run/key, erase the reservation, enlarge store limits, or
retarget the endpoint to escape uncertainty. Use the owning receiver's actual
reconciliation and the canonical recovery procedure; this guide adds no generic
receipt-import or endpoint-migration command. Discord mode does not consume the
JSON `receiptEndpoint` protocol to resend a lost response.

> **Source evidence — receiver reconciliation and conservative failure**
>
> **Claim:** A JSON receiver must supply matching durable delivery authority before the adapter can reconcile an uncertain send safely.
>
> **Implementation:** [Request, reservation and terminal transitions](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/src/delivery-records.ts#L31-L88) [Fresh receiver GET and exact response fields](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/src/receiver.ts#L1-L20)
>
> **Contract or setting:** [Receiver atomicity and retention contract](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/README.md#L57-L88) [Same-origin receipt configuration](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/src/config.ts#L48-L54)
>
> **Test evidence:** [Receiver scenario/protocol](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/tests/verification/reliability/operator-delivery.test.mts#L15-L45) [Reconstruction/delivery assertions](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/tests/verification/reliability/operator-delivery.test.mts#L83-L121) The scenarios assert lost-ACK recovery and bounded permanent failure. They reject an absent/invalid protocol and retain stable delivery identity across reconstructed attempts. Read as Source, not executed for this addition.
>

>
> **Limit:** The repository's test receiver is not evidence that an external endpoint implements atomic durable deduplication or that an uncertain delivery may be replayed.

### Look up a bound Discord receipt without publishing

`operator.receipt` / `lookup` is a separate, allowed-target capability on
`operator.target`. It reads the local delivery store; it does **not** query
Discord, resolve secrets, reserve a delivery, or send POST. Its payload has only
`deliveryId`, `stageId` (the original publishing stage), and `payload` (the
original message envelope). The adapter validates/projects that envelope again.
The caller's run must match the v2 request owner; the supplied original stage,
target, delivery ID and exact projected body must match too. Exactly one terminal
receipt must have that run/original stage, and the bound Discord receipt must
still match its delivery identity/body digest and valid message ID. A later
stage in the same run may request the lookup under its grant; the supplied
publishing stage is not replaced by the later stage's own identity.

Wrong operation/query/target, missing or multiple terminals, changed transport
body, foreign run/stage, legacy v1 requests without explicit owner, or an
unbound Discord acknowledgement fail. A generic JSON receipt does not become a
Discord handoff receipt. Preserve the original store and inspect the matching
request/terminal proof; lookup failure is not permission to send again. The
existing guarded JSON projection path is not an arbitrary ownership upgrade or
a replacement for this Discord lookup. Use the existing retention procedure
rather than editing/compacting raw records by hand.

> **Source evidence — lookup-only Discord receipt ownership**
>
> **Claim:** Local receipt lookup proves the stored delivery's exact run/stage/body binding without producing another delivery.
>
> **Implementation:** [Lookup dispatch and query validation](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/src/adapter.ts#L105-L117) [Owner-bound request and exact terminal selection](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/src/delivery-records.ts#L90-L113)
>
> **Contract or setting:** [Declared request and receipt capabilities](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/plugin.json#L1-L23) [Bound Discord receipt fields](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/skills/common/plugins/operator-messaging/src/discord-receipt.ts#L31-L47)
>
> **Test evidence:** [Reconstructed receipt assertions](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/tests/verification/reliability/discord-delivery-receipt.test.mts#L65-L112) [Explicit invalid receipt vectors](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb/tests/verification/reliability/discord-delivery-receipt.test.mts#L120-L132) The assertions check reconstructed lookup success. They reject foreign run/stage or changed-body bindings. They also reject invalid or legacy acknowledgements. No test or live handoff ran for this addition.
>
> **Revision:** `38d5c8f22d9cc3a923a7fdd421a1c02e4d176fdb`; the linked whole Source objects match this checkout.
>
> **Limit:** A lookup cannot recover a missing remote response by inference, approve a wait, or grant a new sender identity.

## Failure and Interruption

| Observation | Cause to distinguish | Safe next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FILE_MUTEX_ACQUIRE_FAILED` | Required fixed host lock interface unavailable | Stop before state claims. Use a supported host; preserve the failed attempt. |
| Registry, provider, grant, or config validation error | Wrong package/configuration selection | Correct before a new run. Do not change a running graph or package snapshot. |
| Receiver 403 or delivery error | Missing/wrong secret, HMAC, origin/header permission, or receiver response | Preserve request and receipt evidence. If delivery outcome is uncertain, stop and reconcile through the owning receiver. Do not replay publication by starting another run. |
| `WAIT_UNKNOWN_OR_STALE` | Wrong identity or resolved wait | Preserve raw state before reading the same run's durable audit. Do not guess a replacement wait. |
| `WAIT_ISSUER_DENIED` or `WAIT_SIGNAL_TYPE_MISMATCH` | Envelope differs from the active wait | Stop this submission; compare the reviewed signal with the durable request. |
| `WAIT_SIGNAL_STALE` or `WAIT_EXPIRED` | Issue time predates creation or current clock reached expiry | Preserve the rejection. Do not change the clock or journal; expired approval needs a new governed run. |
| Valid command response lost | Acceptance may already be durable | Stop writers and preserve raw run and adapter state before audit. Inspect complete hash-verified journals, then audit under the canonical procedure. Keep the original signal bytes, ID, time, and key. Do not invent a successor signal or repeat an uncertain effect. |
| `RECOVERY_SIGNAL_REQUIRED` | Recovery found an active wait | Follow the canonical signal procedure. Recovery cannot create approval. |
| Terminal run error | Run already succeeded, failed, blocked, or cancelled | Preserve the terminal audit. Use a new governed run for new work. |

For process interruption, use [Recover After Interruption](../operate.md#recover-after-interruption)
with the original graph, platform, package identities, run ID, and storage.
Preserve raw partial bytes and checksums before the first audit or recovery.
Stop on incomplete or corrupt journal records; do not trim them for inspection.
Reconcile unresolved external effects before any permitted canonical repair or
recovery. Audit can create lock files and truncate an unterminated journal tail;
its success alone does not prove that an external operation completed. For this
local input set, use `preserve_rehearsal_state` after writers stop; it binds the
known Core and adapter paths. A missing file is a stop, not permission to create
replacement authority. This guide supplies no
generic receipt import or cancellation command. Stopping the local receiver
does not cancel a durable Nova run. A signal payload with `decision: rejected`
is a separate decision that yields `blocked` with reason `approval.rejected`;
do not mutate the approved signal or replay it as a rejection.

## Deployment Registration

**Status: mandatory, open, and unexecuted.** The input set gives exact
pipeline, platform-template, signal-template, and wait-stage package paths. The
platform template is a loopback fixture; it is not a registered deployment
platform. The local receiver and `operator:local` label are not a deployment
authority or credential. This guide supplies no deployment registration.

Before a measured deployment run, platform operations and product integration
maintainers must jointly record:

- The immutable checkout and runtime/image identity, supported execution host,
  protected operator principal, CLI route, and signal-file ownership/access.
- The exact installed human-approval package content identity, adapter package
  identities, pipeline file and digest, materialized platform file and digest,
  signal-template path and digest, and new run ID with clean journal.
- Approved durable Core, wait, and notification store paths, permissions,
  capacity, retention owner, and backup/evidence location.
- Registered notification target, endpoint/origin, receiver authority, permitted
  network route, named secret binding and environment selector, rotation owner,
  receipt query/reconciliation procedure, and cleanup authority. Record secret
  names and owners; never their values.
- The deployment operator issuer ID in stage config and the matching wait grant,
  target grant, provider selections, adapter origin/method/header permissions,
  byte/time limits, and active-adapter list. Review the effective configuration
  before the run; do not edit it after wait creation.

Stop before deployment execution while any registration is missing. This is
the current blocked step, owned by platform operations for host/access/storage
and product integration maintainers for the registered workflow and packages.
Do not replace the missing registration with a localhost result.

Closure requires a fresh protected deployment run at the recorded immutable
revision, persisted wait and journal head, wrong wait and wrong issuer rejection
before valid submission, exactly one causal resolution, two completed attempts,
the unchanged original delivery receipt, exact replay returning terminal/stale
rejection with no second transition or budget, and cleanup that preserves all
required evidence. Keep actual deployment outputs, exit codes, identities,
checksums, and observations. An unexecuted or blocked run stays open even when
all templates and local tests validate.

## Bind the attempt before interruption

The native supervisor owns process termination and the final Worker result. The
specialist's output alone cannot establish safe cleanup, final resource usage
or a sealed result. Select the exact [Worker contract/version](../../understand/worker-core.md#contract-and-version-model)
and [native launch boundary](../../understand/worker-core.md#native-launch-and-trust-boundary)
before using this procedure. A portable executor result or Buster v1 attempt is
not interchangeable with Prism's native v3 path.

For an actual controlled native-host exercise, first register one disposable
non-production attempt and its original worker ID, attempt ID, claim ID,
generation, profile digest, attempt-spec digest and complete input envelope.
The owning service must submit through its supported authenticated dispatch
path. There is no generic `worker recover` or arbitrary raw-result import CLI
in this procedure. Do not handcraft an HTTP request or copy a fixture envelope
to bypass that service's source, claim or authorization checks.

Require the host operator to identify the real cgroup-v2 root, private ownership
root, attempt-journal root, trusted node-identity file, pool policy, launcher
and UID/GID, engine content identity, storage quotas and exclusive supervisor.
Use the current [native configuration and version contracts](../../understand/worker-core.md#host-and-runtime-identity)
and the owning deployment configuration reference; retain paths and logical
secret references, not credential values. An ordinary writable directory is
not a cgroup. A persistent volume mounted on another node does not prove that
processes on the old node stopped.

Stop if any authority or required host resource is unavailable. This is a
specific safe stop: host/node owner must establish delegated kernel scope and
stable identity; worker/storage owner must establish exclusive original stores;
calling-service owner must bind the submitted envelope and its accepted state.
Do not call a storage-only test native workload execution.

## Follow the durable boundaries

1. **Accepted input:** the journal persists canonical input and immutable
   accepted identity before launch. Record the exact acceptance, not merely an
   HTTP response or a queued task. Admission failure before acceptance is not
   the accepted-attempt interruption scenario.
2. **Ownership:** the supervisor reserves capacity and binds the exact attempt
   to a kernel scope. Preserve ownership phase, scope name, node/boot identity,
   device and inode. Do not infer ownership from a PID or matching directory
   name. Unknown or conflicting ownership stops admission.
3. **In-flight output:** the supervisor spools original binary stdout/stderr
   under the journal output root. Output can contain confidential original
   diagnostics; preserve its permissions and full byte identity. Rendered logs
   are not a replacement. A provisional specialist result is not sealed.
4. **Controlled interruption:** only the registered host owner may stop the
   selected supervisor/workload in its approved window. Use that deployment's
   actual process control and confirm observed exit. This procedure supplies
   no universal kill command because a host PID alone does not bind a kernel
   scope or external cleanup. Keep the caller's original claim/input and any
   connection loss, without creating a new generation to evade contention.
5. **Preserve:** stop new admission and preserve complete original ownership,
   journal, input, spool and any result/process blobs with the owning stores
   fenced. Keep startup/error output and actual exit observations. Do not edit
   phase, counters, input identity, output bytes or result digest to force
   recovery. An integrity failure retains the original bytes and stops.
6. **Owned restart:** the owning service starts one supervisor with the same
   host identity, scope root and stores. Prism's actual worker startup enters
   `NativeWorkerOwnership.supervise`, then runs journal reconciliation before
   it exposes HTTP admission. Do not start a second supervisor or move the
   stores to make readiness green.
7. **Evaluate recovery:** compare the exact cases below. A service that remains
   fenced has not recovered admission merely because its process is running.
   Observe its retained diagnosis and original-attempt result through the
   owning caller; do not synthesize or submit a replacement result.

## Interpret the original-attempt result

Ownership recovery first kills and drains a current matching scope and retains
final counters. After validating the root-managed host identity, recovery moves
an `empty` record with no scope to `disposed`. A missing scope with no binding
or a prior-boot binding becomes `abandoned`, with its retained diagnosis. An
unexplained missing scope for a same-boot bound nonempty record stops recovery.
An unrecorded scope, reappearing retired scope or changed binding also stops it. The full state map remains in
[Restart and Reconciliation](../../understand/worker-core.md#restart-and-reconciliation).
After that ownership boundary:

- **A sealed result already exists:** exact replay returns that result without
  new admission or re-execution. Verify full envelope/result binding and digest
  through the owning caller. Same attempt identity with changed content is a
  conflict, not a new job.
- **A durable process result exists:** reconstruction requires ownership phase
  `disposed` and exact equality between stored final ownership observation and
  process resource counters. The journal also verifies original spool bytes.
  Only then may the supervisor finalize and seal the original attempt result.
- **Accepted input exists but no process result:** quiescent or never-launched
  ownership must be established. Recovery seals `state: errored` with
  `WORKER_NATIVE_INTERRUPTED_RESULT_UNAVAILABLE`, not a fictional successful
  specialist result and not the portable executor's `interrupted` state.
  Proven never-launched work has `cleanup.state: not_required`. Otherwise
  cleanup is `failed`: killing the process tree cannot prove cleanup of
  specialist external effects. Failed cleanup fences new admission.
- **Ownership/output cannot be proved:** errors such as
  `WORKER_NATIVE_JOURNAL_OWNERSHIP_UNPROVEN`,
  `WORKER_NATIVE_RECOVERY_NOT_QUIESCENT`, output corruption or a journal conflict
  retain the stop. Preserve both stores and obtain the host/storage/specialist
  owners' reconciliation. Do not delete the journal, clear its lock or relabel
  it as a new generation.

A seal proves a bound terminal Worker receipt, not application success. An
`errored` sealed result and an explicit fenced stop are legitimate recovery
outcomes. Before new work, reconcile specialist side effects under their owning
contract and retain the prior receipt and cleanup decision. No generic command
here clears an unresolved admission fence.

## Reproduce the local storage/crash controls

From a selected checkout with Node.js 24, GNU `flock` and locked development
dependencies, run the actual local journal/ownership suites:

```bash
env -u NODE_ENV node --test \
  tests/verification/reliability/worker-native-journal.test.mts \
  tests/verification/reliability/worker-ownership-store.test.mts
```

This command explicitly selects the development fixture environment. It is not
a way to weaken a running production worker's identity checks. In production,
missing `PRISM_ENGINE_CONTENT_DIGEST` correctly rejects before Prism profile
imports; use the real installed engine image identity, not an invented digest.

The local journal tests start real writer children, wait for durable accepted
or sealed state, contend on the production `flock`, then send `SIGKILL` to those
owned writers. Original identity and binary diagnostic output survive. Exact
sealed replay returns the original result; changing an already sealed receipt
rejects. A separate accepted-without-result case remains accepted with no
invented result. The tests also reject changed envelope identity, retained disk
overflow, changed spool bytes and live contention. Ownership tests verify
convergence, durable phases, conflicts, unresolved stops and a real supervisor
lock; their ordinary-directory bindings test storage only, not kernel scope.

Expected actual local result is 15 passing tests, zero failed or skipped cases
for this source revision. The fixtures own and remove their temporary trees.
Keep terminal logs/revision separately. These tests do not execute a real
native cgroup workload or demonstrate supervisor recovery of such a workload.

For actual kernel scope/launcher checks, the registered host owner supplies the
real `KUBECLAW_WORKER_TEST_CGROUP_ROOT`, absolute production
`KUBECLAW_WORKER_TEST_LAUNCHER`, trusted
`KUBECLAW_WORKER_TEST_NODE_IDENTITY_FILE` and
`KUBECLAW_WORKER_TEST_POOL_LIMITS_FILE`, then runs:

```bash
npm run verify:worker-core:native-scope
```

That suite requires its real delegated host resources and does not skip missing
prerequisites. The npm command first requires the native-scope TypeScript check
to exit zero, then runs **two** native tests. Require command exit zero, both
tests passing, and zero failed, cancelled or skipped tests. They check actual
scope accounting and final counters after drain, production-launcher UID/GID
and group restrictions, durable ownership, pool admission and exact replay
fencing. Retain the selected revision, actual host-resource identities, complete
terminal output and exit status outside the suite's disposable directories.
This is the expected result, not a report that this guide's author ran it.

A compiler error, missing host input, unexpected child exit, assertion failure,
drain timeout or `Native scope test cleanup failed` is a failed check. Preserve
the first error and the original host/ownership evidence; have the registered
host owner inspect the exact test scopes and remaining children before retrying.
Do not replace a delegated cgroup with an ordinary directory, relax launcher or
pool restrictions, or count only the tests that reached their assertions.

The scope test's finalizer attempts to kill its own remaining children, drain
its created scopes with a five-second bound, and dispose them; cleanup failure
is reported, not a successful result. The launcher/ownership test removes its
private `worker-native-live-*` state tree in its finalizer, but an early host-input
error can occur before that finalizer is installed. On failure, confirm actual
quiescence and identify any retained owned scope or temporary tree with the host
owner; do not assume that a process exit proves cleanup. Retain necessary failure
evidence before retiring only those confirmed private leftovers. Never remove
the delegated cgroup root, trusted node identity, pool policy, production launcher
or unrelated supervisor stores. The suite does not retire a real service's
specialist effects or incident evidence.

Do not treat even a successful suite as a complete live
supervisor-abort→specialist-result recovery exercise; record the original-attempt
chronology above for the actual service.

## Cleanup and change

Only retire owned journal/spool records through the supported retention contract
after original caller reconciliation, retention obligations and external-effect
cleanup pass. Do not remove evidence to relieve quota pressure automatically.
The supervisor owns scope disposal only after quiescence. A disposed scope does
not authorize deleting original specialist evidence or external resources.

For a change, update producer envelope/profile/resource policy and consumer
result binding together, keep old pinned accepted work readable and run the
storage/crash and actual delegated-host checks matched to the changed boundary.
Never reuse a changed generation or edited store to make an old interrupted
attempt appear successful. Where the owning deployment offers no supported
control or reconciliation path, retain that explicit stop and its named owner.
